evidence:
Central claim confirmed. Every table stops at C# 14: `SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:31-32` (`Latest => LanguageVersion.CSharp14`), `:38-43` (`All` = {14,13,12,11,10}), `:52-62` (`ToLanguageVersion`, `V5_0_0 => CSharp14` at :59 and `V5_10_0 => CSharp14` at :60), `:149-159` (`GetMaxLanguageVersion`, `(>= 5, _) => AllLanguageVersions.CSharp14` at :152), `AllLanguageVersions.cs:14-18` (constants stop at `CSharp14 = (LanguageVersion) 1400`), `LanguageVersionProvider.cs:54-60` (`>= 10 => LanguageVersion.CSharp14` at :56). The "shared by the Roslyn 5.0 variant" claim is confirmed by `Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine.5.0.0/Metalama.Framework.Engine.5.0.0.csproj:6`, which compiles `../Metalama.Framework.Engine/**/*.cs` into the 5.0.0 variant, so `SupportedCSharpVersions.cs` is one source file compiled into both variants. `RoslynApiVersion.Current` exists per variant (`eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Generator.cs:93`, `writer.WriteLine( $"\tCurrent = {this._syntax.Version.EnumValue}," )`), so the proposed `Latest => RoslynApiVersion.Current.ToLanguageVersion()` is expressible. The aspect suite runs in both variants (`Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Metalama.Framework.Tests.AspectTests.5.0.0` beside `Metalama.Framework.Tests.AspectTests`), so the argument for keeping `All` shared is sound. Consumer sites verified: `SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:50`, `Options/DefaultProjectOptions.cs:127`, `Options/MSBuildProjectOptions.cs:167-183` (the `Latest` fallback is at :178, not :173-177), `Services/CompilationContext.cs:181`, `CompileTime/CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:1355`, `CompileTime/CompileTimeProjectRepository.Builder.cs:596`, `Metalama.Testing.UnitTesting/TestLanguageVersionProvider.cs:12`, `Pipeline/CompileTime/CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:68`. Diagnostic identifiers verified: `GeneralDiagnosticDescriptors.cs:237` is LAMA0051 `PreviewCSharpVersionNotSupported` and `:246` is LAMA0052 `CSharpVersionNotSupported`; both format their version list with `SupportedCSharpVersions.FormatSupportedVersions()` (`CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:77` and `:87`, `TemplateCompiler.cs:73`). Both baselines pin the ascending list: `Tests/Aspects/Misc/LanguageVersion.t.cs:2` and `Tests/Aspects/LanguageVersion/LanguageVersionPreview.t.cs:2` both read `'10.0', '11.0', '12.0', '13.0', '14.0'`.

Three defects found. First, `CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:349-353` calls `CSharpSyntaxTree.Create`, not `CSharpSyntaxTree.ParseText`, so the compile-time trees are not re-parsed at the compile-time language version; only the predefined polyfill trees are parsed, at `CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:430-440`. Second, `Utilities/Roslyn/LanguageVersionExtensions.cs:33-39` maps `(LanguageVersion) 1300` and `(LanguageVersion) 1400` and throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for anything else, so adding `CSharp15` to `All` without adding a `1500` case makes `FormatSupportedVersions()` (`SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:45`) throw on the LAMA0051 and LAMA0052 paths that the two cited baselines exercise; the proposed change does not mention this file. Third, per the addendum of FACTS.md, `LanguageVersion.CSharp15` does not exist in the consumed Roslyn 5.10 preview, so mapping `V5_10_0` to `CSharp15` before the renumbering to 5.12 would emit an invalid language version into every compile-time compilation.

corrections.what_happens_today: Case (b) reaches LV-2. Case (d): `GetLanguageVersionFromDotNetSdk` returns C# 14 for the .NET 11 SDK, because `LanguageVersionProvider.cs:54-60` maps an SDK major version of 10 or more to `LanguageVersion.CSharp14`. That value becomes the language version of the compile-time compilation (`CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:279`, passed to `CreateEmptyCompileTimeCompilation` at `:285` and used at `:425` to define `EMBED_SYSTEM_TYPES` and at `:432` for the parse options of the predefined polyfill trees), and it becomes `TemplateCompiler.TemplateLanguageVersion` (`TemplateCompiler.cs:51`). The user compile-time trees are not re-parsed at that version: `CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:349-353` calls `CSharpSyntaxTree.Create` on the already-parsed run-time syntax root and only attaches `new CSharpParseOptions( languageVersion, ... )` to it, so a feature that the Roslyn parser rejects at parse time carries whatever diagnostic the run-time parse produced, and only the feature checks that Roslyn performs during binding are re-evaluated against the compile-time language version. The mechanism that actually rejects a template written in a language version above the compile-time one is `RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier` (constructed at `TemplateCompiler.cs:106` with `TemplateLanguageVersion`, comparing `version.ToLanguageVersion()` against it at `RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier.cs:43`, `:65` and `:80`) and reporting `TemplatingDiagnosticDescriptors.TemplateUsesUnsupportedLanguageVersion`. The run-time compilation is unaffected. Under `msbuild.exe` the cap comes from `GetMaxLanguageVersion` (`LanguageVersionProvider.cs:111`), which returns C# 14 for the Roslyn of any Visual Studio 2026 or 2027 MSBuild (`SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:152`, `(>= 5, _)`). Sites: `SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:31-32` (`Latest`), `:38-43` (`All`), `:52-62` (`ToLanguageVersion`, both `V5_0_0` and `V5_10_0` map to C# 14), `:149-159` (`GetMaxLanguageVersion`, every Roslyn 5.x maps to C# 14); `AllLanguageVersions.cs:14-18` (no `CSharp15`); `LanguageVersionExtensions.cs:33-39` (`ToDisplayStringSafe` maps 1300 and 1400 and throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for any other unmapped value); `LanguageVersionProvider.cs:54-60` (SDK major 10 or more maps to C# 14). Direct consumers of `Latest`: `SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:50` (`DefaultParseOptions`), `CodeModel/LanguageOptions.cs:30`, `Options/DefaultProjectOptions.cs:127`, `Options/MSBuildProjectOptions.cs:178` (the fallback taken when `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse` fails at `:173`), `Services/CompilationContext.cs:181`, `CompileTime/CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:1355`, `CompileTime/CompileTimeProjectRepository.Builder.cs:596`, `Metalama.Testing.UnitTesting/TestLanguageVersionProvider.cs:12`, `Pipeline/CompileTime/CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:68`. Indirect consumers, through `DefaultParseOptions`: `RunTimeAssemblyRewriter.cs:88`, `UserCodeInvoker.cs:422`, `Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/BaseTestRunner.cs:218`, `Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/SyntaxTreeStructureVerifier.cs:35`, `Metalama.Testing.UnitTesting/TestContext.CreateRoslynCompilation.cs:156`. (Behaviour matrix: `MSBuildProjectOptions.LanguageVersion` (`:167-183`) would parse `15.0` only in a variant whose Roslyn defines `LanguageVersion.CSharp15`, which no consumed Roslyn does today; in both the 5.0 and the 5.10 variant `TryParse` fails and the value silently falls back to `Latest`, that is C# 14. `GetLanguageVersionFromDotNetSdk` (`:45-72`) yields `min(C# 14, C# 15)` = C# 14 for an explicit 15.0 and `min(C# 14, Preview)` = C# 14 for preview. `TemplateCompiler.TryReadProjectOptions` (`:56-79`) rejects `MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion` of `15.0` with LAMA0052 in both variants today, because `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse` fails at `:62` before the `All` membership test at `:63`; `14.0` passes. `EMBED_SYSTEM_TYPES` is defined (C# 14) in scenarios (b), (c), (d); the manifest language version is serialized as 1400 in scenarios (b), (c), (d), and `CompileTimeProjectManifest.ResolvedLanguageVersion` (`:101`) still defaults to C# 13 for a manifest written by an earlier Metalama.)
corrections.consequence_class: Diagnostic reported, and no wrong output. There is no reachable path today on which C# 15 code is silently accepted: a project that asks for language version 15.0 is rejected by the compiler itself, since no Roslyn that Metalama consumes defines `LanguageVersion.CSharp15`; a project that asks for `preview` is rejected by `CompileTimeAspectPipeline.VerifyLanguageVersion` with LAMA0051 (`CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:70-80`) unless `MetalamaAllowPreviewLanguageFeatures` is set; a `MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion` of 15.0 is rejected with LAMA0052 (`TemplateCompiler.cs:62-75`); and an unparsable `LangVersion` falls back silently to `Latest`, that is C# 14 (`MSBuildProjectOptions.cs:173-178`). The gap is therefore a missing capability rather than a defect that produces incorrect output.
corrections.proposed_change: Add `CSharp15 = (LanguageVersion) 1500` to `AllLanguageVersions`; add `CSharp15` to `All`; and, in the same change, add the case `(LanguageVersion) 1500 => "15.0"` to `LanguageVersionExtensions.ToDisplayStringSafe` (`Utilities/Roslyn/LanguageVersionExtensions.cs:33-39`). The last item is not optional: `FormatSupportedVersions` (`SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:45`) projects every member of `All` through `ToDisplayStringSafe`, whose default arm throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` (`LanguageVersionExtensions.cs:39`), so adding `CSharp15` to `All` alone turns both the LAMA0051 path (`CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:77`) and the LAMA0052 paths (`CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:87`, `TemplateCompiler.cs:73`) into unhandled exceptions, in both Roslyn variants. Map the version of the latest variant to `CSharp15` in `ToLanguageVersion`, and keep `V5_0_0` at `CSharp14`. That mapping must wait for the renumbering of the latest variant to `V5_12_0` (LV-13): the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 preview does not define `LanguageVersion.CSharp15`, so mapping `V5_10_0` to 1500 before that renumbering would place a language version that Roslyn considers invalid into `DefaultParseOptions` and into every compile-time compilation. For the same reason `GetMaxLanguageVersion` should return `CSharp15` for `(5, >= 12)`, not for `(5, >= 10)`, and `CSharp14` for the other 5.x versions; map SDK major 11 or more to `CSharp15` in `LanguageVersionProvider` (`:54-60`). Define `Latest` as `RoslynApiVersion.Current.ToLanguageVersion()` instead of the constant at `SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:31-32`, because the same source file is compiled into both variants (`Metalama.Framework.Engine.5.0.0.csproj:6`) and `RoslynApiVersion.Current` is generated per variant (`eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Generator.cs:93`): the 5.0.0 variant is built against Roslyn 5.0, whose option validation reports a language-version error rather than throwing, so a `Latest` of 1500 would surface there as a compiler diagnostic on every compile-time compilation created from `DefaultParseOptions` (`:50`), from the unit-test provider (`TestLanguageVersionProvider.cs:12`), from `LanguageOptions.Default` (`CodeModel/LanguageOptions.cs:30`) and from every fallback listed above. `All` can stay a shared constant, because it is used only for membership and for the LAMA0051 and LAMA0052 text, which keeps the aspect-test baselines identical in both variants; the price is that the 5.0.0 variant advertises '15.0' in those messages although its own Roslyn cannot parse it, which is acceptable only because `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse` fails first there. Sort `FormatSupportedVersions` (`:45`) explicitly, because `All` is an `ImmutableHashSet` whose enumeration order is not part of its contract and the baselines `Tests/Aspects/Misc/LanguageVersion.t.cs:2` and `Tests/Aspects/LanguageVersion/LanguageVersionPreview.t.cs:2` pin the printed order; both baselines change to include '15.0'.

notes:
The central claim holds and every cited site exists as described. Four corrections were needed.

1. `CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:349-353` calls `CSharpSyntaxTree.Create`, not `ParseText`, so the phrase "the compile-time syntax trees are parsed at C# 14" is inaccurate. The language version is attached as parse options to a tree that the compiler already parsed at the run-time language version. Only the predefined polyfill trees are actually parsed at the compile-time version (`:430-440`). Consequently the claim that "compile-time code that uses C# 15 syntax fails in the compile-time compilation with the compiler's own language-version errors" is true only for the feature checks that Roslyn performs during binding, not for those that its parser performs. The guard that does reject too-new template syntax is `RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier` (`TemplateCompiler.cs:106`), which is driven by `TemplateLanguageVersion` rather than by the parse options.

2. The proposed change omits `Utilities/Roslyn/LanguageVersionExtensions.cs`. Its `ToDisplayStringSafe` maps `(LanguageVersion) 1300` and `(LanguageVersion) 1400` by numeric cast and throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` on the default arm (`:39`). `FormatSupportedVersions` (`SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:45`) applies it to every member of `All`, so adding `CSharp15` to `All` without a `1500` case would throw on exactly the two diagnostic paths that the two cited baselines exercise. This makes the change larger than "S" by one file and turns the two baseline updates into a prerequisite rather than a side effect.

3. The proposed mapping of `V5_10_0` to `CSharp15` and of `(5, >= 10)` to `CSharp15` contradicts the addendum of FACTS.md, which records that `LanguageVersion.CSharp15` was added to Roslyn main on 2026-08-11 and is absent from both the stable 5.9.0 and the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3. The mapping must be tied to 5.12, that is, it must follow LV-13 rather than precede it.

4. The `where` list omitted two direct consumers of `Latest`, `CodeModel/LanguageOptions.cs:30` and `Options/MSBuildProjectOptions.cs:178` (the list cited `:173-177`, which is the failing `TryParse` and its comment, not the `return`), and it listed `Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/BaseTestRunner.cs:218` among the consumers of `Latest` when that site consumes `DefaultParseOptions`.

One further inaccuracy, in `open_questions` rather than in a correctable field: it states that "`TryReadProjectOptions` accepting `15.0` in both variants is correct only because the verifier rejects the syntax at compile time in the 5.0 variant". `TryReadProjectOptions` does not accept `15.0` in the 5.0.0 variant at all. `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse` runs first (`TemplateCompiler.cs:62`) and fails there, because Roslyn 5.0 has no `CSharp15` case in its parse table, so LAMA0052 is reported regardless of the content of `All`. The behaviour matrix of the same finding states this correctly, so the two statements contradict each other. The conclusion that `All` may stay shared is nevertheless right, for that reason rather than for the one given.

Two claims of the proposed change could not be verified from source, because no Roslyn assembly is present in this environment and `Metalama.Compiler` is not cloned: that Roslyn 5.0 reports rather than throws on a `CSharpParseOptions` carrying language version 1500, and that `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse` in Roslyn 5.0 rejects the string "15.0". Both rest on the Roslyn implementation and on FACTS.md line 54. They do not change the direction of the proposal, which is to make `Latest` variant-dependent.

The suggestion to sort `FormatSupportedVersions` is defensive rather than necessary. `All` is built at `SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:38-43` in descending order and the two baselines print ascending order, so the current enumeration of `ImmutableHashSet<LanguageVersion>` already orders by the underlying integer, and 1500 would land last. Sorting is still worth doing, because that order is not part of the contract of `ImmutableHashSet`.

notes:
Verdict: the proposed change is neither implemented, nor in progress, nor tracked by any issue. `already_in_progress` is empty.

Evidence that it is not implemented.
- No test anywhere in the repository exercises either construct. `grep -rn "ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER" --include=*.cs` over the working tree returns exactly two files, both in the framework aspect tests and both about an unrelated subject: Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Metalama.Framework.Tests.AspectTests/Tests/Aspects/DesignTimeInvalidCode/UnknownAccessorInTemplate.cs:7 (`// @RequiredConstant(ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER)`) and UnknownAccessorInTemplate_Roslyn5_0.cs:7 (`// @ForbiddenConstant(ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER)`). No aspect test and no unit test in Metalama.Extensions or Metalama.Patterns carries either directive.
- The Metrics unit test project holds four files only: Metalama.Extensions/src/tests/Metalama.Extensions.Metrics.UnitTests/{AddMetricsTests.cs, LinesOfCodeTests.cs, StatementNumberTests.cs, Metalama.Extensions.Metrics.UnitTests.csproj}. `git log --name-only` over that directory shows its last two touches were pull request #1876 (net8.0 to net10.0) and the 2026.1 commit 129f3040; nothing since.
- The two visitors named in the finding still have no case for either construct. Metalama.Extensions/src/Metalama.Extensions.Metrics/StatementsCountMetricProvider.Visitor.cs overrides DefaultVisit (line 19), VisitBlock (line 36), VisitForStatement (line 48), VisitLabeledStatement (line 59), VisitUnsafeStatement (line 61) and VisitTryStatement (line 63); its DefaultVisit counts any node that is a StatementSyntax (lines 23-26), so a labeled `break` is counted through the base case and a `with(...)` element is not a statement. SyntaxNodesCountMetricProvider.Visitor.cs overrides only DefaultVisit (line 18), which counts one per node and recurses over ChildNodes (lines 20-25), so a WithElementSyntax changes the node count without any code change. Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Sdk/Metrics/SyntaxMetricProvider.cs:78 declares `protected abstract class BaseVisitor : CSharpSyntaxVisitor<T>` and its DefaultVisit at lines 96-110 walks ChildNodesAndTokens. The finding's citations are accurate; what is missing is a test that pins the resulting numbers.
- The Observability walker is unchanged. Metalama.Patterns/src/Metalama.Patterns.Observability/Implementation/DependencyAnalysis/DependencyGraphBuilder.Visitor.cs:54 declares `private sealed partial class Visitor : CSharpSyntaxWalker`, its Visit override at lines 280-291 increments a depth counter and calls ProcessAndResetIfApplicable, VisitArgument at lines 305-311 opens a new root context, and ProcessAndResetIfApplicable at lines 215-278 processes the gathered identifier chains. There is no override for a break, a continue or a collection element, and no test source under Metalama.Patterns/src/tests/Metalama.Patterns.Observability.AspectTests contains a labeled loop.

Evidence that it is not in progress.
- Of the three open pull requests in the survey, none touches these files. metalama/Metalama#1879 adds 38 aspect test sources under Tests/Aspects/Records/ and the unit test CodeModel/CanBeDeclaredExplicitlyTests.cs, and touches nothing in Metalama.Extensions or Metalama.Patterns. metalama/Metalama.Premium#84 changes two build files. metalama/Metalama.Premium#85 changes 47 files, all build files except one expected-output snapshot, and adds no test content.

corrections.what_happens_today: FindCompileTimeCodeVisitor decides whether a syntax tree is fed to the compile-time rewriter. It inherits the default VisitUnionDeclaration, so it does descend into the union's members through DefaultVisit, but it never calls its private VisitTypeDeclaration for the union node itself, so a union alone does not mark the tree as containing compile-time code. When the same file also declares an aspect, the tree is rewritten by ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter, whose VisitClassDeclaration, VisitStructDeclaration, VisitInterfaceDeclaration and VisitRecordDeclaration overrides return null for run-time types. A top-level union is not intercepted, and SafeSyntaxRewriter has no throwing default, so the base rewriter copies the union into the compile-time compilation. CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:349-352 places the rewritten root in a new syntax tree with new CSharpParseOptions(languageVersion) and does not re-parse, so the tree contains a node that a parse at that language version could never produce. Roslyn's DeclarationTreeBuilder then reports a feature-availability diagnostic against the tree's own parse options, on the union keyword, in a file the user never wrote for compile-time. The exact diagnostic depends on the Roslyn build and on the compile-time language version. Against the Roslyn that the repository consumes today, IDS_FeatureUnions requires LanguageVersion.Preview, so the diagnostic is ERR_FeatureInPreview. Against Roslyn 5.12, which the FACTS addendum names as the 2027.0 target, IDS_FeatureUnions requires LanguageVersion.CSharp15, so with a compile-time compilation at C# 14 the diagnostic is CS9327, ERR_FeatureNotAvailableInVersion14. If the 2027.0 work raises the compile-time language version to C# 15, there is no language-version error at all, and the failure moves to the reference set instead: the compile-time compilation always targets netstandard2.0, which contains neither System.Runtime.CompilerServices.IUnion nor UnionAttribute, and Roslyn adds IUnion to the union's implicitly implemented interfaces, so a missing-type error is reported. A union nested in a run-time type reaches PopulateNestedCompileTimeTypes, whose default arm drops it, which is correct by accident.
corrections.consequence_class: Build error in the compile-time compilation, with a message that names a language version or a missing framework type rather than the real cause. The specific message depends on the Roslyn build and on the compile-time language version: ERR_FeatureInPreview on the consumed Roslyn build, CS9327 on Roslyn 5.12 while the compile-time compilation stays at C# 14, and a missing System.Runtime.CompilerServices.IUnion error once the compile-time compilation is raised to C# 15.
corrections.proposed_change: Override VisitUnionDeclaration in ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter and route it to the existing private VisitTypeDeclaration, which classifies by templating scope and therefore also handles a union that the user marks as compile-time. The override cannot be unconditional: Metalama.Framework.Engine.5.0.0 compiles the same source files, and neither UnionDeclarationSyntax nor CSharpSyntaxRewriter.VisitUnionDeclaration exists in Roslyn 5.0.0, so the override has to sit inside a variant guard, today ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER, which is the only such symbol and is defined solely by eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.5.10.0.props. While Metalama consumes a Roslyn 5.10 build the member also carries RSEXPERIMENTAL006 and the override needs an explicit suppression; the marker is removed from Roslyn 5.11 onwards, so on the Roslyn 5.12 target the suppression can be dropped. Alternatively the interception can avoid the new API entirely by testing the raw kind value of UnionDeclaration, which is 9082. Apply the same treatment to FindCompileTimeCodeVisitor, so that a compile-time union is classified rather than silently skipped. Add a compile-time test with a run-time union and an aspect in one file; the test can only run under the latest Roslyn variant, because under Roslyn 5.0.0 the source does not parse as a union at all, and it should be validated both while the compile-time compilation is at C# 14 and after it is raised to C# 15, because the failure it guards against changes form between the two.

notes:
Every external premise of the finding survives, and the mechanism is confirmed end to end against dotnet/roslyn main, the csharplang union proposal and the repository sources. Four corrections are needed, none of which removes the defect.

First, the diagnostic wording. "Feature not available in C# 14" is true only of a Roslyn in which IDS_FeatureUnions requires LanguageVersion.CSharp15. That is true of main, that is Roslyn 5.12 (MessageID.cs:502-507), and false of the build the repository consumes, 5.10.0-1.26365.3, whose public surface equals stable 5.9.0 and in which the same feature requires LanguageVersion.Preview (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:16 and FACTS.md:53-54). In the consumed build MessageID.cs:481-483 takes the preview branch and produces ERR_FeatureInPreview instead of CS9327. The FACTS addendum states that the 2027.0 baseline is expected to carry Roslyn 5.12 (FACTS.md:49), so the finding's wording is right for the target and wrong for today.

Second, the consequence depends on a regime the finding does not name. The finding assumes the compile-time compilation stays at C# 14, which is the current state (FACTS.md:16-17). Raising SupportedCSharpVersions and LanguageVersionProvider to C# 15 is the point of the 2027.0 release, and it removes the language-version error without fixing the defect. The compile-time compilation always targets netstandard2.0 (Metalama.Framework/docs/compile-time-target-frameworks.md:10, :28-31, :213), which has neither System.Runtime.CompilerServices.IUnion nor UnionAttribute, and dotnet/roslyn main src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/Source/SourceNamedTypeSymbol_Bases.cs:378-383 adds GetWellKnownType(System_Runtime_CompilerServices_IUnion) to the implicitly implemented interfaces of every union. The build therefore still fails, with a missing-type error rather than a language-version error. The fix and its test must be validated in both regimes.

Third, the proposed change is not portable across the Roslyn variants as written. Metalama.Framework.Engine.5.0.0 compiles the identical source files through a single Compile Include (Metalama.Framework.Engine.5.0.0.csproj:6), and UnionDeclarationSyntax and CSharpSyntaxRewriter.VisitUnionDeclaration first appear in Roslyn 5.10 (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:60, :62). Fourth, two statements in "what happens today" are imprecise rather than wrong. FindCompileTimeCodeVisitor does reach the union node through the inherited VisitUnionDeclaration and descends into its members by DefaultVisit; what it does not do is classify the union itself. And "a union is run-time code" is a design decision, not a semantic fact: the unions proposal describes an ordinary struct type, and nothing prevents a user from marking one as compile-time. The proposed routing to the private VisitTypeDeclaration is the correct shape precisely because that method classifies by templating scope instead of assuming run-time.

notes: The central claim holds: a with(...) element in a run-time collection expression makes the template compiler throw before regeneration, and regeneration alone removes the throw. Three details are corrected. (1) The crash does not rest on the assumed shape of the Roslyn base visitor: whichever value the base VisitWithElement returns, either its own cast to ArgumentListSyntax or the cast to ExpressionSyntax at MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:137 fails, because WithElementSyntax derives from CollectionElementSyntax (Syntax-5.10.0.xml:816). The confidence can therefore be raised to verified for the crash itself. (2) The exception does not terminate the compiler: SourceTransformer.cs:145-158 catches it and CompileTimeExceptionHandler reports LAMA0001 at the node location with a crash report file, so the user sees an error diagnostic. (3) The statement that the annotator needs no change is only true for the absence of a crash. AddScopeAnnotationToVisitedNode (TemplateAnnotator.cs:693) counts only ExpressionSyntax and InterpolationSyntax children, so the arguments of with(...) never influence the scope of the element or of the collection expression, whereas invocations (:1275-1296) and object creations (:3241) fold argument scopes explicitly. A compile-time argument in an otherwise neutral collection therefore leaves the collection run-time, and TransformArgument (TemplateCompilerRewriter.cs:590-596) converts the argument to a run-time expression. This is a difference in inference, not an error, and the proposed tests should pin it. The proposed test location Tests/Syntax/CollectionExpressions does not exist in the template test project; the existing collection expression tests are aspect tests under Tests/Aspects/CSharp12. @LanguageVersion(15.0) is parsed by LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse and skips the test on a Roslyn that does not know the version (TestOptions.cs:681-696), so the tests are safe for the 5.0.0 variant. Per FACTS.md:47-56, the stable Roslyn that removes the experimental markers is 5.12, not 5.10, and no consumed build exposes C# 15 as a non-preview version, so the tests cannot run before that move. The Roslyn base visitor cast was checked only by the presence of VisitWithElement and WithElementSyntax in the 5.9.0 binary; the exact statement was not decompiled.

Consequently no checked-in file has to be edited for the regeneration, and no generated file can be inspected here to show the missing overrides directly.

2. The grammar the generator sees has the C# 15 nodes removed. eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Model/TreeReader.cs:19 calls RemoveExperimentalDeclarations; line 37 removes every type whose IsExperimental is true, and line 57 removes every experimental field, recursively through Choice and Sequence (lines 63-71). Per FACTS.md, UnionDeclarationSyntax, UnsafeExpressionSyntax, WithElementSyntax and the Name fields of BreakStatementSyntax and ContinueStatementSyntax carry ExperimentalUrl in Syntax-5.10.0.xml, so the generated hashers contain no VisitUnionDeclaration, no VisitWithElement, no VisitUnsafeExpression, and their VisitBreakStatement and VisitContinueStatement do not read the Name field.

3. The consequence for the design-time diff is real. Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.DesignTime/Pipeline/Diff/BaseCodeHasher.cs:19 derives from SafeSyntaxWalker, and Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Sdk/Utilities/Roslyn/SafeSyntaxWalker.cs:35,39 derives from CSharpSyntaxWalker with the default SyntaxWalkerDepth.Node, so a node with no override falls back to DefaultVisit, which descends into child nodes but never visits tokens. The identifier token of a union declaration and the label identifier of a labeled break or continue are therefore not appended to the hash. Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.DesignTime/Pipeline/Diff/DiffStrategy.cs:74-78 selects CompileTimeCodeHasher or RunTimeCodeHasher and compares the resulting XxHash64 value against the stored DeclarationHash at line 80, returning false (no significant difference) when they are equal. A second call site with the same construction is at DiffStrategy.cs:157-159 in GetSyntaxTreeVersion, which the finding does not cite and which a story should also consider.

4. The test file has no such case. Pull request survey. metalama/Metalama#1879 changes the linker, the code model and aspect tests only; the survey records that it touches no eng/ file and no build file, and a grep of its production diff for LanguageVersion, ROSLYN_, net11 and CSharp14/CSharp15 returns nothing. metalama/Metalama.Premium#84 changes two build files, and metalama/Metalama.Premium#85 changes 47 build files plus one expected-output snapshot; neither repository even contains the generator or the hashers. TP-3 and TP-6 describe other consequences of the same stripping (the generated rewriter and the annotator) but propose their own changes, so they are not duplicates. What is specific to TP-9 is the regression test in HasherTests.cs, and it should cover both the compile-time and the run-time hasher, because the run-time hasher is the one used for a syntax tree with no compile-time code (DiffStrategy.cs:74-76) and is the path where a missed rename silently suppresses re-analysis. notes:
Verification of the finding itself. The SDK filter is present as described: Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Workspaces/MSBuildInitializer.cs:84 reads `.Where( i => i.ParsedVersion != null && i.ParsedVersion.Major <= Environment.Version.Major )`, so a process running on .NET 10 rejects a .NET 11 SDK, and the failure surfaces as the MSBuildInitializationException message at MSBuildInitializer.cs:92-94, which says that no compatible SDK was found and advises installing one or running the process with a different runtime. The two hosts are single-target: Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Workspaces/Metalama.Framework.Workspaces.csproj:18 declares `net10.0` and Metalama.LinqPad/src/Metalama.LinqPad/Metalama.LinqPad.csproj:6 declares `net10.0-windows`.

The proposed change is not implemented. Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Workspaces/README.md and Metalama.LinqPad/src/Metalama.LinqPad/README.md contain no statement about the host runtime, the .NET SDK, or their relationship; both are short package descriptions with links to the conceptual and API documentation. `git log` on the two files shows no commit since 129f3040 (a merge of pull request #1771, on the 2026.1 line). Metalama.Framework/docs/platform-support.md contains no occurrence of "Workspaces" or "LinqPad", and Directory.Packages.md mentions Workspaces only in the Roslyn binding-identity paragraph at line 178 and LinqPad only in the solution list at line 326.

The nearest existing statement is a build-file comment, not user documentation. Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Workspaces/Metalama.Framework.Workspaces.csproj:5-17 states that the MSBuild version, and therefore the .NET runtime version, must match the version of the .NET SDK used for the project, that only .NET 10 is supported, and that Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild 5.10 ships assets for net10.0 and net472 only. That comment is addressed to a maintainer reading the project file, it explains the choice of target framework rather than the requirement placed on the user's machine, and it is not visible to a consumer of either package.

Pull requests. The open pull requests do not touch this. metalama/Metalama#1879 changes only the linker, the code model and aspect tests, and its survey entry records that no Markdown, .props, .targets or eng/ file is modified. metalama/Metalama.Premium#84 changes two build files of Premium. metalama/Metalama.Premium#85 changes build files of Premium and one expected-output snapshot; it adds no net11.0 string anywhere, and Premium contains no Workspaces or LinqPad project. Among the pull requests merged since 2026-08-15, only #1883 and #1877 touch the two host projects, and both do so by changing target frameworks; #1891 added Metalama.Framework/docs/platform-support.md, which does not mention either package; #1886 added the MetalamaPlatformRequirement item for user projects.

Issues. Two searches of metalama/Metalama returned nothing that implements or scopes this. The first ("Workspaces or LinqPad requires a .NET SDK matching the host runtime major version") returned #944, #1832, #1247 and #422, none of which is about documenting the requirement. The second ("MSBuildLocator cannot find a compatible SDK, net11.0 target for the LinqPad driver") returned nineteen issues, of which the only open and relevant ones are #1921, the .NET 11 meta-issue, and #679, an unrelated Rider assembly-locator defect. The sub-issue list of #1921 (#1860, #1861, #1864, #1865, #1876, #1884, #1881, #1887, #1893, #1894, #1896, #1897, #1898, #1903, #1913, #1885) contains no documentation issue for these two packages, and no issue proposing a net11.0 target for the LinqPad driver.

Scope caution for the story. The finding proposes no code change to the filter, and that restraint should be preserved: the constraint at MSBuildInitializer.cs:84 is a property of MSBuild, since an SDK of a higher major band cannot be loaded into a lower runtime, so widening the filter would replace a clear failure by a load failure. The story is therefore a documentation story, and it should also state that the second half of the proposal, a net11.0 target for the LinqPad driver, is conditional on a LINQPad release that hosts .NET 11, which is unverified in this session.

evidence:
CS0261 for a union part and a struct part. `ErrorCode.ERR_PartialTypeKindConflict = 261` (dotnet/roslyn main, src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Errors/ErrorCode.cs:224). Its message now names unions explicitly: "Partial declarations of '{0}' must be all classes, all record classes, all structs, all unions, all record structs, or all interfaces" (src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/CSharpResources.resx:1161-1163). A union declaration has its own declaration kind, `DeclarationKind.Union`, and `EnumConversions.ToDeclarationKind` maps `SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration` to it (src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Declarations/DeclarationKind.cs:27,40). Partial parts merge only when name, arity and kind are equal (src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Declarations/SingleTypeDeclaration.cs:249-262, `TypeDeclarationIdentity.Equals`), so a `partial union` part and a `partial struct` part never merge, and the diagnostic is reported at namespace level by SourceNamespaceSymbol.cs:358-359 (`case ({ IsPartial: true }, SourceMemberContainerTypeSymbol { IsPartial: true })`) and for nested types by SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:1457-1460. The premise is confirmed.

A union has TypeKind.Struct and IsRecord false. `EnumConversions.ToTypeKind` maps `DeclarationKind.Struct`, `DeclarationKind.Union` and `DeclarationKind.RecordStruct` to `TypeKind.Struct` (src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/EnumConversions.cs:34-37). `SourceMemberContainerTypeSymbol.IsRecord` and `IsRecordStruct` compare `declaration.Declarations[0].Kind` with `DeclarationKind.Record` and `DeclarationKind.RecordStruct` respectively (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:1038-1051), so both are false for a union, while `IsUnionDeclaration` (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:1054-1058) is the union flag. The premise that a union reaches the `TypeKind.Struct when !type.IsRecord` arm is therefore sound on the Roslyn side.

`partial` is legal on a union. `MakeModifiers` adds `DeclarationModifiers.Partial` to the allowed modifiers of `TypeKind.Struct` and withholds only `Ref` from a union (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:341-347).

The open question is resolved, and its answer is the opposite of the hypothesis. The parser makes the case list optional for a union: `var paramList = CurrentToken.Kind == SyntaxKind.OpenParenToken || isExtension ? ParseParenthesizedParameterList(forExtensionOrUnion: isExtension || isUnion) : null;` (src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Parser/LanguageParser.cs:1838-1839), and `UnionDeclarationSyntax.ParameterList` is nullable in the public API (src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt:43, and the sole factory `SyntaxFactory.UnionDeclaration(...)` at line 71 takes `ParameterListSyntax? parameterList`). Only one part may carry it: `noteTypeParameters` assigns `builder.DeclarationWithParameters` for the first part that has a parameter list and reports `ERR_MultipleRecordParameterLists` for any further one (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:4107-4149), whose message is "Only a single partial type declaration may have a parameter list" (CSharpResources.resx:6621-6623) and whose code is 8863 (ErrorCode.cs:1872). `ERR_UnionDeclarationNeedsCaseTypes` (CS9370, ErrorCode.cs:2475) is reported only when no part carries a parameter list (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:4992-5060). Every union part is visited even when it has neither a case list nor members, because `DeclarationTreeBuilder` sets `HasAnyNontypeMembers` unconditionally for a union declaration (src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Declarations/DeclarationTreeBuilder.cs:744-747), so the generated part is processed and simply returns from `noteTypeParameters` (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:4109-4112). The csharplang grammar does write the case list as mandatory and says nothing about partial parts (proposals/csharp-15.0/unions.md:741-748; the only occurrence of "partial" in the document is line 742).

Modifier merging across partial parts. `MakeAndCheckTypeModifiers` combines the modifiers of the parts with `result |= mods` (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:453-459), `DeclarationModifiers.Closed` is in the allowed set of `TypeKind.Class` (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:331-332), and `IsClosed` reads the merged flags (`internal sealed override bool IsClosed => HasFlag(DeclarationModifiers.Closed)`, SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:902). No diagnostic requires every part to repeat `closed`; the only `closed` conflicts are with `sealed`, `static` and explicit `abstract` (CS9381 and CS9384, SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:374-381, ErrorCode.cs:2490,2493). The closed-class statement is therefore verified rather than plausible.

Standard citation. In ECMA-334 draft-v8, §15.2.7 is the section "Partial type declarations"; the "if one or more parts" rules for `abstract`, `sealed` and `static` are stated in the class-modifier subsections of §15.2.2 and only cross-reference §15.2.7 (standard/classes.md lines 98, 108, 130). The standard describes no `closed` modifier, so it cannot state the rule for it.

Feasibility of the proposed factory call. `SyntaxKind.UnionKeyword` is a contextual keyword whose text is "union" and which maps to `SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration` (src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Syntax/SyntaxKindFacts.cs:867, 1305, 1438, 1892), so `SyntaxFactory.Token(SyntaxKind.UnionKeyword)` produces the keyword token. `UnionDeclarationSyntax` and `SyntaxFactory.UnionDeclaration` appear on `main` without an `[RSEXPERIMENTAL006]` prefix (PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt:36-71), consistent with the addendum of FACTS.md lines 55-56 and with report 08 section "Attribute changes between the 5.10 snap and the 5.11 snap": the markers were removed on 2026-08-11 and the first stable package without them is expected to be 5.12.

Language-version condition. The `union` keyword is recognised as a type-declaration keyword only when the feature is enabled: `IsEnabledRecordOrUnionKeyword` calls `IsFeatureEnabled(MessageID.IDS_FeatureUnions)` (LanguageParser.cs:1678-1690). Per FACTS.md lines 54-56, no Roslyn that Metalama consumes today exposes C# 15 as a non-preview language version, so this scenario arises only on the Roslyn 5.12 latest variant, or under `LanguageVersion.Preview` before it.

Base list on a union. The parser parses a base list for a union like any non-extension type declaration (LanguageParser.cs:1841), the public API exposes `UnionDeclarationSyntax.BaseList` (PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt:42), and the interfaces of a type declared in several parts are the union of the interfaces of each part (standard/classes.md:341). The only union-specific restriction is CS9387 for a union member provider interface (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:2103-2106, CSharpResources.resx:8381-8383), which is not an interface that Metalama introduces. The generator passes a non-null `baseList` whenever an interface is introduced (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Pipeline/DesignTime/DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs:176, 215-216, 288).

Do not copy the case list from the primary syntax: only one partial part may carry a parameter list, and a second one is CS8863, ERR_MultipleRecordParameterLists, "Only a single partial type declaration may have a parameter list" (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:4107-4149, ErrorCode.cs:1872, CSharpResources.resx:6621-6623). corrections.consequence_class: Diagnostic reported, namely the compiler error CS0261 in the generated design-time file, for a partial union with introduced members, on a Roslyn build where the union feature is enabled; no impact for a closed class, where the merged modifiers of the parts make the type closed even though the generated part does not repeat the modifier.

notes:
The finding survives. Its central premise, that the generated partial struct part collides with a partial union part and produces CS0261, is confirmed in the compiler sources, and the error message of ERR_PartialTypeKindConflict was updated to name unions, which is direct evidence that Roslyn intends this collision.

Three corrections.

First, the open question is resolved, and the answer is the reverse of the hypothesis it raised. A partial union part must not repeat the case list. The parser makes the parameter list optional for a union (LanguageParser.cs:1838-1839), exactly one part may carry it, and a second one is CS8863. CS9370, ERR_UnionDeclarationNeedsCaseTypes, is reported only when no part carries it. A part that carries neither a case list nor members is still processed, because DeclarationTreeBuilder.cs:744-747 sets HasAnyNontypeMembers unconditionally for a union declaration. The generator should therefore pass parameterList: null, which is what the two record arms already do, and the finding must not fall back to copying ParameterList from the primary declaration syntax.

Second, the closed-class statement is no longer merely plausible. Roslyn combines the modifiers of the parts with a bitwise OR in MakeAndCheckTypeModifiers, and IsClosed reads the merged value, so a generated part without the closed modifier compiles. The citation of the standard should be adjusted: in ECMA-334 draft-v8, §15.2.7 is the section defining partial type declarations, while the rules that a class is abstract, sealed or static if one or more parts say so are in the class-modifier subsections of §15.2.2 (standard/classes.md lines 98, 108 and 130). The standard has no closed modifier at all, so the compiler source is the only authority for it.

Third, the proposed change says the union part should have no base list. That would drop the introduced interfaces, which are the reason the design-time part is generated at all (DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs:176 and :215-216 build the base list from InjectInterface transformations). A union may implement interfaces: the parser parses a base list for a union, the node exposes BaseList, and the interfaces of the parts are merged. The only union-specific restriction is CS9387 for a union member provider interface, which is not an interface Metalama introduces. The arm should pass baseList through.

One condition worth recording in the finding. The whole scenario is reachable only where IDS_FeatureUnions is enabled. Per the addendum of FACTS.md, no Roslyn that Metalama consumes today exposes C# 15 as a non-preview language version, and the non-experimental union API first reaches a stable package in Roslyn 5.12, so this work belongs with the 5.12 latest variant and must be gated to it, as the finding already anticipates through CM-13.

One fact the finding does not record changes the shape of the fix. A central helper already exists: Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Utilities/Roslyn/SyntaxKindExtensions.cs:33-34 declares the extension property SyntaxKind.IsTypeDeclaration as the same hand-written list without UnionDeclaration, and line 41 declares IsBaseTypeDeclaration on top of it. CM-6 is not a duplicate of any other finding of the report. CM-7 is adjacent, because both concern syntax-level recognition of a union declaration, but it proposes visitor overrides rather than kind lists; a single story may reasonably carry both.

corrections.what_happens_today: Two premises need correction. First, the copied union does not compile silently. DeclarationTreeBuilder.VisitTypeDeclaration calls MessageID.IDS_FeatureUnions.CheckFeatureAvailability(diagnostics, node, node.Keyword.GetLocation()) for every UnionDeclarationSyntax it declares, nested or not (DeclarationTreeBuilder.cs on main and at the 5.10 window commit 27d6bed6), and the SyntaxNode overload evaluates the check against syntax.SyntaxTree.Options (MessageID.cs:396-406, 441-451, 466-467). Metalama creates the compile-time syntax tree with new CSharpParseOptions(languageVersion) where languageVersion is C# 14 (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:279, :351; FACTS). A union copied verbatim into the compile-time tree therefore produces an error at the union keyword in the compile-time compilation: ERR_FeatureInPreview with the consumed 5.10 preview (RequiredVersion is Preview there) and ERR_FeatureNotAvailableInVersion ("feature is not available in C# 14, please use language version 15.0 or greater") with Roslyn 5.12 (MessageID.cs:472-484, 500-505). The silent branch (union copied, no manifest entry, templates inside not transformed, no accessibility or TypeFabric checks) exists only once the compile-time language version is raised to C# 15 (TP-8). Second, the note about SourceNamedTypeImpl.TypeKind is resolved and no longer open: Roslyn adds no TypeKind value for unions (TypeKind.cs on main: 16 values, highest Extension = 14) and EnumConversions.ToTypeKind maps DeclarationKind.Union to TypeKind.Struct (EnumConversions.cs:35-38), consistent with the proposal that a union declaration is lowered to a plain struct (unions.md:783-790, 872). SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:69-78 therefore returns TypeKind.Struct for a union and does not throw. A further qualification: a UnionDeclarationSyntax node can only reach ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter when the user compilation was parsed with the union feature enabled, because the parser recognizes the contextual union keyword only when IsFeatureEnabled(IDS_FeatureUnions) (LanguageParser.cs:1678-1690, 2494-2510); under the current Metalama.Framework.targets rewrite of LangVersion 15.0 to 12.0 (FACTS), or under C# 14, the text `union U(A, B);` inside a class is parsed as something other than a union declaration. The finding describes the state after C# 15 is enabled for user code, which is the intended target of 2027.0.
corrections.consequence_class: While the compile-time language version is C# 14: diagnostic reported (a compile-time compilation error at the union keyword for a union nested in a compile-time type; compile-time compilation errors on references to a dropped compile-time union nested in a run-time type). Once the compile-time language version is C# 15 (TP-8): silent wrong output for the union nested in a compile-time type (missing manifest entry, untransformed templates, no accessibility or TypeFabric checks); the dropped union nested in a run-time type stays silent until a reference to it fails in the compile-time compilation.
corrections.proposed_change: Keep the proposal with three adjustments. (1) SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration cannot be named in the 5.0.0 variant either (Syntax-5.0.0.xml has no UnionDeclaration or UnionKeyword), so adding the kind to the three switch lists requires a #if ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER branch exactly like naming UnionDeclarationSyntax; only the type test avoids the variant branch for the switch lists, while the VisitUnionDeclaration overrides in the three visitors still require the latest variant (and, after the renumbering recorded in FACTS, that variant is 5.12). (2) The type test `member is TypeDeclarationSyntax` also matches ExtensionBlockDeclarationSyntax, which derives from TypeDeclarationSyntax in both grammars (Syntax-5.0.0.xml:2036, Syntax-5.10.0.xml:2083) and today falls into the default arm of TransformCompileTimeType (:555-558); write the test as `member is TypeDeclarationSyntax and not ExtensionBlockDeclarationSyntax` (and the same in PopulateNestedCompileTimeTypes) so that extension blocks keep their current path. (3) The open question is answered by the semantics: the proposal grammar uses struct_modifier and struct_member_declaration (unions.md:741-747), the declaration is lowered to a plain struct (unions.md:783-790, 872), Roslyn declares it with TypeKind.Struct (EnumConversions.cs:35-38), and the parser accepts it as a class member through ParseMemberDeclarationCore and IsTypeDeclarationStart (LanguageParser.cs:3249, 3317, 2494-2510). A union nested in a run-time type should therefore be treated like a struct in PopulateNestedCompileTimeTypes: report RunTimeTypesCannotHaveCompileTimeTypesExceptTypeFabrics when it is compile-time, with no un-nesting. The two proposed aspect tests remain appropriate; they must set the language version to 15.0 or preview, otherwise the parser does not produce a UnionDeclarationSyntax at all.
corrections.size: S after regeneration (unchanged).

notes: Premises checked and their status. (a) UnionDeclarationSyntax derives from TypeDeclarationSyntax: confirmed (Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1954; main Syntax.xml:3513). (b) The 5.0.0 variant cannot name UnionDeclarationSyntax: confirmed, and the same holds for SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration (zero occurrences in Syntax-5.0.0.xml). (c) The base rewriter copies the union with its members: confirmed; CSharpSyntaxRewriter.VisitUnionDeclaration exists in the consumed 5.10 API as [RSEXPERIMENTAL006] (delta report line 62), so Visit(member) on a UnionDeclarationSyntax rebuilds the node from its visited children. (d) \"Whether a copied union compiles depends on TP-8 and on where Roslyn checks IDS_FeatureUnions\": resolved rather than left open. The check is in DeclarationTreeBuilder.VisitTypeDeclaration and reads the parse options of the node's own syntax tree, so the copied union fails in a C# 14 compile-time compilation (ERR_FeatureInPreview under the consumed 5.10 preview, ERR_FeatureNotAvailableInVersion under 5.12) and compiles only when the compile-time language version becomes C# 15. This changes the consequence class for the compile-time-type case from silent to diagnostic-reported until TP-8 lands, after which the silent case applies. (e) \"The compile-time compilation is created with C# 14 parse options\": confirmed (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:279, :351; FACTS). (f) \"FACTS records no new TypeKind for unions, to be confirmed\": confirmed and closed; TypeKind has no Union member on main, and DeclarationKind.Union maps to TypeKind.Struct, so SourceNamedTypeImpl.TypeKind returns Struct and does not throw. (g) Nesting of a union declaration in a class is permitted by the parser (member-level path) and by the declaration builder (VisitTypeChildren); the proposal does not restrict it and its grammar uses struct member and modifier productions. The code search of dotnet/roslyn tests returned no test explicitly named for a nested union, so the nesting evidence is the parser and declaration code, not a test. (h) The experimental markers: on main, UnionDeclarationSyntax, WithElementSyntax and the Name fields of BreakStatementSyntax and ContinueStatementSyntax no longer carry ExperimentalUrl (main Syntax.xml:3513, 1874, 2503, 2514), only UnsafeExpressionSyntax does (line 1069); the consumed Syntax-5.10.0.xml still carries the marker on the union node (line 1954), so \"after regeneration\" means after adopting the 5.12 grammar, in line with the FACTS addendum. notes:
The central claim holds in the code. At CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:87 the argument tuple for LAMA0052 is built by calling ToDisplayStringSafe on the offending version, and that helper throws for any value it does not enumerate (LanguageVersionExtensions.cs:39). The value 1500 has no arm (the highest arm is (LanguageVersion) 1400 at line 34), so the diagnostic designed for the situation is replaced by the generic crash diagnostic LAMA0001. The catch at SourceTransformer.cs:145 and the isHandled assignment at CompileTimeExceptionHandler.cs:198 confirm that the exception is swallowed after the error is reported, so the build fails with LAMA0001 rather than terminating the compiler. The consequence class is accurate: the outcome is not silent, and it is not a wrong transformation.

Four details required correction.

First, the framing. The finding is titled and written as present-tense behaviour, but the code path cannot be entered with the Roslyn build the repository consumes. FACTS.md:54 records that LanguageVersion.CSharp15 is absent from Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 5.10.0-1.26365.3, so 15.0 is not parseable by the compiler and MapSpecifiedToEffectiveVersion cannot yield 1500. The defect is latent and becomes reachable only with the stable Roslyn that defines CSharp15.

Second, the confidence statement names "the stable 5.10". Per FACTS.md:48-49 no stable 5.10 exists and the November 2026 baseline is expected to carry Roslyn 5.12, so the trigger is the move to Roslyn 5.12.

Third, the scenario list is silent about the implicit case, which is intercepted upstream. Metalama.Framework.targets:118-121 rewrites an implicitly set LangVersion that is not one of 12.0, 13.0, 14.0, default, latest, latestMajor or preview to 12.0 and warns, so only an explicitly written 15.0, default, latest or latestMajor can carry 1500 into the pipeline.

Fourth, the claim about TemplateExpansionContext.cs:874-875 is half right. The guard at TemplateExpansionContext.cs:867 requires requiredLanguageVersion to be greater than targetLanguageVersion, so targetLanguageVersion at line 875 can never be 1500 inside that branch; only requiredLanguageVersion at line 874 can, and only after LV-3 makes RoslynApiVersion.ToLanguageVersion return 1500 (today it caps at CSharp14, SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:59-60).

On the proposed change, two engineering points. The explicit 1500 arm and the numeric fallback are redundant with each other; the fallback alone covers every future version, so proposing both is not minimal. If an explicit arm is wanted, the codebase convention is AllLanguageVersions.cs, which exists precisely to name versions the compiled-against Roslyn may not define. The fallback must remain the discard arm: replacing the discard by a relational pattern arm leaves the switch expression non-exhaustive, which produces CS8509, and CodeQuality.targets promotes warnings to errors under ContinuousIntegrationBuild. Both forms compile against the Roslyn 5.0 and the latest variants, because neither names a member absent from the lower reference assembly. The unit test is feasible: the class is internal but Metalama.Framework.Engine.csproj:45 grants InternalsVisibleTo to the unit test project.

One observation that strengthens the finding: the existing aspect test LanguageVersion.cs with @LanguageVersion(8.0) and its baseline LanguageVersion.t.cs:2 pin LAMA0052, and they pass only because 800 happens to have an arm in the switch. No test covers a version above the supported range, which is why the asymmetry is not caught.

notes:
The finding is sound in substance and wrong in one number. The restore failure it describes is real and was confirmed independently against nuget.org for all five Roslyn packages the cited projects reference. What does not survive is the version it names as the exit: there is no stable Roslyn 5.10, and there will not be one, so a plan phrased as "until the stable Roslyn 5.10 is consumed" has no event to wait for. The exit is either the stable 5.12 expected in November 2026 or the stable 5.9.0 that is already published.

Three qualifications are worth carrying into the report.

First, the November 2026 date is an inference from the quarterly release cadence and from the version bumps on dotnet/roslyn main, not a published commitment. The impact report states this explicitly at 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:15, and its limitations section adds that the Roslyn version of the .NET 11 general availability SDK is not published. A release gate that is written as if the date were fixed will need revision if the cadence changes.

Second, the gate has a prerequisite outside this repository. Step 1 of updating-roslyn.md is to update Metalama.Compiler first, and Metalama.Compiler is not cloned in this session, so no statement about its readiness for Roslyn 5.12 can be made here.

Third, the fallback to the stable 5.9.0 deserves to be stated in the finding, because it changes the shape of the risk. The 5.9.0 assemblies expose the same public API as the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3, so the move would be a renumbering that does not remove any API the code uses, and it would remove the prerelease dependency without waiting for November. It buys nothing for C# 15, because neither build exposes LanguageVersion.CSharp15, but the C# 15 work is a separate gate from the public restorability of the packages.

The open question about the LINQPad `Package:` assembly metadata is outside the sources of authority assigned to this verification and remains open. It does not affect the verdict, because the Workspaces and AspectTesting package dependencies fail on nuget.org regardless of what LINQPad does with that metadata.

The proposed build check that fails packing when RoslynMaxVersion carries a prerelease label and the configuration is public is not affected by any of the above and remains a reasonable safeguard.

notes: Refutation attempts. (1) The pins: all three locations in eng/src/Program.cs and the props comment are exactly as stated, except that the finding cites `Metalama.Framework.props` without its directory; the file is Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Package/build/Metalama.Framework.props, and the buildTransitive copy only imports it. Confirmed. (2) \"Corresponds to the .NET 10 SDK era\": Program.cs:26 pins 10.0.400 and platform-support.md:199-203 records that this is the SDK Visual Studio 2026 18.9 installs. Confirmed. (3) \"A later MSBuild\": the Roslyn main branch is versioned 5.12 and its version bumps are titled after Visual Studio 18.11 and 18.12, and Roslyn minor versions map to Visual Studio minor versions (platform-support.md:149-151), so the November 2026 MSBuild is expected to be 18.12. Plausible; the branding \"Visual Studio 2027\" and its major number could not be verified because learn.microsoft.com is not reachable from this session. The open question stands. (4) \"By A2, a Roslyn at or above 5.10\": the bound is true but the inference LV-11 draws from it, that `GetMaxLanguageVersion` must map `(5, >= 10)` to C# 15, rests on A2's statement that any Roslyn at or above 5.10 supports C# 15, which the FACTS addendum (lines 54-56) and the delta report (lines 18, 32) refute for 5.10 and for 5.11 builds before 2026-08-11. The finding survives because its subject, the stale Build Tools pin and the coverage gap for the November MSBuild, does not depend on the exact boundary; only the boundary constant changes. (5) `GetLanguageVersionFromMSBuild` reads the assembly version, not the informational version, so a 5.12 stable and a 5.12 preview both present `5.12.0.0`, and the `(5, >= 12)` boundary cannot distinguish them; this is acceptable because the only 5.12 builds are on or after the 2026-08-25 bump, all of which contain `CSharp15`. (6) The MSBuild.exe cap concerns which language version Metalama selects for the compile-time compilation; the compilation itself is performed by the hosting Roslyn of Metalama.Compiler, so a wrong cap of C# 15 with a compiler still on Roslyn 5.10 would fail through the LV-2 path (`ToDisplayStringSafe` throwing for 1500) rather than at the MSBuild Roslyn. This reinforces that the boundary must follow the compiler's Roslyn (5.12 per the addendum) and not the earliest preview that carried the feature. No statement about C# 15 feature semantics or the csharplang proposals is made by this finding, so those sources were not needed.

Value { get; }` (unions.md:787). One case is not covered by the rule: the proposal also recognises any class carrying `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.UnionAttribute` as a union type (unions.md:12, :37 and the `[AttributeUsage(Class | Struct)]` declaration at unions.md:42-43). notes:
The finding survives. Its central external premise, that a union is a value type and therefore not TypeKind.Class, is correct and well supported by both the proposal and the Roslyn symbol mapping, and its conclusion, that no code change is needed and one test should be added, stands.

Three corrections were needed and none of them overturns it. The first is that the outcome is two diagnostics rather than one, because the AttributeUsage of ObservableAttribute excludes structs; this matters only for the expected output of the proposed test, and it is a fact about the attribute declaration combined with the C# semantics of a union, not about Metalama logic. The second is that the proposal recognises a second, attribute-marked form of union that can be a class and that does pass the eligibility rule; that form is the subject of an unresolved csharplang open question, so it is a scoping note rather than a defect. The third is a sequencing fact: nothing in this finding can be implemented before Roslyn 5.12 and the raising of Metalama's supported language version, because unions are a preview-only feature in every Roslyn build Metalama consumes today.

Two items I could not verify and that are stated as such. Whether Roslyn accepts `[Union]` on a class in practice, as opposed to in the proposal text, was not checked against the compiler binaries; only the proposal and the error codes recorded in the API delta report were read. Whether an inherited `[Observable]` instance, propagated from an interface annotated with the aspect to a union that implements it, is silently skipped or reported was not traced through the inheritance path; the `ExceptForInheritance()` qualifier at ObservableAttribute.cs:52 excludes only EligibleScenarios.Inheritance, which the documentation at Metalama.Framework/Eligibility/EligibleScenarios.cs:55-61 describes as the aspect propagating to derived types, so the class rule still applies when the inherited instance is applied to the union itself.

notes:
The central claim is supported by the code and survives the attempt to refute it. Four details required correction.

First, the crash site is wrong for most cases. LinkerInjectionRegistry.cs:326 is reached only if template expansion has already succeeded, and template expansion fails first, because it needs a lexical scope and LexicalScopeFactory derives the type declaration through GetDeclaringType, whose kind list also omits UnionDeclaration. For a union at namespace level the failure is therefore at LexicalScopeFactory.cs:193 (override) or 121 (introduction). For a union nested in a class, GetDeclaringType silently returns the enclosing class, so the lexical scope is wrong rather than absent and execution proceeds to the registry. For a union in a compilation unit with no namespace, FindMemberDeclaration throws at SyntaxExtensions.cs:21 while the insert position is computed.

Second, the exception type is not AssertionFailedException in a shipped build. Invariant.AssertNotNull throws only under `#if DEBUG` (Invariant.cs:146-165); the release overload returns the null reference, so the same sites raise NullReferenceException or ArgumentNullException. The consequence class "crash" is correct either way.

Third, LinkerInjectionRegistry.cs:325 can throw KeyNotFoundException before line 326, because _transformedSyntaxTreeMap contains only syntax trees the rewriter actually modified.

Fourth, two citation slips: the `is BaseTypeDeclarationSyntax` test attributed to SyntaxExtensions.cs:73 is at CodeModelExtensions.cs:73, and the Compile item of the 5.0.0 variant project is at line 6, not line 7. The Where paths are also missing the Metalama.Framework/src prefix.

The proposed change is workable. SafeSyntaxRewriter seals Visit and documents VisitCore as the extension point, and VisitTypeDeclaration<T> compiles with T = TypeDeclarationSyntax. Two wording defects: the dispatch must discriminate on node type rather than SyntaxKind, because RecordDeclarationSyntax carries two kinds; and the type test must be added to the kind lists of FindMemberDeclarationOrNull and FindSymbolDeclaringNode rather than substituted for them. The change is also incomplete as written unless GetDeclaringType is fixed, which the finding does list but does not identify as the first failure point.

Two scope observations that are not defects. The behaviour is prospective rather than current: a union cannot reach the linker unless the project compiles under a preview language version, since Metalama.Framework.targets rewrites an implicitly set LangVersion to 12.0 and CompileTimeAspectPipeline.VerifyLanguageVersion rejects anything outside SupportedCSharpVersions.All (FACTS.md). And ExtensionBlockDeclaration is missing from the same three kind lists without ill effect, because an extension block is never the subject of ToInsertPosition; that is why the omission of UnionDeclaration was not caught by the existing tests.

corrections.what_happens_today:
`VerifyLanguageVersion` is declared only in `CompileTimeAspectPipeline` (lines 62 to 92) and called only at line 177. Its comment at lines 64 and 65 states that Roslyn does not set the language version properly at design time, so the other pipelines do not check it. A search over `Metalama.Framework.DesignTime` and `Engine/Pipeline/DesignTime` finds no read of `LanguageVersion`, `AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures` or `SupportedCSharpVersions`; the only match is the comment at `DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs:54`. One language version check is nevertheless reachable at design time, although it does not cover `LangVersion`: `TemplateCompiler.TryReadProjectOptions` (`TemplateCompiler.cs:56-79`) validates the `MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion` property against `SupportedCSharpVersions.All` and reports LAMA0052, and it runs both from `CompileTimeCompilationBuilder` (line 295) and from `TemplatingCodeValidator`, which the design-time analyzer invokes (`TheDiagnosticAnalyzer.cs:181`).

The compile-time project is built with `LanguageVersionProvider` in every scenario, design time included (`ServiceProviderFactory.cs:170`, `CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:279`), and that provider caps the project version at C# 14 for any SDK major of 10 or more (`LanguageVersionProvider.cs:56`).

The description of a C# 15 project requires three corrections.

First, a project whose C# 15 language version is implicit is not analysed at C# 14. When `LangVersion` is not set in the project file, Metalama.Compiler sets `LangVersionImplicitlySet`, and `Metalama.Framework.targets:118-120` rewrites `LangVersion` to 12.0 for any value outside 12.0, 13.0, 14.0, `default`, `latest`, `latestMajor` and `preview`. The `MetalamaCheckLangVersion` target at lines 243 to 246 then emits a warning during the build. The rewrite happens during property evaluation, so the design-time build sees 12.0 as well, and the two agree at C# 12.

Second, LAMA0052 cannot be raised for the value 15.0 with the Roslyn versions consumed today, and `ToDisplayStringSafe` cannot receive the value 1500. `LanguageVersion.CSharp15` is absent from Roslyn 5.0.0 and from the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 build, so `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse` fails at `MSBuildProjectOptions.cs:173` and the fallback at line 178 returns `SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest`, while the command line compiler rejects an explicit `LangVersion` of 15.0 with its own error before the pipeline runs. The `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` of `LanguageVersionExtensions.cs:39` is therefore a hazard of the move to a Roslyn that defines C# 15, not a description of the present state.

Third, the case that is genuinely silent at design time today is `LangVersion=preview`. `MSBuildProjectOptions.LanguageVersion` returns `Preview`, `LanguageVersionProvider` caps the compile-time compilation at C# 14, no diagnostic is produced in the editor, and the build reports LAMA0051 (`CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:70-78`) unless `MetalamaAllowPreviewLanguageFeatures` is set (line 72). The aspect test `LanguageVersionPreview` pins that message, and the test `Misc/LanguageVersion` pins LAMA0052 for the value 8.0.

The generated design-time syntax trees reuse the parse options of the compilation (`DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs:54-57`), so they follow the project language version and need no change.
corrections.consequence_class: Today the inconsistency is real but narrow: `LangVersion=preview` is silent at design time and reports LAMA0051 at build, while an implicitly set C# 15 language version is lowered to C# 12 by the targets, with a build warning, consistently at design time and at build. After the move to a Roslyn that defines `LanguageVersion.CSharp15`, and before `SupportedCSharpVersions` is extended, the compile-time pipeline no longer reports LAMA0052 for such a project but throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` in `ToDisplayStringSafe`. `SourceTransformer` catches that exception and reports it through `ICompileTimeExceptionHandler` (`SourceTransformer.cs:145-158`), so the build fails with an internal error diagnostic instead of the intended message, and the compiler does not crash.
corrections.proposed_change: No design-time change is required. The compile-time change must add `AllLanguageVersions.CSharp15 = (LanguageVersion) 1500`, which follows the numeric cast pattern already used for versions 10 to 14 (`AllLanguageVersions.cs:14-18`) and therefore compiles against both the Roslyn 5.0 and the latest reference assemblies, extend `SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest`, `All`, `ToLanguageVersion` and `GetMaxLanguageVersion`, add the 1500 case to `ToDisplayStringSafe`, and add a case for SDK major 11 in `LanguageVersionProvider.GetLanguageVersionFromDotNetSdk`. It must also update the two aspect test baselines that embed the list of supported versions, `Tests/Aspects/Misc/LanguageVersion.t.cs` and `Tests/Aspects/LanguageVersion/LanguageVersionPreview.t.cs`, and revise the value list of the `LangVersion` rewrite in `Metalama.Framework.targets:118`, which does not contain 15.0 and therefore lowers an implicitly set C# 15 project to C# 12. Keeping the design-time pipeline free of the `LangVersion` check remains correct, because the design-time host may present a Roslyn whose `Default` maps to a different version from the one used during the build.
corrections.size: S

notes: The central claim of DT-4, that the language version verification lives only in `CompileTimeAspectPipeline` and that no design-time code path verifies the project `LangVersion`, is supported by the code and by the two aspect test baselines that pin LAMA0051 and LAMA0052 as compile-time-only failures. Three supporting details were refuted and corrected: a design-time-reachable check does exist for the separate `MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion` property; an implicitly set C# 15 project is lowered to C# 12 by `Metalama.Framework.targets` at both design time and build, not processed at C# 14; and neither LAMA0052 for the value 15.0 nor the `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for 1500 can occur with the Roslyn versions consumed today, since `LanguageVersion.CSharp15` does not exist there. The exception is also caught and converted into an internal error diagnostic rather than crashing the compiler. The proposed change remains valid and minimal, and the numeric cast pattern of `AllLanguageVersions` confirms that it compiles in both Roslyn variants, but it must additionally cover the two aspect test baselines and the value list of the targets rewrite.

Placing `"5.10.0"` in it would produce the order `4.0.1, 4.4.0, 4.8.0, 4.12.0, 5.10.0, 5.0.0, 5.12.0`, and the position in that array is the version order: `RoslynVersion.Index` (`Model/RoslynVersion.cs:13,15`) drives `VersionDetector.DetectVersions` (`Model/VersionDetector.cs:13,21,37-38,52`), the numeric values of the generated enum (`Generator.cs:90`) and the `TargetApiVersion` switch (`Generator.cs:442-473`), and `RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier` compares `RoslynApiVersion` values ordinally (`RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier.cs:48,70,85`). `V5_10_0` would take the value 4 and `V5_0_0` the value 5, which inverts the two versions and mis-attributes the minimal version of every syntax node and field. The correct edit keeps the ordering: write `string[] versionNames = [.. legacyVersionNames, "5.0.0", "5.10.0", "5.12.0"]` and introduce a separate collection, for example `string[] versionsWithoutGeneratedCode = [.. legacyVersionNames, "5.10.0"]`, against which the skip test at `GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:32` is performed. The rest of item 3 stands: `V5_10_0` then remains a member of the generated enum, `Syntax-5.10.0.xml` stays beside the new `Syntax-5.12.0.xml`, and the generated directory becomes `.generated/5.12.0`. The proposed range test in `SatisfiesCurrentProcess` is also unsound as stated. Accepting any declared version at or below the current one would make both entries of a two-variant extension satisfy the current process, because a package registers one `MetalamaExtensionAssembly` item per variant (`Metalama.Framework/docs/extensibility.md:129-136`). `ExtensionLoaderBase.GetExtensionAssemblyPaths` returns every satisfying reference (`ExtensionLoaderBase.cs:35-37`), `LoadExtensionAssemblies` loads each path (`:66-80`) and `DiscoverExtensionTypes` collects the `ExportExtensionAttribute` of each assembly with no deduplication (`:119-138`), so every extension of that package would be registered twice. Prefer the second alternative already named in the proposal: report a diagnostic, or at least a warning, from `GetExtensionAssemblyPaths` when a package declares extension assemblies and every one of them is rejected. A range test, if wanted, has to be accompanied by a selection of the highest satisfying variant per package rather than by acceptance of all of them.

ExecuteAsync then calls context.UpdateTree with an unchanged root (ChangeVisibilityCodeAction.cs:46-48), and CodeActionContext.ToCodeActionResult reports the file as changed (CodeActionContext.cs:82-93). The user sees the code fix succeed and nothing change. The interface and indexer cases exist today and are independent of C# 15. C# 15 adds a third case, the union declaration: UnionDeclarationSyntax derives from TypeDeclarationSyntax (Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1954-1978) and a union declaration accepts accessibility modifiers (csharplang csharp-15.0/unions.md:741-744 and 763). That case is not reachable on the dependencies consumed today, because the node is marked experimental in the consumed Roslyn 5.10.0-1.26365.3 and unions are gated on LanguageVersion.Preview there (MessageID of the 5.10 window, lines 496-505); it becomes reachable with the move to the stable Roslyn 5.12.
corrections.proposed_change: Replace the per-kind overrides on type declarations with a single branch that applies TypeDeclarationSyntax.WithModifiers to any TypeDeclarationSyntax. Place it in an override of VisitCore, not of Visit: SafeSyntaxRewriter.Visit is sealed (SafeSyntaxRewriter.cs:44) and the class directs derived classes to VisitCore. TypeDeclarationSyntax.WithModifiers is shipped public API on every consumed variant (PublicAPI.Shipped.txt:2607), so the branch covers interfaces today and unions later without naming UnionDeclarationSyntax, which is experimental in the consumed build and absent from the Roslyn 5.0 grammar. Do not claim that it covers extension blocks: the extension declaration grammar has no modifier production (csharplang csharp-14.0/extensions.md:32-34), and in any case the rewriter changes modifiers only on the declaring syntax references of the target symbol (ChangeVisibilityCodeAction.cs:127). Add VisitIndexerDeclaration, which also covers the extension indexers that C# 15 introduces, since they reuse IndexerDeclarationSyntax. Add aspect tests ChangeVisibility_Interface and ChangeVisibility_Indexer, which need no new language version. Defer a union test: it requires the move to the stable Roslyn 5.12, in which LanguageVersion.CSharp15 exists (main LanguageVersion.cs:283) and the experimental marker on the union node is removed (main Syntax.xml:3513), plus LangVersion 15 and the corresponding raise of Metalama's own language version plumbing. If such a test is added, it needs a @RequiredConstant, and Premium must define the constant in the props of its latest Roslyn variant, whose number follows the core variant and is expected to be 5.12.0 rather than 5.10.0; Premium defines no such constant today (its only variant props are Roslyn.4.12.0.props:8 and Roslyn.5.0.0.props:8).
corrections.consequence_class: Silent wrong output.
