notes:
The finding survives the correction. Its substance, which is that the rewriter silently reports success while changing nothing for declaration kinds it does not handle, rests on the interface and indexer cases, and neither depends on C# 15. The union case is a correctly identified future addition: unions are a C# 15 feature, their declaration node derives from TypeDeclarationSyntax, and a union declaration accepts accessibility modifiers, so it would fall into the same gap.

Two premises about the version timeline are wrong and are corrected above. There is no stable Roslyn 5.10, and LangVersion 15 is not selectable on the build Metalama consumes today, where unions are a preview feature. The correct statement is that the union test waits for Roslyn 5.12.

Two further corrections concern the proposed remedy rather than the defect. SafeSyntaxRewriter.Visit is sealed, so the single override must be on VisitCore. An extension block cannot carry an accessibility modifier, so the claim that the blanket override covers extension blocks is inaccurate, although the override remains harmless for them.

One item was not verified in this session and is stated as an assumption in the corrected text: whether Metalama.Compiler will move to Roslyn 5.12, which FACTS.md:50 records as unverified because that repository is not cloned. The union test depends on it.

Verdict: the proposed change is "None.", and the code confirms that nothing needs to be done. No pull request and no issue implements or scopes any change here, and none is required.

Verification of the mechanism the finding describes.

1. /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/TestOptions.cs:681-700 handles the `@LanguageVersion` directive. When `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse` fails (line 682) and the argument is an integral number greater than or equal to 10 (line 689), the option sets `SkipReason` (line 691) instead of throwing. The comment at line 688 states the intent explicitly: "The version may be a valid number but still not recognized by the current version of Roslyn." A non-numeric or non-integral argument still throws `InvalidTestOptionException` (line 696), and the comment at line 695 records why the distinction matters: "Throwing here may kill test discovery."

2. /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/TestOptions.cs:702-721 repeats the same structure for `@DependencyLanguageVersion`, with the skip at line 712 and the throw at line 717.

3. The skip reaches xunit. /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/TestOptions.cs:48 declares `SkipReason` and line 53 declares `IsSkipped`. /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/TestInput.cs:72 copies it into the test input, /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/XunitFramework/TestCase.cs:46-53 exposes it as the xunit skip reason, and /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/XunitFramework/TestExecutor.cs:311 reports `new TestSkipped( test, testInput.SkipReason )`. A test file carrying `// @LanguageVersion(15)` therefore reports as skipped, not as failed.

4. The runner applies the parsed version only when one was parsed. /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/BaseTestRunner.cs:218-224 starts from `SupportedCSharpVersions.DefaultParseOptions` (line 218) and calls `WithLanguageVersion` only inside `if ( testInput.Options.LanguageVersion != null )` (lines 221-224). A skipped test never reaches this code, so there is no path that would pass an unrecognized version to Roslyn.

5. The two variants share the same test files, so the per-file skip is the only separation available. /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Metalama.Framework.Tests.AspectTests.5.0.0/Metalama.Framework.Tests.AspectTests.5.0.0.csproj:10 includes `../Metalama.Framework.Tests.AspectTests/**/*.cs`, and line 12 imports `eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.5.0.0.props`. The same shape exists for the linker, template, unit test and benchmark suites (the `.5.0.0` directories under /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/tests/).

6. A second, explicit selector already exists for cases where a test must run in one variant only: `@RequiredConstant` and `@ForbiddenConstant` (/home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/TestOptions.cs:609-616, applied in /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/TestInput.cs:76-95). /home/user/Metalama/eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.5.10.0.props:10 defines `ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER` for the latest variant only, and two aspect tests already use the pair: /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Metalama.Framework.Tests.AspectTests/Tests/Aspects/DesignTimeInvalidCode/UnknownAccessorInTemplate.cs:7 and .../UnknownAccessorInTemplate_Roslyn5_0.cs:7.

Two qualifications to the finding as worded, neither of which creates work.

A. The title says the infrastructure "already skips C# 15 tests in the Roslyn 5.0 variant". The mechanism is not variant-aware; it is version-agnostic. It skips whenever the Roslyn that the test assembly was built against does not recognize the number. According to FACTS.md line 54, neither the Roslyn 5.0 variant nor the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 preview exposes `LanguageVersion.CSharp15`, so today such a test would be skipped in both variants, not only in the Roslyn 5.0 one. evidence:
Premise 1, the renumbering target is 5.12. Confirmed. `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/roslyn/main/eng/Versions.props` lines 7-8 give `MajorVersion` 5 and `MinorVersion` 12 (fetched 2026-09-03). `git ls-remote --heads https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn refs/heads/release/dev18*` returns only `release/dev18.0` and `release/dev18.3`. The flat-container index of `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp` on nuget.org ends at 5.0.0, 5.3.0-2.final, 5.3.0, 5.6.0, 5.9.0, so stable packages appear at every third minor and the next one is 5.12. `08-roslyn-api-delta.md` summary point 1 records the same cadence and states that the November 2026 date is an inference. Two datings support the date: 5.9.0 was published on 2026-08-17, about seven weeks after `main` left the 5.9 window on 2026-06-29, and `main` entered the 5.12 window on 2026-08-25 (`08-roslyn-api-delta.md` reference table).

Premise 1b, the .NET 11 SDK as build host. `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/sdk/v11.0.100-preview.7.26381.103/eng/Version.Details.xml` pins `Microsoft.Net.Compilers.Toolset` at 5.10.0-1.26363.117, that is a Roslyn build of 2026-07-13 in an SDK build of 2026-07-31 (Arcade short date, `(year-2000)*1000 + month*50 + day`). This is one minor behind `main` at the same date and corrects `08-roslyn-api-delta.md` summary point 4, which recorded 5.8.0 at preview.5 (2026-06-01) and no later tag. Extrapolating the same one-minor lag to a November 2026 general availability gives 5.12 for the .NET 11 SDK.

Premise 2, `V5_12_0 => CSharp15`. Confirmed. `LanguageVersion.CSharp15 = 1500` was added by dotnet/roslyn#84799 on 2026-08-11, inside the 5.11 window, and `Default`, `Latest` and `LatestMajor` map to it from the same commit (`08-roslyn-api-delta.md`, table "Members added to `main` after the 5.10 window", row `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.LanguageVersion`; FACTS.md:55). The 5.12 window opened on 2026-08-25, after that commit, so every 5.12 build carries the member.

Premise 3, the roll-forward argument behind the threshold of `RoslynVariantPolicy` and behind the proposed range test in `SatisfiesCurrentProcess`. Confirmed at its root: `eng/Versions.props` line 16 on `main` sets `AssemblyVersion` to `$(MajorVersion).$(MinorVersion).0.0` for official builds, which is why a payload bound against 5.10 loads in a 5.12 host and never the reverse, as `Metalama.Framework/docs/platform-support.md:248-249` and `Metalama.Framework/docs/updating-roslyn.md:16` assert. `08-roslyn-api-delta.md`, paragraph introducing the API delta table, records that nothing was removed from the public API between 5.0 and `main` apart from `params` and experimental-attribute changes, so such a load is also source and binary compatible.

Premise 4, failure mode 1. Confirmed. `Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Options/TargetedAssemblyReference.cs:22-24` tests `this.TargetRoslynVersion.Equals( RoslynApiVersion.Current.ToVersion() )`, and `Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Extensibility/ExtensionLoaderBase.cs:30-39` filters on `SatisfiesCurrentProcess` and logs nothing about the rejected entries. The declaration pattern is real and documented at `Metalama.Framework/docs/extensibility.md:127-135`, which shows `TargetRoslynVersion="5.10.0"` as a literal. The extension is not saved by an assembly-name mismatch either, because extensions bind to the unsuffixed `Metalama.Framework.Sdk` (`Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Sdk/Metalama.Framework.Sdk.csproj:4` targets `netstandard2.0` with no variant suffix), while only the engine assembly carries the suffix (`Metalama.Framework.Engine.csproj:12`).

Premise 5, failure mode 2. Confirmed. `Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Serialization/ManifestJsonContext.cs:73` adds `new JsonStringEnumConverter()` to the manifest serializer options, and `Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CompileTime/Manifest/TemplateSymbolManifest.cs:31` declares `UsedApiVersion` as `RoslynApiVersion?`, so the member name is written and an unknown name throws on read. The remedy is available: `eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:17` already holds four legacy names, `:31-34` skips generation for them, and `eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Generator.cs:81-96` emits an enum member for every document including the legacy ones, with `Current`, `Lowest` and `Highest` computed separately.

Premise 6, the `CS1014` history. Not corroborated. The three methods that produce `CS1014` for an unknown accessor name are textually identical between `release/dev18.0` and the 5.10 window: `ParseAccessorList` (`LanguageParser.cs:4204-4238` at 5.0, `:4400-4434` at the 5.10 window), `IsPossibleAccessor` (`:4267-4275` and `:4463-4471`) and `ParseAccessorDeclaration` (`:4480-4520` and `:4670-4712`). For the input of the test, the identifier `setx` (`Tests/Aspects/DesignTimeInvalidCode/UnknownAccessorInTemplate.cs:31`), all three versions take the `!accessorName.IsMissing` branch and add the error on that identifier. The baselines do differ (`UnknownAccessorInTemplate.t.cs:2` reports on `setx`, `UnknownAccessorInTemplate_Roslyn5_0.t.cs:2` on an empty span), so the observation is real, but the explanation recorded at `Directory.Packages.md:215` and repeated by the finding, that Roslyn 5.0 and Roslyn 5.10 report the error on different spans, is not supported by the parser source.

Premise 6b, whether 5.12 moves the diagnostic. `IsPossibleAccessor` was rewritten on `main` (`LanguageParser.cs:4445-4489`) and `ParseModifiers( accMods, forAccessors: true, ... )` became `ParseAccessorModifiers( accMods )` (`:4388`, `:4397`). For `setx` the outcome is unchanged: no modifier parses, the token is an `IdentifierToken`, `IsPossibleAccessor` returns true at `:4483-4485`, and the error lands on the identifier at `:4406-4408`. Template compiler, modifier path. The code generator emits, for every grammar field of a node, `Argument(this.Transform(node.<Field>))` (eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Generator.cs:514). The `Modifiers` field is declared as `SyntaxList<SyntaxToken>` with no `<Kind>` children (eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Syntax-5.10.0.xml:626, 634, 652, 675, 1151), so the emitted call binds to the `Transform( SyntaxTokenList list )` overload, which maps every token through `Transform( SyntaxToken )` (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Templating/MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:180-204, in particular the per-token projection at :203). `Transform( SyntaxToken )` falls through its `switch` for any keyword token and emits a factory call whose kind argument is produced by `Transform( SyntaxKind )` (MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:269-294, in particular :274 and :288-293). `Transform( SyntaxKind kind ) => this.MetaSyntaxFactory.Kind( kind )` (MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:137) and `Kind` builds the member access `SyntaxKind.<kind.ToString()>` at run time (MetaSyntaxRewriter.MetaSyntaxFactoryImpl.cs:78-82). No grammar entry, no generated visitor and no version check is involved: the generated `RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier` only guards version-specific node types, version-specific fields, and version-specific kinds of a single `SyntaxToken` field through `node.<Field>.Kind()` (Generator.cs:118-156), and `ClosedKeyword` appears nowhere in Syntax-5.10.0.xml (only `UnionKeyword`, at line 1959).

Reachability of the modifier path. The template compiler is never invoked on a type declaration. Every call site passes a method declaration, an accessor declaration or a variable declarator (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CompileTime/CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter.cs:864-866, :957-960, :1303-1305). The `closed` modifier is a type-declaration modifier, so it cannot occur in a template body.

Patterns. `VisitIsPatternExpression` derives the scope from the left expression and propagates it to the pattern (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Templating/TemplateAnnotator.cs:1533-1555, decision at :1535-1537). `VisitSwitchStatement` derives `switchScope` from the annotated governing expression and propagates it to labels and statements (TemplateAnnotator.cs:2877-2945, decision at :2879-2895). `VisitDeclarationPattern` (TemplateAnnotator.cs:1508-1531) and `VisitCasePatternSwitchLabel` (TemplateAnnotator.cs:2954-2964) use existing pattern nodes only.

The compile-time trees are created with `new CSharpParseOptions( languageVersion, ... )` (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:349-354), where `languageVersion` comes from `ILanguageVersionProvider.GetCompileTimeLanguageVersion()` (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:279), which caps at `LanguageVersion.CSharp14` for a .NET SDK of major version 10 or higher and then takes the minimum with the project language version (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Utilities/LanguageVersionProvider.cs:45-70). Before emitting, `TryEmit` writes each compile-time tree to disk and reparses it from its text with those same parse options (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:515-528), so a construct that the C# 14 parser does not accept produces a parse diagnostic there rather than depending on a symbol-level feature check. corrections.what_happens_today: The `Modifiers` field is declared in the grammar as `SyntaxList<SyntaxToken>` with no `<Kind>` children (eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Syntax-5.10.0.xml:626), and the generated call `this.Transform(node.Modifiers)` (Generator.cs:514) binds to the `Transform( SyntaxTokenList list )` overload, which transforms the list token by token (MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:180-204). `Transform( SyntaxToken )` emits `SyntaxFactory.Token(SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword)` for any keyword token, the kind being produced by name at run time from `kind.ToString()` (MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:274 and :288-293; MetaSyntaxRewriter.MetaSyntaxFactoryImpl.cs:78-82). No grammar entry and no version check is involved, and `ClosedKeyword` appears nowhere in the grammar. The path is in any case unreachable for `closed`: the template compiler is invoked only on method declarations, accessor declarations and variable declarators (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter.cs:864, :957, :1303), never on a type declaration, and `closed` is a type-declaration modifier. A `switch` or an `is` over a union value uses existing pattern nodes, and the annotator derives the scope from the switched expression (TemplateAnnotator.cs:1533-1555 and :2877-2945). In compile-time scope a `closed` compile-time class is copied with its modifiers unchanged into the compile-time compilation (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter.cs:669-696), whose parse options carry the compile-time language version, which is capped at C# 14 until TP-8 (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:279 and :349-354; LanguageVersionProvider.cs:45-70). Before emitting, every compile-time tree is written to disk and reparsed from its text with those parse options (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:515-528), so no assumption about symbol-level modifier checks in Roslyn is needed: a C# 14 parse of `closed class` fails there. notes:
The central claim is supported: the `closed` modifier and patterns over union types require no change to the template compiler, and the proposed change of "none" stands. Three details are corrected or strengthened.

First, the type name. The grammar declares `Modifiers` as `SyntaxList<SyntaxToken>` (Syntax-5.10.0.xml:626), but the generated C# property is a `SyntaxTokenList`, so the emitted `this.Transform(node.Modifiers)` binds to the overload at MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:180, not to the generic `Transform<T>( SyntaxList<T> )` at :207. Both overloads project element by element, so the conclusion is unaffected.

Second, and more substantially, the templating path described in the finding is not merely unaffected by `closed`, it is unreachable. The template compiler is only ever called on a method declaration, an accessor declaration or a variable declarator (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter.cs:864, :957, :1303). A type-declaration modifier cannot appear in a template body, so no `ClosedKeyword` token can reach `Transform( SyntaxToken )`. This makes the "no impact" conclusion stronger than the finding's own reasoning. It also removes a latent concern: `MetaSyntaxFactoryImpl.Kind` builds the kind expression from `kind.ToString()`, so an enumeration value unknown to the running Roslyn would produce invalid text such as `SyntaxKind.8453`; because the path is unreachable, this cannot occur.

Third, the finding marks the compile-time compilation consequence as an assumption about where Roslyn performs modifier feature checks, and rates it "plausible". That assumption is not needed. `TryEmit` writes each compile-time syntax tree to disk and reparses it from its text with the compile-time parse options before calling `Emit` (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:515-528). A compile-time compilation pinned at C# 14 therefore reparses `closed class` under C# 14, and the feature is gated at C# 15, so an error is produced at parse time whatever Roslyn does at the symbol level. The failure then reports LAMA0222 plus the underlying C# errors (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:643-647). The consequence class as written, "No impact (templating); diagnostic reported (compile-time compilation) until TP-8", is correct and can be rated verified rather than plausible.

One boundary worth recording, because it is not part of this finding but bounds when the compile-time case can occur at all. For a `closed` compile-time class to reach the compile-time compilation, the run-time compilation must already parse it, which requires C# 15 in the user project. `TransformCompileTimeType` first reports every error that the run-time semantic model produces over the type's span and aborts with `ErrorsInSourceCode` (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter.cs:461-495), so if the run-time language version is too low the user sees the run-time C# error instead, and the compile-time error is never reached. Both outcomes are diagnostics, not crashes and not silence.

No assertion or exception was found on this path. `Transform( SyntaxToken )` has no exhaustive `switch` over modifier kinds, and the generated version checker inspects only version-specific nodes, fields and single-token field kinds, none of which cover the `Modifiers` list.

No test pins the behaviour, which is expected: no `closed` or union support exists in the repository yet.

The evidence is a single Roslyn commit, "Add C# 15 language version (#84799)" of 2026-08-11, which added `LanguageVersion.CSharp15`, moved the six feature checks from `Preview` to `CSharp15` and removed the experimental markers; it lands after the 5.10 window that contains the consumed build (08-roslyn-api-delta.md line 17). Everything the finding says about `@LanguageVersion(15.0)` and about `ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER` is therefore true of a future Roslyn 5.12 and false of the Roslyn consumed today. One consequence is worth stating separately, because it is a silent failure rather than a build error: a test annotated `@LanguageVersion(15.0)` before the Roslyn move does not fail, it is reported as skipped in both variants, so an author could commit a C# 15 test suite that asserts nothing and see a green run. Two further points were checked and did not change the verdict. The claim that a `net11.0` leg changes nothing because the language version is decided by `LangVersion` and by the engine holds for these projects, because they set `LangVersion` explicitly from `LangMaxVersion`; the general statement that the .NET 11 SDK implies `LangVersion` 15.0 for a `net11.0` project could not be verified here, because no `LangVersion` inference was found in Microsoft.NET.Sdk.targets, Microsoft.NET.Sdk.CSharp.props or Microsoft.NET.Sdk.BeforeCommon.targets on dotnet/sdk main, and it is not load-bearing for this finding. The open question of the finding, whether the Patterns aspect tests need a `RequiredConstants` gate, has no external premise and was not re-examined.

notes: The central claim holds end to end: the experimental members are stripped before generation, the generated overrides hash only the remaining fields and never call the base visitor, the untouched node types fall through to a node-depth DefaultVisit that ignores tokens, and an equal hash short-circuits the change detection with no diagnostic, assertion or trace. The consequence class is accurate: for a compile-time file the undetected change means the pipeline is not paused and the stale compile-time project keeps serving results; for a run-time file the cached aspect results for that tree are reused. The claim that for run-time code only the union identifier case applies is a slight simplification: the run-time skip covers only BlockSyntax, ArrowExpressionClauseSyntax and EqualsValueClauseSyntax (Generator.cs:714-722), so a with element or unsafe expression outside those three positions (for example in an attribute argument) would also be hashed through DefaultVisit, but DefaultVisit still visits its child nodes and the only missed information is the kind of the keyword token, so no additional practical case results. The verdict is corrected rather than confirmed because the proposed test addition cannot be written against the current DefaultParseOptions and must be guarded for the 5.0.0 test variant, neither of which the finding mentions. The behaviour of CSharpSyntaxWalker.DefaultVisit at SyntaxWalkerDepth.Node (child nodes visited, tokens not) is Roslyn behaviour that could not be read from the repository.

The central claim and the consequence class survive verification. No Premium or core leg runs on the .NET 11 software development kit, the baseline includes it, and the platform check stays silent on it because `MaximumSdkVersion` is 11.0, so a load failure of the merged licensing task would indeed reach a user first.

Three details are wrong and one open question is answerable.

1. The statement that every standalone project targets `net10.0` is inaccurate. The two `Issue32827` projects target `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`. The report already records this in its own non-findings section, so the finding contradicts itself.

2. The proposed change names the `MsbuildSolution` entries as part of a .NET 11 leg. Those entries run the desktop `MSBuild.exe`, located through `FindMSBuildExeUsingVsWhere` in PostSharp.Engineering.BuildTools, whose `MSBuildRuntimeType` is `Full`. `Metalama.Licensing.targets:13` then selects `tasks/net472`, so those legs cannot exercise the `net10.0` task on any software development kit. Only the `ManyDotNetSolutions` entry can, because it runs `dotnet build`.

3. The proposed change assumes that the core decision is still open. It is not. The core repository documents that the software development kit dimension is delegated to `metalama/Metalama.Tests.DotNetSdk`, and it excludes `net11.0` from its own scenario matrix for want of targeting packs on the agents, under issue #1884. A `global.json` per scenario plus a container component is therefore a departure from the recorded decision rather than an application of it.

4. The open question is answerable from the PostSharp.Engineering.BuildTools assemblies of versions 2023.2.420 and 2023.2.423 present in this environment: the preferred-version catalogue holds `V_6_0`, `V_8_0`, `V_9_0` and `V_10_0` only, so it carries no .NET 11 entry, but `DotNetComponent` takes a version string, which the core repository already passes directly for 10.0.400. The catalogue is therefore not a blocker.

Where the decision is made: TemplateCompiler.TemplateLanguageVersion is ILanguageVersionProvider.GetCompileTimeLanguageVersion() (TemplateCompiler.cs:51), overridden by MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion when set and contained in SupportedCSharpVersions.All (:58-79). LanguageVersionProvider returns the minimum of the SDK-derived version (>= 10 => CSharp14, :54-60) and the project's LangVersion (:62-71); on the msbuild.exe path it uses GetMaxLanguageVersion of the bundled Roslyn (:111). The same value is the MaximalAcceptableLanguageVersion of the verifier (TemplateCompiler.cs:106) and the parse-option version of the compile-time compilation (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:349-353, :360, :425-432).

How the constant is tested: as the finding states, with one correction. The default parse options of every aspect test are read at BaseTestRunner.cs:218, not :216. CompileTimeCompilationBuilderTests.TemplateLanguageVersion (:1915-1966) pins C# 13 explicitly, so it does not observe a change of Latest. The .t.cs files that pin the supported list are Tests/Aspects/LanguageVersion/LanguageVersionPreview.t.cs:2 (LAMA0051) and Tests/Aspects/Misc/LanguageVersion.t.cs:2 (LAMA0052).

What must change to accept C# 15: the six items of the finding are correct, but item (1) understates the reason and the scope. LanguageVersion.CSharp15 is absent not only from Roslyn 5.0 but also from the Roslyn build that the latest variant consumes, 5.10.0-1.26365.3, and from the highest stable Roslyn on nuget.org, 5.9.0 (FACTS.md:54). AllLanguageVersions.CSharp15 = (LanguageVersion) 1500 is therefore required for both variants, not only for the lower one, and LanguageVersionProvider.cs:56 must use that constant as well, because it names LanguageVersion.CSharp14 directly today.

The variant problem is consequently not a variant problem alone but a Roslyn-version prerequisite. Setting Latest to 1500 gives an unknown language version to every parse in both variants, not only in the 5.0.0 one: DefaultParseOptions (:50) feeds every aspect test (BaseTestRunner.cs:218), every linker and unit test, RunTimeAssemblyRewriter.cs:88 and UserCodeInvoker.cs:422, and Latest is also the fallback of MSBuildProjectOptions.LanguageVersion (:167-181), of DefaultProjectOptions.LanguageVersion (:127), of LanguageOptions.Default (:30) and of CompilationContext (:181). notes:
The central claim holds. Every file and line cited exists and says what the finding says it says, and I could not refute the mechanism: the language-version plumbing does stop at C# 14 in the six places named, FormatSupportedVersions does call ToDisplayStringSafe over every member of All so that adding an unmapped version throws on the LAMA0051 and LAMA0052 paths, the two .t.cs files do pin the literal list of supported versions, and commit 08d065a9 does show that the previous branch expressed exactly this situation with a preprocessor branch that the current doctrine now excludes.

The verdict is "corrected" rather than "confirmed" for three reasons. First, the finding attributes the missing LanguageVersion.CSharp15 member to Roslyn 5.0 alone; the addendum of FACTS.md (:54) establishes that the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 build and the highest stable Roslyn on nuget.org both lack it, so the change is blocked on the move to Roslyn 5.12 and not merely complicated by the lower variant. That reframes the recommended run-time derivation of Latest: it is still the better form, but it is not a solution to the problem the finding describes, only a containment of it. Second, the finding's remark that @LanguageVersion(15.0) skips the test on the 5.0.0 variant is true of the mechanism and misleading about the effect, because today the directive skips on both variants and a new C# 15 suite would report success while running nothing. Third, the consequence class omits the larger of the two consequences, namely that Latest is the fallback language version of six further sites and the parse-option version of the whole test suite, so an unrecognised value does not stay confined to the diagnostic paths.

Minor citation defects, all corrected in the "where" field: BaseTestRunner.cs is :218 and not :216; the finding asserts that the template language version becomes the verifier's MaximalAcceptableLanguageVersion and the compile-time parse option without citing TemplateCompiler.cs:106 or CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:360; and the doctrine it proposes to amend is stated in six places rather than the two it names.

One claim I could not settle from this repository, and which the finding correctly records as an open question: whether CSharpParseOptions on a Roslyn that does not know the value rejects (LanguageVersion) 1500 with a diagnostic or accepts it silently. Answering it requires the Roslyn assemblies, which I did not run or inspect here.

evidence:
Shape of the node. `Syntax-5.10window.xml:1874-1880` and `Syntax-main.xml:1874-1880` both declare `<Node Name="WithElementSyntax" Base="CollectionElementSyntax">` with exactly two fields, `WithKeyword` of type `SyntaxToken` and `ArgumentList` of type `ArgumentListSyntax`. `Syntax-main.xml:1862` declares `<AbstractNode Name="CollectionElementSyntax" Base="CSharpSyntaxNode" />`. The node therefore has no `ExpressionSyntax` child and is not itself an `ExpressionSyntax`, as the finding states.

Shape of the Roslyn base visitor, which the finding marked as an assumption. In the generated Roslyn source for the consumed 5.10 preview, `Syntax.xml.Main.Generated.5.10.cs:1528` declares `public partial class CSharpSyntaxRewriter : CSharpSyntaxVisitor<SyntaxNode?>` and `:1747-1749` contains `[Experimental(...UrlFormat = "https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/82210")] public override SyntaxNode? VisitWithElement(WithElementSyntax node) => node.Update(VisitToken(node.WithKeyword), (ArgumentListSyntax?)Visit(node.ArgumentList) ?? throw new ArgumentNullException("argumentList"));`. The cast of the result of `Visit(node.ArgumentList)` to `ArgumentListSyntax` is present in the base implementation exactly as the finding assumed. The same method exists on the main branch at `Syntax.xml.Main.Generated.cs:1744-1745`, without the `[Experimental]` attribute. `CSharpSyntaxVisitor<TResult>.VisitWithElement` (`Syntax.xml.Main.Generated.cs:237`) and `CSharpSyntaxWalker.VisitWithElement` (`:991`) both delegate to `DefaultVisit`, so the rewriter override is the only one that performs a cast.

Absence of a generated override in Metalama. `eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Syntax-5.10.0.xml:816` carries `ExperimentalUrl="https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/82210"` on `WithElementSyntax`, and a search of the repository for `VisitWithElement`, `WithElementSyntax` and `TransformWithElement` in `.cs` and `.xml` files returns that one line and nothing else. The generated `MetaSyntaxRewriter` therefore contains no `VisitWithElement`, so the Roslyn base implementation runs, which is the premise the crash depends on.

Availability of the factory used after regeneration. `Syntax.xml.Main.Generated.5.10.cs:3493` declares `public static WithElementSyntax WithElement(SyntaxToken withKeyword, ArgumentListSyntax argumentList)` and `:3502-3503` declares `public static WithElementSyntax WithElement(ArgumentListSyntax? argumentList = default)`. `SyntaxKind.cs:410` shows `WithKeyword = 8442`, a pre-existing kind, and `:948` shows the new `WithElement = 9081`; the token kind the regenerated `TransformWithElement` would pass to `Transform(SyntaxToken)` is therefore not new. The `Transform(ArgumentListSyntax?)` overload that the finding names exists at `Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Templating/MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:171-173`.

Language semantics of the element. `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/csharplang/main/proposals/csharp-15.0/collection-expression-arguments.md` gives the grammar `collection_element : expression_element | spread_element | with_element` and `with_element : 'with' argument_list`, states that a compile-time error is reported when the element is not the first element of the collection expression, permits an empty argument list, and disallows the element for arrays and spans. `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Metalama/ccf204f4-b0b3-5fe6-a8de-fe20f6791d2c/scratchpad/impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:131-137` reports the same grammar, the champion issue dotnet/csharplang#8887, the tracking issue dotnet/roslyn#80613 and the error numbers CS9354 to CS9359. The element therefore occurs only inside a collection expression, which is the only place the finding claims it occurs.

Language version gating. `MessageID-5.10.cs:497-503` places `IDS_FeatureCollectionExpressionArguments` in the group that returns `LanguageVersion.Preview`; `MessageID-main.cs:500-507` places it in the group that returns `LanguageVersion.CSharp15`. `LanguageVersion-main.cs:283` declares `CSharp15 = 1500`, and a search for `CSharp15` in `LanguageVersion-5.10.cs` returns nothing. This matches the addendum of FACTS.md (lines 54-56).
notes:
Every external premise of TP-4 holds, and the one the finding itself rated only "plausible" is now verified from the Roslyn generated source rather than assumed.

Confidence upgrade rather than a correction. The finding says "assumption on the shape of the Roslyn base visitor" and rates its confidence "plausible (the base visitor cast)". The base implementation is `node.Update(VisitToken(node.WithKeyword), (ArgumentListSyntax?)Visit(node.ArgumentList) ?? throw new ArgumentNullException("argumentList"))` (Syntax.xml.Main.Generated.5.10.cs:1747-1749), so the cast is real and the confidence field may be raised to "verified" for that clause as well. The failure mode is exactly the one the finding describes: the base method casts, and it casts to `ArgumentListSyntax`, which is the type the transforming `VisitArgumentList` does not return.

Two precisions that do not change the finding.

First, reachability today has a precondition the finding does not state. In the consumed build 5.10.0-1.26365.3 and in the stable 5.9.0, `IDS_FeatureCollectionExpressionArguments` requires `LanguageVersion.Preview` (MessageID-5.10.cs:497-503), and `LanguageVersion.CSharp15` does not exist there. A `with(...)` element therefore parses into a user compilation only under `LangVersion=preview`, which `Metalama.Framework.targets` leaves untouched (FACTS.md line 22) and which `CompileTimeAspectPipeline.VerifyLanguageVersion` accepts when `AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures` is set (FACTS.md line 21). The crash described in "what happens today" is thus reachable today, but only on that configuration; after the move to the stable Roslyn it becomes reachable on any project compiled as C# 15, because `MessageID-main.cs:500-507` gates the feature on `LanguageVersion.CSharp15`.

Second, the version at which "after regeneration" occurs. The finding does not name a Roslyn version, so the addendum's correction of "5.11" to 5.12 (FACTS.md lines 48-49) does not touch it. It is worth recording that the two changes the finding depends on arrive together: the removal of the `ExperimentalUrl` marker on `WithElementSyntax` (present at Syntax-5.10window.xml:1874, absent at Syntax-main.xml:1874), which makes the generator emit `VisitWithElement` and `TransformWithElement`, and the addition of `LanguageVersion.CSharp15` (LanguageVersion-main.cs:283, added 2026-08-11 per FACTS.md line 54), which is what a test annotated `@LanguageVersion(15.0)` needs. The proposed test is therefore feasible at the same moment the regeneration is, which is what "once the stable grammar is consumed" in the proposed change already implies. That test will also need `SupportedCSharpVersions` to admit C# 15, which is the subject of the language-version findings rather than of TP-4.

One observation offered to the code lens rather than asserted here. `Transform<T>` (MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:106-139) has a second failure path for this node: when `GetTransformationKind(node)` is not `Transform`, the switch at lines 120-133 tests for `ExpressionSyntax`, `ArgumentSyntax` and `StatementSyntax`, and a `WithElementSyntax` matches none of them, because `CollectionElementSyntax` derives from `CSharpSyntaxNode` (Syntax-main.xml:1862). The default arm throws `AssertionFailedException`. Whether that path is reachable depends on the scope the annotator assigns, which is the code lens's question. The wrapping the finding describes is correct in either case: `SyntaxProcessingException.ShouldWrapException` (SyntaxProcessingException.cs:27-29) excludes only `SyntaxProcessingException`, `OperationCanceledException` and `TaskCanceledException`, and requires a source tree file path, which a user template has.

evidence:
Confirmed premises.

1. A union declaration produces TypeKind.Struct. scratchpad/roslyn/DeclarationKind.cs declares `DeclarationKind.Union` and maps `SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration` to it; scratchpad/roslyn/EnumConversions.cs:35-38 maps `DeclarationKind.Struct`, `DeclarationKind.Union` and `DeclarationKind.RecordStruct` to `TypeKind.Struct`. No `TypeKind` value is added: `grep TypeKind scratchpad/api/main_Core_Unshipped.txt scratchpad/api/510_Core_Unshipped.txt` returns nothing, and scratchpad/impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:94 records `TypeKind` at 16 values with `Extension = 14` as the highest.

2. A union declaration is not a record. scratchpad/roslyn/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:1038-1052 defines `IsRecord` and `IsRecordStruct` as `Declarations[0].Kind == DeclarationKind.Record` and `== DeclarationKind.RecordStruct`, and :1054-1060 defines `IsUnionDeclaration` as `Declarations[0].Kind is DeclarationKind.Union`, so all three are mutually exclusive. The proposal resolves the point explicitly: scratchpad/unions.md:861-872, "A union declaration is a plain struct, not record struct. The ```record union ...``` isn't supported".

3. The `ref` modifier is forbidden and `readonly` is allowed but not implied. scratchpad/roslyn/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:340-345: `case TypeKind.Struct:` grants `Partial | ReadOnly | Unsafe | Safe`, then `if (!this.IsRecordStruct && !this.IsUnionDeclaration) allowedModifiers |= DeclarationModifiers.Ref;`. `IsReadOnly` is `HasFlag(DeclarationModifiers.ReadOnly)` at :890, so `readonly` is only ever the declared modifier.

notes:
The finding is a preamble that carries no consequence of its own, and every load-bearing external premise holds: a union declaration is a non-record struct with `TypeKind.Struct`, no new `TypeKind` value exists, `ref` is forbidden and `readonly` is neither implied nor forbidden, the instance-field and public one-parameter-constructor restrictions are as described, and case types are ordinary types in the declaration's parameter list rather than a new kind of declaration. Three corrections are needed and the finding survives all of them.

The first is the one that matters for the sub-findings. The statement "exposes `ITypeSymbol.IsUnion` and `UnionCaseTypes`" is placed under "what happens today" but is sourced from Roslyn main. Per the FACTS addendum, main is 5.12 and the consumed build is the 5.10.0-1.26365.3 preview of 2026-07-15, in which `IsUnion` is experimental and `UnionCaseTypes` has no public counterpart at all. Any sub-finding that proposes reading either member is proposing work that depends on the move to Roslyn 5.12, and the member must in any case be gated to the latest variant because the Roslyn 5.0 variant that serves Rider has neither.

The second is a scoping correction. The finding's title says "a union declaration", which is correct, but its prose then says "a union is an ordinary non-record struct to every aspect". The proposal recognises any class or struct carrying `[Union]` as a union type, and Roslyn keeps `IsUnionDeclaration` and `IsUnionType` apart, so a union type may be a class or a record and the parameter-list statement does not apply to it. The distinction matters if a sub-finding proposes surfacing `IsUnion` in the code model, because that flag will be true for types that are not structs.

The third is that the preamble understates the restrictions. The prohibition on instance fields is stated by Roslyn's own diagnostic as covering auto-properties and field-like events, and there is a fourth restriction the finding does not mention: every explicitly declared constructor in a union declaration must chain through a `this(...)` initializer (CS9375). Both bear directly on what an aspect can introduce into a union.

One open item from the API delta report is now closed: report line 272 recorded that the shape of the entries in `UnionDeclarationSyntax.ParameterList` had not been verified. `LanguageParser.ParseParenthesizedParameterList(forExtensionOrUnion: true)` parses each entry with `identifierIsOptional: true` and requires at least one entry, so a case type is a `ParameterSyntax` carrying a type and, normally, no identifier.

I did not verify the Metalama-side premises beyond reading the two cited members of `SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs`, which match the finding: the `TypeKind` switch has no arm that a union could reach other than `Struct`, and `IsRecord` is a direct read of `NamedTypeSymbol.IsRecord`.

A `partial union` reports IsPartial == false, because SourceNamedTypeImpl.IsPartial switches on SyntaxKind.IsTypeDeclaration (CodeModel/Source/SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:344) and the kind list at Utilities/Roslyn/SyntaxKindExtensions.cs:33-35 omits UnionDeclaration, so the switch falls to `_ => default` and the modifier test at line 351 returns false. As a result the design-time generator reports LAMA0048 TypeNotPartial (Pipeline/DesignTime/DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs:158-163) and IntroduceMemberAdvice.ValidateBuilder reports CannotIntroducePartialMemberToNonPartialType (AdviceImpl/Introduction/IntroduceMemberAdvice.cs:217-223) for partial members introduced into a union. Both diagnostics are wrong, because the union is in fact partial. The other sites are latent, in the sense that they are guarded by the earlier failure described in LK-1.

Supporting detail, corrected against the Roslyn sources.

The symbol shape of a union is now established and no longer an open question. Roslyn synthesizes no primary constructor symbol for a union (scratchpad/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:4952-4977). It synthesizes one `SynthesizedUnionCtor` per case type; that class derives from `SynthesizedInstanceConstructor` and therefore from `SynthesizedMethodSymbol`, whose `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` is empty (scratchpad/SynthesizedUnionCtor.cs:14, scratchpad/SynthesizedMethodSymbol.cs:21-27). It also synthesizes the `Value` property as a `SynthesizedUnionValuePropertySymbol`, constructed with the union `TypeDeclarationSyntax`, so its `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` is that union declaration (scratchpad/SynthesizedUnionValuePropertySymbol.cs:13-41, scratchpad/SourcePropertySymbolBase.cs:110 and 559-563).

Consequently `IsPrimaryConstructor` (Utilities/Roslyn/SymbolExtensions.cs:283-291) returns false for a union case constructor because the declaration syntax is null, not because the kind test fails. The conclusion that LinkerLateTransformationRegistry.cs:143-160 and 181-197 are unreachable for a union therefore still holds. If those methods were reached, `Enumerable.Single` would throw InvalidOperationException for no matching element, not an AssertionFailedException, because the union declaration fails the kind half of the predicate rather than the ParameterList half.

`Linking/SymbolExtensions.GetDeclarationFlags` reaches its default `throw new AssertionFailedException` (line 63) for the union `Value` property and its getter, whose primary declaration syntax is the union declaration, and not for the case constructors, whose primary declaration syntax is null and which take the `case null: return default;` branch at lines 59-60.

`ImplicitLastOverrideReferenceInliner.GetInliningAnalysisInfo` is reachable for both. Lines 22-29 fall back to the containing type's primary declaration syntax when the symbol has none, which for a union case constructor substitutes the union declaration, so the kind test at line 72 fails and the throw at line 73 is taken in either case.

The claim that the union-synthesized members are ineligible for override is only half correct. The `Value` property is indeed excluded, because OverrideFieldOrPropertyOrIndexerAdviceRule requires MustBeExplicitlyDeclared (EligibilityRuleFactory.cs:88) and the symbol reports IsImplicitlyDeclared. The case constructors are not excluded: OverrideConstructorAdviceRule (EligibilityRuleFactory.cs:51-56) requires only MustNotBeRecordCopyConstructor and the declaring-type rule at lines 39-49, which admits TypeKind.Struct, and a union is a struct. LinkerRecordHelper.GetSynthesizedMethodOverrideTargets (line 45) filters on a record declaration kind and would therefore silently omit such a constructor rather than crash. The record kind switches consequently do need attention if union case constructors are to be overridable, contrary to the earlier statement that they need no change.

The HasModifier detail is wrong in its stated consequence. `ModifierHelper.GetTypeSyntaxModifierList` (CodeModel/Helpers/ModifierHelper.cs:198) contains no Unsafe branch; the Unsafe branch that calls HasModifier is in GetMemberSyntaxModifierList (line 178), which is used for methods, constructors, properties, indexers, events and fields. `SymbolModifiersHelper.GetSyntaxModifierList` (Utilities/Roslyn/SymbolModifiersHelper.cs:16-40) throws for SymbolKind.NamedType. No code path propagates `unsafe` from a named-type declaration through HasModifier, for a union or for any other type kind, so the omission of UnionDeclaration from the HasModifier kind list has no effect on type declarations. It remains correct for members declared inside a union with ordinary member syntax.
corrections.proposed_change:
Replace the kind lists by `node is TypeDeclarationSyntax` tests wherever the intent is a declaration that can contain members: the callers of SyntaxKindExtensions.IsTypeDeclaration (in particular SourceNamedTypeImpl.IsPartial at line 344, which is the site that produces today's wrong diagnostics), FindSymbolDeclaringNode, GetDeclaringType and Linking.SymbolExtensions.GetDeclarationFlags. Note that IsBaseTypeDeclaration (SyntaxKindExtensions.cs:41) is defined in terms of IsTypeDeclaration and must keep working, and that GetDeclaringType already requires `node is TypeDeclarationSyntax` in its when clause, so the kind list there is redundant and can simply be deleted.

Keep the record-only kind lists for the record-synthesized-member logic, but treat LinkerRecordHelper.GetSynthesizedMethodOverrideTargets (line 45) as in scope rather than out of scope, because union case constructors are eligible for OverrideConstructor advice and are implicitly declared with no syntax of their own.

IsPrimaryConstructor must exclude unions, because the union ParameterList holds case types and not primary constructor parameters. Do not exclude RecordDeclarationSyntax: records do have primary constructors, IsPrimaryConstructor returns true for them today, and PrimaryConstructorTests pins that behaviour. The workable test is `declarationSyntax is TypeDeclarationSyntax { ParameterList: not null } && declarationSyntax.RawKind != 9082`, where 9082 is SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration. In practice the exclusion is defensive only, since a union case constructor has no declaring syntax at all and already fails the test.

The numeric RawKind comparison cannot be retired when the experimental attribute is removed. Per the FACTS.md addendum the next stable Roslyn is 5.12, not 5.10, and SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration does not exist at all in the Roslyn 5.0.0 variant that serves Rider (scratchpad/syntaxkind-50.cs). Naming the constant would therefore break the 5.0.0 build regardless of the experimental marker. The numeric literal, with a comment naming the constant it stands for, is needed until the 5.0.0 variant is dropped, or the site must be gated by a ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER conditional.

notes:
The central claim is supported by the code and the verdict is "corrected" rather than "confirmed" because three substantive details are wrong.

First and most important, the proposed fix for IsPrimaryConstructor contains a clause, `and not RecordDeclarationSyntax`, that would regress records. Record primary constructors are recognized today through exactly this method, and three unit tests assert the resulting behaviour. Applying the proposal as written would fail the build.

Second, the open question is answerable from the Roslyn sources already downloaded in the scratchpad, and the answer splits the two synthesized member families. Union case constructors have no declaring syntax, so GetDeclarationFlags is safe for them; the union Value property does report the union declaration, so GetDeclarationFlags is not safe for it. Separately, ImplicitLastOverrideReferenceInliner has a null fallback to the containing type's syntax that was not noticed, and that fallback makes its throw reachable for both families.

Third, the eligibility argument used to dismiss the record kind switches applies to properties, events and methods but not to constructors, so those switches are not as clearly out of scope as stated.

The "5.10" naming in the proposal contradicts the FACTS.md addendum, and the reason given for the numeric RawKind workaround is incomplete: the workaround is required by the Roslyn 5.0.0 variant, not by the experimental attribute.

Sizing at M still looks right, and possibly light, given that IsTypeDeclaration is a public member of a public static class in Metalama.Framework.Engine and has eight call sites.

evidence:
Confirmed premises.

1. C# 15 is language version 1500 and its display string is "15.0". On dotnet/roslyn main, `CSharp15 = 1500` (scratchpad/roslyn/LanguageVersion.main.cs:283), `IsValid` accepts it (:308-329), `ToDisplayString` returns "15.0" (:414, case at :452), `TryParse` accepts "15" and "15.0" (:470, :582), `MapSpecifiedToEffectiveVersion` returns `CSharp15` for `Default`, `Latest` and `LatestMajor` (:594-601) and `CurrentVersion` is `CSharp15` (:607). Proposed change (4), the `(LanguageVersion) 1500 => "15.0"` case in `LanguageVersionExtensions.ToDisplayStringSafe` (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Utilities/Roslyn/LanguageVersionExtensions.cs:33-39, whose current highest case is `(LanguageVersion) 1400 => "14.0"`), matches Roslyn's own string exactly.

2. Roslyn 5.0 has no `LanguageVersion.CSharp15`. On branch release/dev18.0 the highest member is `CSharp14 = 1400` (scratchpad/roslyn/LanguageVersion.dev18.0.cs:268), `IsValid` has no case for 1500 (:293-318), `TryParse` stops at "14"/"14.0" (:450, :556-562) and `MapSpecifiedToEffectiveVersion` maps `Default`/`Latest`/`LatestMajor` to `CSharp14` (:569-580). The numeric-cast workaround of `AllLanguageVersions` (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Utilities/AllLanguageVersions.cs:14-18) is therefore required, as the finding states.

3. The five csharplang proposals named in the theme exist under proposals/csharp-15.0/ (HTTP 200 for unions.md, closed-hierarchies.md, labeled-break-continue.md, collection-expression-arguments.md, extension-indexers.md).

Premises that need correction.

4. The consumed latest variant cannot accept C# 15 either. `LanguageVersion.CSharp15` was added by dotnet/roslyn#84799 on 2026-08-11, after the consumed build `5.10.0-1.26365.3` (a main build of 2026-07-15) and after the stable 5.9.0 (FACTS.md:54-56; impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:17, :78). In the consumed build and in 5.9.0, the six C# 15 features are gated on `LanguageVersion.Preview` and `Default`/`Latest`/`LatestMajor` map to `CSharp14` (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:16, :78). The finding's "variant problem" is therefore not confined to the 5.0.0 variant: today both variants reject 1500.

5. The version numbers "RoslynApiMinVersion is 5.10" and `@RequiredConstant(ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER)` are wrong. nuget.org serves stable Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 5.0.0, 5.3.0, 5.6.0 and 5.9.0 only; main is versioned 5.12 and the next stable is expected to be 5.12 (FACTS.md:48-49; 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:15, :18). Roslyn 5.10 is precisely the window that lacks `CSharp15`, so 5.10 is the wrong gate both by numbering and by capability. The addendum records that the move to the stable Roslyn is a renumbering of the latest variant to 5.12.0 (FACTS.md:49), which also renames the aspect-test constant.

6. Open question 2 is answered, and neither branch as phrased is correct. `CSharpParseOptions.WithLanguageVersion` does not validate: it stores the value and calls `MapSpecifiedToEffectiveVersion`, whose default arm returns the version unchanged (scratchpad/roslyn/CSharpParseOptions.dev18.0.cs:99-108; LanguageVersion.dev18.0.cs:569-580). The value is rejected later, as a compiler diagnostic: `CSharpParseOptions.ValidateOptions` adds `ErrorCode.ERR_BadLanguageVersion` when `IsValid()` is false (CSharpParseOptions.dev18.0.cs:247-255), whose message is "Provided language version is unsupported or invalid: '{0}'" (release/dev18.0 src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/CSharpResources.resx), formatted with `LanguageVersion.ToString()`, that is "1500". Feature checks compare `MessageID.RequiredVersion() > version`, so with 1500 every C# 14 feature is enabled and no C# 15 syntax is parsed, because the 5.0 parser has no such grammar. A C# 15 compile-time assembly in a Roslyn 5.0 host therefore fails with a diagnostic, not with an exception and not silently.

7. A consequence for the test plan. `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse("15.0")` returns false on Roslyn 5.0 (LanguageVersion.dev18.0.cs:556-562) and equally on the consumed 5.10 preview, because `LanguageVersion.cs` received no commit between 2025-08-07 and 2026-08-11 (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:17). `TestOptions.cs:681-699` then sets `SkipReason` rather than throwing, so `@LanguageVersion(15.0)` aspect tests would be skipped on every variant, not only on the 5.0.0 one, until the latest variant is Roslyn 5.12.

8. The SDK premise is an anticipation, not a verified fact. That the .NET 11 SDK defaults a net11.0 project to C# 15 follows from Roslyn main mapping `Default` to `CSharp15` (LanguageVersion.main.cs:594-601) and from FACTS.md:22, but which Roslyn the .NET 11 general-availability SDK carries is not published; the only data point is the tag NET-SDK-11.0.100-preview.5.26302.115 of 2026-06-01, whose eng/Versions.props says 5.8.0 (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:268). The `>= 11 => CSharp15` arm of `LanguageVersionProvider.cs:54-60` is therefore correct only once that SDK's compiler is known to have `CSharp15`.

The finding survives all of this: every work item it lists is still required, and its recommended derivation of `Latest` from `RoslynApiVersion.Current.ToLanguageVersion()` is still the right shape (SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:31-32, :36-42, :50, :52-62). Only the gating version and the assumption that the currently consumed Roslyn can host the change are wrong.

evidence: What happens today, verified end to end. Roslyn adds DeclarationModifiers.Abstract to a source class that carries the Closed modifier (scratchpad SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:401-403, in the `case TypeKind.Class` arm, which also covers record classes), and an explicit `abstract` on a closed class is an error (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:380-381). A closed class read from metadata also reports IsAbstract, because the flag is emitted and read back: PENamedTypeSymbol.cs:2137-2145 reads TypeAttributes.Abstract, and Roslyn's ClosedClassesTests.cs:1180-1192 asserts `classC2.IsAbstract` on a closed class loaded through a MetadataReference. In Metalama, IsAbstract is a direct read of Symbol.IsAbstract (SourceMemberOrNamedType.cs:36-44) and IsSealed of Symbol.IsSealed (:23), so IsAbstract is true and IsSealed is false. CanBeInherited is `IsReferenceType && !IsSealed` (SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:44), therefore true. HasDefaultConstructor requires `IsAbstract: false` for a class (SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:175-178), therefore false. MustNotBeAbstract tests `!member.IsAbstract` (EligibilityExtensions.cs:740-743), therefore rejects the type. No member named IsClosed, GetClosedDerivedTypeInfo or ClosedKeyword exists anywhere under Metalama.Framework/src (grep on 2026-09-03 returned nothing), so no diagnostic, assertion or crash is involved: the consequence class "No impact" holds. The Roslyn API side: ITypeSymbol.IsClosed and GetClosedDerivedTypeInfo exist in the consumed 5.10 build but are marked [RSEXPERIMENTAL006] (scratchpad api/510_Core_Unshipped.txt:7-8; ClosedDerivedTypeInfo at :3-6; ITypeSymbol.cs:163-172), and are absent from Roslyn 5.0. Derived-type index: for a full compilation the index is built from every type of compilation.Assembly.GetTypes() (PartialCompilation.cs:449-459, AnalyzeType at DerivedTypeIndex.Builder.cs:58-96), so every subtype declared in the current assembly is recorded. For a design-time partial compilation, GetClosure (PartialCompilation.cs:358-445) indexes only the types declared in the input syntax trees plus their base types and interfaces (AddTypeRecursive at :385-430), so a subtype declared in another file of the same project is not in the index. DirectOnly and All filter to types of the current compilation (DerivedTypeIndex.cs:74-93, :117-127); IncludingExternalTypesDangerous does not (:98-103), and its documentation already warns that only declared or attribute-used types and their base types are indexed (DerivedTypesOptions.cs:41-44). The behaviour of the options is pinned by Metalama.Framework.Tests.UnitTests/CodeModel/DerivedTypesTests.cs:34-53. Variant policy: eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.5.10.0.props:8-10 and Roslyn.5.0.0.props:8-11 state that no production source branches on ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER. Implementations that would need the new member: SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:36, the facade SourceNamedType.cs:30 (see the IsRecord pattern at :514-520), IntroducedNamedType.cs:28 (:200), IntroducedExtensionBlock.cs:31 (:190) and NamedTypeBuilder.cs:30 (:36).

The read of ITypeSymbol.IsClosed cannot be written as a direct member access: the member does not exist in Roslyn 5.0, so the Roslyn.5.0.0 variant would not compile, and the policy in eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.5.10.0.props:8-10 forbids production `#if ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER`; in the Roslyn.5.10.0 variant the member is marked [Experimental("RSEXPERIMENTAL006")] (api/510_Core_Unshipped.txt:8), so the reference also needs a `#pragma warning disable RSEXPERIMENTAL006` or a NoWarn entry, which Directory.Build.props:9 does not provide today. The finding therefore depends on the cross-theme gating decision of the report (reflection shim, numeric access or lifting the `#if` policy) and cannot be implemented in isolation. Mention in the DerivedTypesOptions documentation that, for a closed type declared in the current assembly and in a full compilation, DirectOnly returns the complete set of direct subtypes, because the full-compilation index is built from every type of the assembly (PartialCompilation.cs:449-459). Do not state this for design time: the partial-compilation index built by GetClosure (PartialCompilation.cs:358-445) contains only the types declared in the input syntax trees and their base types, so a subtype declared in another file of the same project is absent and DirectOnly is not exhaustive there. For a closed type declared in a referenced assembly, the subtypes live in that assembly and are indexed only when they are base types of indexed types, so GetClosedDerivedTypeInfo (also RSEXPERIMENTAL006, api/510_Core_Unshipped.txt:3-7) would be the only complete source; it is worth considering only for that case and only in the latest variant.

notes: The central claim is confirmed: the code model has no IsClosed, and every derived property (IsAbstract, IsSealed, CanBeInherited, HasDefaultConstructor, MustNotBeAbstract) has the value the finding states, with no diagnostic, assertion or crash involved. Two details of the proposed change were wrong or incomplete. corrections.what_happens_today: Metalama.Framework.props:33 sets MaximumSdkVersion to 11.0, and :39 documents the intent as the supported SDK versions being 10.0 and 11.0, that is, major.minor lines. Metalama.Framework.targets:399 computes _MetalamaSdkVersion as $(NETCoreSdkVersion) with the prerelease suffix removed, for example 11.0.100, and Metalama.Framework.targets:411-413 reports LAMA0601 when $([MSBuild]::VersionGreaterThan($(_MetalamaSdkVersion), %(_MetalamaPlatformRequirement.MaximumSdkVersion))) is true. With the .NET 10 SDK the comparison 10.0.400 against 11.0 is false and nothing is reported. With the .NET 11 SDK the comparison is 11.0.100 against 11.0. The conclusion does not depend on which version parser MSBuild uses: under the SimpleVersion semantics, in which absent components are zero, 11.0 is 11.0.0.0 and 11.0.100 is greater; under the System.Version semantics, in which absent components are -1, 11.0.100 is also greater. There is no plausible comparer under which a version compares equal to its own prefix, so the diagnostic is reported for every .NET 11 SDK. The target framework rule does not have this problem, because $(TargetFrameworkVersion) is v11.0 and Metalama.Framework.targets:322 trims it to 11.0, which is neither greater nor less than the maximum. The minimum rules are safe for the same reason, because 10.0.400 is not less than 10.0. Two secondary observations. First, the prerelease strip at line 399 is not required by the comparison functions, which ignore a prerelease suffix themselves, but it does feed nothing else and is harmless. Second, the resulting message contradicts itself, because the SupportedSdkVersionsDescription sentence appended at line 413 states that the supported .NET SDK versions are 10.0 and 11.0 while the first sentence states that the .NET SDK 11.0.100 is not supported.
corrections.consequence_class: Diagnostic reported. Every user building with a .NET 11 SDK, which the baseline places in the supported set, gets the warning LAMA0601 "'Metalama.Framework' does not support the .NET SDK 11.0.100, which is newer than 11.0. Check whether a newer version of 'Metalama.Framework' is available. The supported .NET SDK versions are 10.0 and 11.0." It is a Warning task, so an ordinary build continues, but the warning becomes an error in any project that sets TreatWarningsAsErrors, and the target is hooked before _CheckForInvalidConfigurationAndPlatform (Metalama.Framework.targets:392) so that it also appears in design-time builds. It is reported once per project, because the target runs for the first target framework only.
corrections.proposed_change: Compare the .NET SDK against MaximumSdkVersion on major.minor only, but do so in the maximum rule alone. Truncating _MetalamaSdkVersion itself at Metalama.Framework.targets:399 would also change the minimum rule at :406-408, which shares that property, and would remove feature-band precision from MinimumSdkVersion, a piece of documented requirement metadata that a contributing package may legitimately set to a value such as 10.0.200; this repository itself pins a feature band, 10.0.400 at eng/src/Program.cs:26. Introduce a second property, for example _MetalamaSdkVersionMajorMinor computed as the first two components of $(NETCoreSdkVersion), and use it in the condition at :412 only, with a comment stating that MaximumSdkVersion names the last supported major.minor line. Writing 11.0.99999 in the props file is the alternative, and it is worse, because it leaves the same trap for every requirement contributed by another package. Add a regression scenario that pins the boundary. The smallest form is a fifth requirement in the existing Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Standalone/SupportedPlatform.ContributedRequirements project, for example Test.CurrentSdk, whose MaximumSdkVersion is computed from the running SDK as $(NETCoreSdkVersion.Split('.')[0]).$(NETCoreSdkVersion.Split('.')[1]) so that the scenario stays valid when the agent SDK moves, with "warning LAMA0601.*'Test[.]CurrentSdk'" added to the ForbiddenDiagnosticsRegexes of its test.json. A hardcoded major.minor would have to be revised each time eng/src/Program.cs:26 moves to a new line. The existing Test.LegacySdk requirement (SupportedPlatform.ContributedRequirements.csproj:39-41) uses 1.0 and cannot catch the boundary.

notes:
The central claim is supported by the code and holds under every plausible version-comparison semantics, so the "verify with one dotnet build first" caveat of the original confidence note can be relaxed to a confirmation rather than a precondition. No .NET SDK or MSBuild is installed in this container (no dotnet on PATH and no Microsoft.Build.dll on disk), and the task forbids building, so the comparison was not executed; the argument instead shows that both candidate parsers, MSBuild's SimpleVersion with zero-filled components and System.Version with -1 components, make 11.0.100 greater than 11.0.

Three corrections. First, a citation error: the Test.LegacySdk requirement is at SupportedPlatform.ContributedRequirements.csproj:39-41, with MaximumSdkVersion 1.0 on line 40, not at :41-43. Second, the consequence is a warning that a project with TreatWarningsAsErrors turns into an error and that also surfaces in design-time builds, which the original text did not state. Third, and most substantive, the first option of the proposed change is not minimal as written: truncating _MetalamaSdkVersion at Metalama.Framework.targets:399 also feeds the MinimumSdkVersion rule at :406-408, so it would silently drop feature-band precision from a documented piece of requirement metadata. The truncation belongs in the maximum comparison only.

Two further observations that do not change the verdict. The same off-by-one-line-of-versions hazard exists for MaximumNETFrameworkVersion at Metalama.Framework.targets:340-342, because $(TargetFrameworkVersion) for .NET Framework carries three components, for example 4.7.2; the current baseline sets no MaximumNETFrameworkVersion, so nothing is reported today, but a contributed requirement that sets it to 4.8 would warn on net481. And the message produced by the maximum rule contradicts the SupportedSdkVersionsDescription sentence it appends, which is independent evidence that 11.0 was written as a major.minor line rather than as a full version.

Roslyn's generated CSharpSyntaxVisitor.VisitUnionDeclaration and CSharpSyntaxVisitor<TResult>.VisitUnionDeclaration call DefaultVisit, and CSharpSyntaxRewriter declares its own override of VisitUnionDeclaration that calls node.Update on the visited children without going through DefaultVisit. notes:
The finding survives. Every premise that carries it is true: UnionDeclarationSyntax exists as a TypeDeclarationSyntax with the exact field shape of StructDeclarationSyntax, the visitors inherit a VisitUnionDeclaration they do not override, and the type-level logic they run for classes, structs and records is therefore skipped for a union. Three corrections are needed.

First, the stated mechanism is right only for walkers. The finding attributes the descent to DefaultVisit in all cases, but CSharpSyntaxRewriter has its own generated override, and the plain CSharpSyntaxVisitor and CSharpSyntaxVisitor<TResult> do not descend at all. This matters because three of the twenty listed classes are of the non-descending kind, and for them the consequence is a null or empty result for the whole union subtree rather than a partially handled one. That is a stronger failure than the finding describes, not a weaker one.

Second, the proposed change understates the constraint. Suppressing the experimental diagnostic is not sufficient, because the Roslyn 5.0.0 variant has no such API at all; the overrides need per-variant conditional compilation, which no production file uses today. Conversely, the suppression itself is temporary: the Roslyn version that the 2027.0 baseline actually targets no longer marks the API experimental.

Third, "the same helper as VisitStructDeclaration" is safe for identity, attributes, modifiers and members, but not for ParameterList, which on a union carries the case types as identifier-less ParameterSyntax entries.

Two bounding observations that do not affect the verdict. A union symbol has TypeKind.Struct, so the twelve TypeKind switches with a throwing default arm are not reached, and the failure stays silent as the finding says. And the consequence cannot be observed until the language-version plumbing accepts C# 15: today Metalama.Framework.targets rewrites a LangVersion of 15.0 to 12.0 with a warning (FACTS.md:22), and no Roslyn that Metalama consumes exposes C# 15 as a non-preview language version (FACTS.md:56), so this work is ordered after the language-version and Roslyn-variant changes of theme 01.

corrections.what_happens_today:
Three corrections to the external premises, none of which removes the mechanism the finding describes.

First, the trigger is not "the stable 5.10 package". No stable Roslyn 5.10, 5.11 or 5.12 package exists on nuget.org; the published stable versions of Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp are 5.0.0, 5.3.0, 5.6.0 and 5.9.0, dotnet/roslyn main is versioned 5.12, and the November 2026 baseline is expected to carry Roslyn 5.12. What removes the experimental markers is a single Roslyn commit, "Add C# 15 language version (#84799)" of 2026-08-11, which lands inside the 5.11 window. Regeneration therefore starts to emit code as soon as the consumed Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp build is later than that commit, whether that build is a prerelease of the roslyn-consolidated feed or a stable package. In practice the step is the renumbering of the latest variant from 5.10.0 to 5.12.0 described in updating-roslyn.md step 7 and step 8, with the grammar added as a new file Syntax-5.12.0.xml (step 4 forbids renaming the previous file) and the version name changed in GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:17-18.

Second, UnsafeExpressionSyntax does not un-strip. On dotnet/roslyn main today, Syntax.xml carries exactly one ExperimentalUrl, on UnsafeExpressionSyntax, and every UnsafeExpressionSyntax entry of the public API file keeps the [RSEXPERIMENTAL006] prefix; MessageID.RequiredVersion returns LanguageVersion.Preview for IDS_FeatureUnsafeEvolution. Of the five stripped declarations of Syntax-5.10.0.xml (three node types and two fields, not four declarations), only four un-strip: UnionDeclarationSyntax, WithElementSyntax and the Name field of BreakStatementSyntax and of ContinueStatementSyntax. Every mention of VisitUnsafeExpression, TransformUnsafeExpression, a MetaSyntaxFactoryImpl.UnsafeExpression method, a PartialUpdate for UnsafeExpressionSyntax and a hasher visit for UnsafeExpression must be removed from the list of what regeneration produces. This also answers the open question of the finding: the answer is that UnsafeExpressionSyntax stays experimental, so TP-5 remains in force after regeneration.

Third, the statement that RoslynApiVersion.g.cs is unchanged holds only under the refuted assumption that the identity stays 5.10.0. The enum is generated from the version-name list of GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:17-18 (Generator.cs:64-98), so the renumbering replaces V5_10_0 by V5_12_0 and changes the Current and Highest members, and the three hand-written references in SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:60, :85 and :142 change with it. The generated-code directory moves from Metalama.Framework/.generated/5.10.0 to .generated/5.12.0, which updating-roslyn.md step 10 already covers.

The premises that survive unchanged are the ones that carry the finding: the experimental markers are compile errors on any reference from generated code, which is the stated reason for the stripping in TreeReader.cs:25-42 and is not suppressed anywhere in the repository; the four-argument SyntaxFactory.BreakStatement and ContinueStatement overloads, the four-parameter Update, the twelve-parameter SyntaxFactory.UnionDeclaration and the WithElement factories all exist in the un-marked public API; and the two mismatch scenarios remain real, namely that updating the package without the grammar generates nothing and that updating the grammar without the package fails the build of the latest variant with RSEXPERIMENTAL006.
corrections.consequence_class: Build error when the grammar file and the consumed Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp build are not moved together, in either direction. When they are moved together the regeneration is not without effect: the generated RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier gains overrides that report the version-specific-node diagnostic for a union declaration, a with-element and a labeled break or continue used in a template, and the generated MetaSyntaxRewriter, MetaSyntaxFactoryImpl, partial-update extensions and code hashers gain the corresponding members. The correct statement is therefore "build error if the two updates are not simultaneous; otherwise a behaviour change confined to the newly generated members", not "otherwise no impact".
corrections.proposed_change:
The check as proposed is unsound in both directions and would have to be reformulated.

It would never pass. UnsafeExpressionSyntax carries ExperimentalUrl in the 5.10 grammar, in the 5.11 grammar and on main, and the Roslyn source comment says the feature stays in preview until C# 16, so a check that fails whenever the grammar file still declares an ExperimentalUrl on a node would fail permanently once the package label is stable.

Its signal is also the wrong one. The presence of a prerelease label on the consumed package version does not track the removal of the markers: the stable 5.9.0 package still has all five markers, while the 5.11 prerelease builds already have only one. The removal is decided by Roslyn commit #84799 of 2026-08-11, not by a package becoming stable.

A sound check compares the local Syntax-<version>.xml with the grammar of the exact Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp build that the latest variant references, declaration by declaration, and fails when a declaration that the local file marks experimental is no longer marked in that build. If comparing against the upstream grammar is not practical in the build, the second-best check is a stored list of the declarations that are knowingly stripped, so that the appearance of a newly stripped declaration, or the disappearance of a listed one, has to be acknowledged explicitly.

The documentation sentence must also be reconciled with what updating-roslyn.md step 4 already says. That step already instructs the reader to keep the experimental nodes in the copied file, so the addition is not a new instruction but a consequence to state: when the new Roslyn removes the marker from a node, the generator starts emitting code for that node in the latest variant only, which changes MetaSyntaxRewriter.g.cs, RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier.g.cs, SyntaxNodePartialUpdateExtensions.g.cs and the two code hashers, and the grammar file and the referenced package must move in the same commit.
corrections.size: S

notes:
Verdict is "corrected" rather than "refuted" because the mechanism of the finding does not depend on the version number or on the identity of the third node: the generator strips on ExperimentalUrl, the stripping ends when the consumed Roslyn drops the marker, and the grammar file and the referenced package must move together or the build fails. All three corrections are to external premises: the non-existence of a stable Roslyn 5.10, the criterion "stable" instead of "later than the 2026-08-11 commit", and the persistence of the experimental marker on UnsafeExpressionSyntax.

Two residual uncertainties, stated as such. The removal of the markers is observed on the main branch and at the 5.11 snapshot; no release branch for Visual Studio 18.12 exists yet, so the claim that the stable 5.12 package will not carry the markers is an inference from the fact that release branches are cut from main, not an observation of a shipped package.
