evidence:
LV-10 contains no premise about C# 15 language semantics, about a csharplang proposal, or about the Roslyn public API. Its external premises are about the target frameworks of csc, about .NET assembly forward compatibility, and about MSBuild and the .NET SDK. Each was checked against the upstream repositories and against nuget.org.

Premise 1, "net10.0;net472, the two frameworks for which csc.exe is built" (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.CompilerExtensions.Resources/Metalama.Framework.CompilerExtensions.Resources.csproj:5-6). CONFIRMED, and it survives the move to the stable Roslyn 5.12. On dotnet/roslyn main, src/Compilers/CSharp/csc/AnyCpu/csc.csproj:5 declares TargetFrameworks as "$(NetRoslynSourceBuild);net472"; eng/targets/TargetFrameworks.props:19-26 sets NetRoslyn and NetRoslynAll to net10.0, and lines 50-58 set NetRoslynSourceBuild to NetRoslynAll for every build that is not source-only. Roslyn 5.12 therefore still builds the .NET Core csc for net10.0. Only the source-only build in the virtual monolithic repository substitutes NetCurrent (TargetFrameworks.props:35-46).

Premise 2, "a host running on .NET 11 still loads the net10.0 flavour". CONFIRMED. This is ordinary .NET forward compatibility, and the repository doctrine states the same conclusion for the compiler payload: Metalama.Framework/docs/platform-support.md:338-339 records that the net10.0 compiler declares rollForward=Major and runs on .NET 11. The direction matters: a net10.0 payload loads into a .NET 11 process, and the converse does not hold. The selection code that the finding cites is unconditional on the runtime version, as claimed: Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Options/TargetedAssemblyReference.cs:19-20 and Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Extensibility/ExtensionLoaderBase.cs:31 both choose net472 when RuntimeInformation.FrameworkDescription starts with ".NET Framework" and net10.0 otherwise.

Premise 3, "Microsoft.Build keeps assembly version 15.1.0.0 across MSBuild releases". CONFIRMED on four release lines of dotnet/msbuild: eng/Versions.props declares AssemblyVersion 15.1.0.0 on branch vs17.14 (line 8, VersionPrefix 17.14.60), on vs18.0 (line 8, VersionPrefix 18.0.34), on vs18.9 (line 9, VersionPrefix 18.9.14) and on main (line 9, VersionPrefix 18.12.0). The comment at eng/Versions.props:80-92 of vs18.0 states that the assembly version is deliberately fixed and that only FileVersion follows the release.

Premise 4, "so the 18.0.2 compile-time reference resolves against the MSBuild of a .NET 11 SDK through the locator" (Directory.Packages.props:35-50). REFUTED as stated, and corrected below. The stable assembly identity settles the compile-time reference only. The MSBuild that a .NET 11 SDK carries is not a net10.0 build. dotnet/msbuild Directory.Build.props sets LatestDotNetCoreForMSBuild to net10.0 on branch vs18.0 (line 28) and on vs18.9 (line 42), to net9.0 on vs17.14 (line 30), and to net11.0 on main (line 41), where eng/Versions.props:6 reads VersionPrefix 18.12.0. The published packages agree: Microsoft.Build 18.0.2, 18.6.3 and 18.9.6 on nuget.org each carry exactly lib/net10.0 and lib/net472. dotnet/sdk main is the .NET 11 SDK (eng/Versions.props:6-8: VersionMajor 11, VersionMinor 0, VersionSDKMinor 1) and pins Microsoft.Build to 18.12.0-1.26452.110 (eng/Version.Details.xml:31). A process built for net10.0 and running on the .NET 10 runtime therefore cannot load the MSBuild of a .NET 11 SDK.

The repository does not attempt that load, which is why the finding survives. Both locator hosts filter the candidate software development kits by runtime major version: /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Workspaces/MSBuildInitializer.cs:84 keeps only i.ParsedVersion.Major <= Environment.Version.Major, and /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Metalama.DesignTime.HostSimulator/MSBuildEnvironment.cs:50 keeps only sdk.Version.Major <= Environment.Version.Major. When no candidate remains, MSBuildInitializer.cs:90-94 throws MSBuildInitializationException with a message that names the incompatibility. The affected projects state the rule themselves: Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Workspaces/Metalama.Framework.Workspaces.csproj:4-5 and :18, Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Metalama.DesignTime.HostSimulator/Metalama.DesignTime.HostSimulator.csproj:4-6, and eng/src/DesignTimeSolution.cs:38-42.

Roslyn version timeline, cross-check. The addendum of FACTS.md places the November 2026 baseline at Roslyn 5.12 and Visual Studio 18.12. The MSBuild and SDK evidence agrees: MSBuild 18.12 is the version that the .NET 11 SDK consumes, and dotnet/msbuild main carries a package validation baseline of 18.11.0-1.26426.2, whose Arcade date stamp is 2026-08-26.

corrections.what_happens_today: The finding groups the MSBuild sites with the payload literals and explains them by the stable assembly identity of Microsoft.Build. That explanation is incomplete. The assembly version 15.1.0.0 is indeed frozen across releases (dotnet/msbuild eng/Versions.props on branches vs17.14, vs18.0, vs18.9 and main), so the compile-time reference to 18.0.2 binds against any later MSBuild. What the identity does not settle is the runtime. MSBuild 18.0 through 18.9 are built for net10.0 and MSBuild 18.12, the version that the .NET 11 SDK consumes, is built for net11.0 (dotnet/msbuild Directory.Build.props:41 on main, versus :28 on vs18.0 and :42 on vs18.9; dotnet/sdk eng/Version.Details.xml:31). A net10.0 host process running on the .NET 10 runtime cannot load it. The two locator hosts in this repository do not fail with an assembly-load error, because both restrict the candidate software development kits to a major version at or below the running runtime (MSBuildInitializer.cs:84, MSBuildEnvironment.cs:50); when nothing qualifies, MSBuildInitializer.cs:90-94 throws a diagnostic exception. The consequence is that these two sites are pinned to the .NET software development kit generation rather than to the embedded payload flavour, and that on a machine carrying only the .NET 11 SDK, Metalama.Framework.Workspaces and the LinqPad driver find no usable MSBuild, although platform-support.md:196-197 admits the .NET 11 SDK into the supported set.
corrections.proposed_change: Keep the consequence class of the finding, and correct two statements in its text. First, replace the sentence about assembly version 15.1.0.0 with: the assembly version of Microsoft.Build is frozen at 15.1.0.0, so the compile-time reference to 18.0.2 binds against any later MSBuild; the constraint that remains is the runtime, because the MSBuild of a .NET 11 SDK is built for net11.0 and a net10.0 host process cannot load it. Second, split the site list: the payload literals (the CompilerExtensions projects, TargetedAssemblyReference.cs, ExtensionLoaderBase.cs, the extension property files) move only if the embedded Core flavour moves, whereas Metalama.Framework.Workspaces.csproj:18, Metalama.DesignTime.HostSimulator.csproj:6, eng/src/DesignTimeSolution.cs:42 and MicrosoftBuildVersion move together with the dotNetSdkVersion pin of eng/src/Program.cs. Record as an open question whether Metalama.Framework.Workspaces must gain a net11.0 asset for a user machine that carries only the .NET 11 SDK, since platform-support.md:196-197 places that SDK inside PB-2027.0.
corrections.consequence_class: No impact for 2027.0, conditional on the build staying pinned to a .NET 10 SDK. A residual user-facing consequence exists on a machine that carries only the .NET 11 SDK, and it belongs in the open questions rather than under "No impact".

notes:
The finding survives. Every literal it lists is internally consistent, and none of them must change for 2027.0.

Three remarks on the boundary of this verification. First, the stable Roslyn 5.12 does not disturb the CompilerExtensions premise: Roslyn main still builds the .NET Core csc for net10.0, so the pair net10.0 and net472 remains the pair for which csc is built. Second, the direction of .NET compatibility is what makes the payload sites safe, and it is the reverse of the MSBuild case: a net10.0 payload loads into a .NET 11 process, while a net11.0 MSBuild does not load into a net10.0 process. The finding treats both as the same kind of statement. Third, whether Metalama.Framework.Workspaces needs a net11.0 asset is a design decision for the platform baseline and may already belong to another finding of this analysis; I record it as a consequence of the corrected premise and do not claim it as a defect of LV-10 itself.

Not verified in this session, and stated as an assumption: the exact MSBuild version that the released .NET 11 SDK will carry. The evidence is dotnet/sdk main at version 11.0.1xx pinning Microsoft.Build 18.12.0-1.26452.110, which is a preview pin that can still move within the 18.12 line. It cannot move back to a net10.0 MSBuild without dotnet/msbuild main reverting LatestDotNetCoreForMSBuild.

evidence:
The finding contains no premise about C# 15 semantics, about a csharplang proposal, or about the Roslyn compiler public API. Its external premises concern the Roslyn version timeline, the layout of the Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild package, MSBuild and the .NET SDK. Each was tested.

1. Roslyn version timeline. The finding names "Roslyn 5.10" as a shipping version four times. The nuget.org flat container index for Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild ends at 5.9.0 (fetched https://api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer/microsoft.codeanalysis.workspaces.msbuild/index.json, 2026-09-04: 5.0.0, 5.3.0, 5.6.0, 5.9.0 and no 5.10, 5.11 or 5.12). The addendum of FACTS.md:48-49 states that dotnet/roslyn main carries MinorVersion 12 and that the November 2026 baseline is expected to be Roslyn 5.12, the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 being a main build with no stable counterpart. "Roslyn 5.10" is therefore the name of the consumed prerelease, not of a shipping version.

2. The package layout premise survives the renumbering. The 5.9.0 package downloaded from nuget.org contains lib/net10.0 and lib/net472 only, plus contentFiles/any/any/BuildHost-net472 and contentFiles/any/any/BuildHost-netcore. On dotnet/roslyn main, src/Workspaces/MSBuild/Core/Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild.csproj declares <TargetFrameworks>$(NetRoslynSourceBuild);net472</TargetFrameworks>, and eng/targets/TargetFrameworks.props sets NetRoslyn = NetRoslynAll = net10.0 with NetRoslynSourceBuild = $(NetRoslynAll). The library assets will therefore still be net10.0 and net472 in the stable release, so the constraint that keeps Metalama.Framework.Workspaces at net10.0 (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Workspaces/Metalama.Framework.Workspaces.csproj:5-8, :18) is confirmed. The net10.0 asset of Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild 5.9.0 references System.Runtime 10.0.0.0, read from its AssemblyRef table, which confirms that it cannot load on a .NET runtime below 10.

3. The open question about the build host is answered, and the finding states it incorrectly. The build host is not net10.0 and net472. On main, src/Workspaces/MSBuild/BuildHost/Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild.BuildHost.csproj declares <TargetFrameworks>$(NetRoslynBuildHostNetCoreVersion);net472</TargetFrameworks>, and eng/targets/TargetFrameworks.props sets NetRoslynBuildHostNetCoreVersion = net8.0. The runtimeconfig.json extracted from contentFiles/any/any/BuildHost-netcore of the 5.9.0 package reads {"tfm": "net8.0", "framework": {"name": "Microsoft.NETCore.App", "version": "8.0.0"}, "rollForward": "Major"}. The comment quoted from the Core csproj on main says the deployed build host is used so that the process can "potential rollforward to a runtime that supports the SDK version", and the build host csproj adds that "The version targeted is only used for build time, since we use MSBuildLocator to discover the proper version at runtime". The build host therefore does roll forward and selects its own SDK out of process. The csproj lines 5-8 the finding cites describe the library assets, not the build host.

4. The frozen assembly version premise is true and is stronger than the citation supports. Directory.Packages.md:309 asserts the freeze only for Microsoft.Build 17.x. Measured with dnfile on packages downloaded from nuget.org, Microsoft.Build 18.0.2 (lib/net10.0 and lib/net472) and Microsoft.Build 18.9.6 (lib/net10.0) all carry AssemblyVersion 15.1.0.0, and the net10.0 asset of Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild 5.9.0 references Microsoft.Build.Framework at assembly version 15.1.0.0. dotnet/msbuild main eng/Versions.props sets VersionPrefix 18.12.0 and AssemblyVersion 15.1.0.0, with the comment that there is "a fixed AssemblyVersion for compat (15.1.0.0), but varied FileVersion". The November 2026 MSBuild is therefore still an 18.x with the same binding identity, so the 18.0.2 compile-time pin remains loadable. The nuspec of Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild 5.9.0 declares a dependency on Microsoft.Build.Framework 18.0.2, which matches the pin in Directory.Packages.props:35-52.

5. The .NET SDK premise is confirmed in the baseline document. Metalama.Framework/docs/platform-support.md:195-197 reads "The floor is the .NET 10 SDK. The .NET 11 SDK, released in November 2026, is also in the set", and :136-137 says Visual Studio 2027 is expected in November 2026 with .NET 11 and C# 15. The corollary that a machine carrying Visual Studio 2027 alone has only the .NET 11 SDK is not verifiable today, because Visual Studio 2027 is unreleased; platform-support.md:200-203 only records that Visual Studio installs an SDK through the Microsoft.NetCore.Component.SDK component, 10.0.400 for Visual Studio 2026 18.9.

6. The code premise is unaffected. Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Workspaces/MSBuildInitializer.cs:83-84 filters on ParsedVersion.Major <= Environment.Version.Major and :92-94 raises the message the finding quotes, and Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Workspaces/Workspace.cs:283 calls MSBuildInitializer.Initialize before Workspace.cs:303 calls MSBuildWorkspace.Create. The failure therefore occurs in Metalama's own in-process registration, before any Roslyn build host is started, so the roll-forward behaviour of the build host does not remove the failure.

7. LINQPad. www.linqpad.net and forum.linqpad.net are both blocked by the egress proxy, as the finding reports. A web search returned the summary that LINQPad 9 needs .NET 8 or later to start and that scripts can target .NET 6 through .NET 10, with a secondary claim that LINQPad 9 covers .NET 10 and .NET 11. This is a search summary of an unreachable page and is weak evidence, so the open question is only partially answered.

corrections.what_happens_today: MSBuildInitializer lists the SDKs with dotnet --list-sdks and keeps only those whose major version is at most Environment.Version.Major (MSBuildInitializer.cs:83-84), then registers the highest one. The filter is correct for the in-process registration, because the MSBuild assemblies of an SDK target the runtime of that SDK: the net10.0 asset of Microsoft.Build 18.0.2 and the net10.0 asset of Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild 5.9.0 both bind to System.Runtime 10.0.0.0 and cannot load into an older runtime. The Workspaces package is net10.0 only, and the latest Roslyn variant keeps that shape: on dotnet/roslyn main the Workspaces.MSBuild project targets $(NetRoslynSourceBuild);net472 with NetRoslyn equal to net10.0, and the 5.9.0 package on nuget.org ships lib/net10.0 and lib/net472 only. The version named 5.10 in the repository is the consumed prerelease 5.10.0-1.26365.3; the stable that ships with Visual Studio 2027 and the .NET 11 SDK is expected to be Roslyn 5.12 (FACTS.md:48-49), and nuget.org carries no stable above 5.9.0. The LinqPad driver is net10.0-windows and the samples state that LINQPad 9 is required; the only evidence available here about the LINQPad runtime is a web search summary, because linqpad.net and its forum are blocked by the egress proxy, and that summary reports that LINQPad 9 starts on .NET 8 or later and that queries may target .NET 6 through .NET 10. Under PB-2027.0 the .NET 11 SDK is in the supported set (platform-support.md:195-197), and a developer who installs Visual Studio 2027 alone may have the .NET 11 SDK and not the .NET 10 SDK, which is plausible but unverifiable while Visual Studio 2027 is unreleased. On such a machine a .NET 10 host throws MSBuildInitializationException with the message at MSBuildInitializer.cs:92-94, which already names the cause. The failure belongs to Metalama alone: Workspace.cs:283 calls MSBuildInitializer.Initialize before Workspace.cs:303 creates the MSBuildWorkspace, and the Roslyn build host that would load the projects is a separate process targeting net8.0 and net472 whose runtimeconfig.json sets rollForward to Major, so Roslyn itself would roll forward to the .NET 11 runtime and pick a compatible SDK. A .NET 11 host of the net10.0 asset selects the .NET 11 SDK and loads its MSBuild against the Microsoft.Build 18.0.2 compile-time reference, which is declared with ExcludeAssets="runtime" in Metalama.Framework.Workspaces.csproj:61. That works because MSBuild freezes its binding identity: Microsoft.Build 18.0.2 and 18.9.6 both carry AssemblyVersion 15.1.0.0, and dotnet/msbuild main pins AssemblyVersion to 15.1.0.0 while its VersionPrefix is 18.12.0. The pin must not rise, because the .NET 10 SDK remains the lowest host (Directory.Packages.props:35-52).
corrections.proposed_change: Document in the Workspaces and LinqPad READMEs that the host runtime major decides which SDK the in-process MSBuild registration can use and that a .NET 10 host needs a .NET 10 SDK. When recording this, name the Roslyn variant rather than the number 5.10, because the stable is expected to be renumbered 5.12. Consider a net11.0 target for the LinqPad driver only if a LINQPad release hosts .NET 11, which the available sources do not establish. No code change is proposed for the filter. A separate question, outside this finding, is whether the in-process registration is still required at all, given that Roslyn performs the project evaluation in a build host process that selects its own SDK.
corrections.size: S
corrections.consequence_class: Assertion or crash (an exception at workspace load), on a plausible but unverified environment. The environment premise that remains unverified is the default SDK set of Visual Studio 2027; the Roslyn build host premise is now verified and does not contribute to the failure.

notes: Three corrections, none of which removes the finding. First, the version number: "Roslyn 5.10" is the consumed prerelease and not a shipping version, and the stable expected in November 2026 is 5.12; the package shape the finding depends on is unchanged on dotnet/roslyn main, so the finding survives the renumbering. Second, the parenthetical about the build host is wrong: the build host targets net8.0 and net472, not net10.0 and net472, and its shipped runtimeconfig.json sets rollForward to Major, so the open question is answered affirmatively. Because Metalama raises the exception in its own initializer before MSBuildWorkspace.Create runs, this correction changes the explanation but not the outcome. Third, the frozen assembly version premise is true and better supported than the cited line, which speaks only of Microsoft.Build 17.x: 18.0.2, 18.9.6 and main all carry AssemblyVersion 15.1.0.0. One premise remains genuinely unverified, namely that a machine with Visual Studio 2027 alone lacks the .NET 10 SDK, and one is only weakly supported, namely the runtime of LINQPad 9, since linqpad.net and forum.linqpad.net are blocked by the egress proxy. The finding has no premise about C# 15 semantics, about a csharplang proposal, or about the Roslyn compiler public API.

corrections.what_happens_today: `ImmutabilityExtensions.cs:40-58` returns `Deep` for the listed special types and for delegates, enums, pointers and function pointers; `:80-88` returns `Deep` for a non-reference type in the `System` namespace that is not in the exclusion list; `:90-93` returns `Shallow` when `INamedType.IsReadOnly` is true; `:95` returns `None` otherwise. `INamedType.IsReadOnly` is the Roslyn symbol property (`SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:169`), which for a source struct is exactly the declared `readonly` modifier. Roslyn maps a union declaration to `TypeKind.Struct` and allows `readonly` on it without implying it, so a union declared without `readonly` is `ImmutabilityKind.None`. `GraphBuildingContext.cs:74-84` (`IsDeeplyImmutable`) delegates to `GetImmutabilityKind` and returns true whenever the kind is not `None`, so `Shallow` already counts as immutable there. `DependencyGraphBuilder.Visitor.cs:119-129` reports warning `LAMA5161` (`WarningChildrenOfNonInpcFieldsOrPropertiesAreNotObservable`, severity `Warning`, `DiagnosticDescriptors.cs:93-99`) for a stem whose type is neither immutable nor treated as `INotifyPropertyChanged`. In an `[Observable]` class, a computed property that reads `this.Shape.Value` makes `Shape` the stem (`DependencyGraphBuilder.Visitor.cs:238-253`) and reports the warning as if the union could change behind the reference. The compiler forbids every instance field of a union other than the backing field of the synthesized get-only `Value` property, so `Shallow` (or `Deep` when all case types are deeply immutable) is the accurate classification. A union declared `readonly` already avoids the warning today, which is the available workaround.
corrections.proposed_change: In `GetImmutabilityKind`, return at least `Shallow` for union types. Returning `Shallow` is sufficient to remove the warning, because `IsDeeplyImmutable` tests `!= ImmutabilityKind.None` (`GraphBuildingContext.cs:78`). This needs a code model surface for `IsUnion` (theme 03): `ImmutabilityExtensions` is compile-time code compiled by the Roslyn of the host, which is bounded by `RoslynApiMinVersion` 5.0.0 (`Directory.Build.props:11-16`, `Directory.Packages.props:23`), and `Metalama.Patterns.Immutability` has no Roslyn variant multitargeting, so it cannot reference a Roslyn API that exists only in the latest variant, even behind a conditional compilation symbol. The branch must live in `Metalama.Framework.Engine`, which is built per variant. The second half, `Deep` when every case type is deeply immutable, is not implementable against the Roslyn the repository consumes today: `ITypeSymbol.UnionCaseTypes` exists only on Roslyn main (5.12) and is absent from both the 5.10 preview and the stable 5.9 (`scratchpad/ITypeSymbol_510.cs:147-160` against `scratchpad/roslyn/ITypeSymbol.cs:150-158`), so it either waits for the move to the stable Roslyn or derives the case types from the synthesized one-parameter case constructors. Add an aspect test next to the existing classification tests (`tests/Metalama.Patterns.Immutability.AspectTests/ClassificationTests.cs:36`, which prints `GetImmutabilityKind` per type) and an aspect test in `Metalama.Patterns.Observability.AspectTests/Diagnostics` modelled on `ChildPropertyOfNonInpcProperty.cs`, asserting that no `LAMA5161` is reported for a union stem.
corrections.size: M. The change in `GetImmutabilityKind` plus its tests is small once theme 03 exposes `IsUnion`; the theme 03 surface and, for the `Deep` case, the move to a Roslyn that exposes `UnionCaseTypes` are what make it medium.

notes:
The central claim is supported by the code and survived every refutation attempt. Attempts that failed: (1) I checked whether the union type could be diverted earlier in `GetImmutabilityKind`; it is not, because a union is `TypeKind.Struct`, has no `SpecialType`, is an `INamedType`, is not in the `System` namespace and is not `IsReadOnly` unless declared so. (2) I checked whether an implicit `readonly` is applied to unions; `SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:340-346,890` shows `readonly` is merely allowed, and `IsReadOnly` is the declared modifier alone, so the open question of the finding is answered "no" for the July 2026 snapshot and remains open only for the stable compiler. (3) I checked whether the member access chain would be truncated before the stem is validated; it is not, because `Value` is a property and the `TakeWhile` at `DependencyGraphBuilder.Visitor.cs:240-243` accepts properties, so `Shape` is the stem and `Value` the leaf. (4) I checked whether a nullable union property would take a different path; `GetElementaryType` (`RoslynExtensions.cs:100-110`) unwraps `Nullable<T>` and yields the same union type. (5) I checked whether the consequence could be silent or a crash; the descriptor is severity `Warning` and no assertion is on the path.

Details corrected. The cited line ranges were off by one to three lines and omitted the `return ImmutabilityKind.None` at `ImmutabilityExtensions.cs:95` and the descriptor file. The `IsReadOnly` test at `:90` is not restricted to non-`System` value types: a `System` value type in the exclusion list of `:98-103`, such as `ReadOnlySpan`, also falls through to it and is classified `Shallow`. The name `IsDeeplyImmutable` is misleading: it accepts `Shallow`, which is why returning `Shallow` for a union is enough to remove the warning and why a `readonly union` is already free of it today. The `Deep` half of the proposed change rests on `ITypeSymbol.UnionCaseTypes`, which is present only on Roslyn main (5.12) and absent from the consumed 5.10 preview and the stable 5.9, so that half depends on the Roslyn move as well as on theme 03. The reason for the theme 03 dependency is stronger than the finding states: the Patterns packages are not built per Roslyn variant and their compile-time code is compiled by the Roslyn of the host, bounded by `RoslynApiMinVersion` 5.0.0, so conditional compilation is not an available fallback there; only the engine has per-variant builds.

The proposed test project, `Metalama.Patterns.Observability.CompileTimeTests`, exists, but the classification itself belongs to `Metalama.Patterns.Immutability`, whose existing classification tests are aspect tests (`ClassificationTests.cs`, `SystemTypeClassificationTests.cs`). Note also that `Metalama.Patterns.Immutability.csproj` declares `InternalsVisibleTo` for a project `Metalama.Patterns.Immutability.CompileTimeTests` that does not exist under `Metalama.Patterns/src/tests`; that is unrelated to this finding.

The claims about union semantics rest on the Roslyn sources captured in the scratchpad (a July 2026 snapshot), not on the Metalama repository, and Metalama.Compiler is not cloned, so the behaviour of the stable compiler is an assumption.

evidence:
1. `closed` is a class-only modifier and is implicitly abstract. dotnet/roslyn `main`, `src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/Source/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:331-332` adds `DeclarationModifiers.Closed` to `allowedModifiers` only under `case TypeKind.Class: case TypeKind.Submission:` (structs at :341, interfaces at :348 and delegates at :352 do not receive it); `:399-403` adds `DeclarationModifiers.Abstract` for a closed class; `:374-382` reports `ERR_ClosedSealedStatic` for `sealed` or `static` and `ERR_ClosedExplicitlyAbstract` for an explicit `abstract`. Error numbers from `src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Errors/ErrorCode.cs:2489-2493` and `:2507`: `ERR_ClosedTypeNameDisallowed = 9380`, `ERR_ClosedSealedStatic = 9381`, `ERR_ClosedBaseTypeBaseFromOtherAssembly = 9382`, `ERR_UnderspecifiedClosedSubtype = 9383`, `ERR_ClosedExplicitlyAbstract = 9384`, `ERR_ClosedBadDerivedTypesProperty = 9395`; messages in `src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/CSharpResources.resx:8354-8374`, including "'{0}': a closed type cannot be marked abstract because it is always implicitly abstract."
2. The derivation restriction is stated by the proposal on the assembly and again on the module. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/csharplang/main/proposals/csharp-15.0/closed-hierarchies.md: "If a class in one assembly is declared `closed` then it is an error to directly derive from it in another assembly." and "The same restriction applies to modules. A subtype of a `closed` type must be located within the same module as the base type."
3. Subtype discovery is over the source module of the compilation being compiled: `SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:920-923` (`findClosedSubtypes` seeds its stack with `DeclaringCompilation.SourceModule.GlobalNamespace`). A type introduced into the same compilation is therefore included in `CandidateClosedSubtypeDefinitions` and in the synthesized `[IsClosedType(DerivedTypes = ...)]` attribute.
4. Exhaustiveness follows the set of direct derived types: closed-hierarchies.md, "A `switch` expression that handles all of the direct descendants of a closed class will be considered to have exhausted that class."
5. A closed class requires well-known attributes: `SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:1978-1982` calls `Binder.GetWellKnownTypeMember(compilation, WellKnownMember.System_Runtime_CompilerServices_IsClosedTypeAttribute__ctor, diagnostics, location)` and the same for `CompilerFeatureRequiredAttribute__ctor`, both with a diagnostic bag, so a target framework without those types produces a missing-member error. This also confirms the point that the API delta report could not verify (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Metalama/ccf204f4-b0b3-5fe6-a8de-fe20f6791d2c/scratchpad/impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:270).
6. `SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword = 8453` is absent from Roslyn 5.0: `release/dev18.0`, `src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Syntax/SyntaxKind.cs` has no `ClosedKeyword` and its highest contextual keyword is `ExtensionKeyword = 8451`. It is present but experimental in the stable 5.9.0 and in the consumed 5.10 preview: `src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` at commit `35d9211b841e7613c1d2f8f5af6d628ace696c4c`, line 72, reads `[RSEXPERIMENTAL006]Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword = 8453 -> ...`. On `main` the same file, line 73, carries no prefix. The identity of the 5.9.0 and consumed 5.10 public API is established in 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:16 and :90.
7. The experimental marker is a real build gate: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/csharplang/main/proposals/csharp-12.0/experimental-attribute.md states that the diagnostic is "technically a warning, so that the compiler allows suppressing it", but "it is treated as an error for purpose of reporting", suppressed by `#pragma warning disable <DiagnosticId>` or the equivalent compiler option. Under Metalama's continuous integration build every warning is an error in any case (/home/user/Metalama/CLAUDE.md, section "Warnings").
8. No consumed Roslyn exposes C# 15 as a non-preview language version: FACTS.md:54 (LanguageVersion.CSharp15 absent from 5.9.0 and from the consumed 5.10 preview, added to `main` on 2026-08-11) and FACTS.md:48-49 (the next stable package is expected to be 5.12, and the latest variant is to be renumbered to 5.12). Metalama's own plumbing stops at C# 14 (FACTS.md:16-22).

Partial parts do not each need the modifier: `SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:429-459` (`MakeAndCheckTypeModifiers`) iterates `declaration.Declarations` and accumulates `result |= mods`, so `closed` on one part applies to the merged type. This answers the open question at 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:271.
10. where: dotnet/csharplang main proposals/csharp-12.0/experimental-attribute.md (severity of the experimental diagnostic)
corrections.what_happens_today: An aspect cannot introduce a closed class or a union, and neither omission causes a crash. Introducing a class derived from a closed class is permitted, with two precisions. First, the proposal requires the same module and not only the same assembly (closed-hierarchies.md: "The same restriction applies to modules. A subtype of a `closed` type must be located within the same module as the base type."); an introduction always lands in the compilation being transformed, so both conditions hold. Second, the compiler discovers the subtypes by walking DeclaringCompilation.SourceModule.GlobalNamespace (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:920-923), so an introduced derived type is included in the synthesized [IsClosedType(DerivedTypes = ...)] attribute. That inclusion has a semantic consequence that the "No impact" class does not cover: because a switch is exhaustive only when it handles all direct descendants of the closed class, an aspect that introduces a derived type makes a previously exhaustive switch over that base non-exhaustive, and the compiler reports the existing CS8509 and CS8655 diagnostics against the transformed compilation at the user's source location.
corrections.proposed_change: (Optional for 2027.0) Add `bool IsClosed { get; set; }` to INamedTypeBuilder and an IsClosed reader on INamedType, and emit the `closed` modifier in GetTypeSyntaxModifierList, subject to four external constraints. First, gate the emission on the latest Roslyn variant after that variant moves to the stable Roslyn (expected 5.12, per FACTS.md:48-49), not on the 5.10 variant: SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword carries [RSEXPERIMENTAL006] in the stable 5.9.0 and in the consumed 5.10 preview (PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt at 35d9211b, line 72), and naming it there requires an explicit suppression of RSEXPERIMENTAL006, which the continuous integration build would otherwise reject; the prefix is absent on main. Second, gate it on the effective language version being C# 15, which no consumed Roslyn exposes (LanguageVersion.CSharp15 is absent from 5.9.0 and from the consumed preview, FACTS.md:54), so this work depends on the C# 15 enablement and on Metalama.Framework.targets accepting LangVersion 15.0 (FACTS.md:22). Third, make IsClosed mutually exclusive with IsSealed, IsStatic and an explicit IsAbstract in the builder, and suppress the `abstract` token when IsClosed is set, because a closed class is implicitly abstract (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:399-403) and `sealed`, `static` or an explicit `abstract` are CS9381 and CS9384; restrict IsClosed to class declarations, since the modifier is allowed only for TypeKind.Class (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:331-332). Fourth, treat the availability of System.Runtime.CompilerServices.IsClosedTypeAttribute and CompilerFeatureRequiredAttribute in the target framework as an eligibility condition, because the compiler requires both well-known members for a closed type (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:1978-1982), which matters for the Desktop flavour. A generated partial part need not repeat the modifier, because partial declarations combine their modifiers (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:429-459). Union introduction is out of scope for 2027.0.
corrections.size: S for `closed`, but only after the move to the stable Roslyn and the C# 15 enablement; on the consumed 5.10 preview it is not deliverable without suppressing RSEXPERIMENTAL006 and without a C# 15 language version. L for unions.
corrections.consequence_class: No impact for the missing ability to introduce `closed` or `union`. A separate, low-probability semantic consequence exists for the supported case: introducing a class derived from a closed class can turn a previously exhaustive user switch into a non-exhaustive one and produce CS8509 or CS8655 in the transformed compilation.

notes:
Every external premise of the finding holds in substance, so the finding survives; three of them need a correction and one consequence is missing.

Confirmed without change: `closed` adds no syntax node and is only a token in the Modifiers list, so rewriters that update the original declaration preserve it; SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword is 8453 on main and absent in Roslyn 5.0 (release/dev18.0 SyntaxKind.cs stops at ExtensionKeyword = 8451); unions are a new declaration form whose introduction is a large change and reasonably out of scope.

Corrected premise 1: the finding cites the same-assembly rule; closed-hierarchies.md states the assembly rule and then a stricter module rule. The finding's conclusion is unaffected, because an introduction lands in the compilation being transformed.

Corrected premise 2: "gated on the 5.10 variant" understates the gate. ClosedKeyword is [RSEXPERIMENTAL006] in the stable 5.9.0 and in the consumed 5.10 preview, and the marker is removed only from the 5.11 window onwards, so the first stable package that exposes it plainly is expected to be 5.12. Separately, emitting the modifier is only meaningful when the effective language version is C# 15, and LanguageVersion.CSharp15 does not exist in any Roslyn that Metalama consumes today.

Corrected premise 3: the proposed builder property interacts with modifiers that ModifierHelper already emits. A closed class is implicitly abstract, and `abstract`, `sealed` and `static` are errors on it (CS9384, CS9381); the modifier is accepted only on class declarations; and the feature requires the IsClosedTypeAttribute and CompilerFeatureRequiredAttribute well-known members in the target framework.

Missing consequence: because exhaustiveness of a switch over a closed class is computed from its direct descendants in the source module, an aspect that introduces a derived class can invalidate the exhaustiveness of a user switch and produce CS8509 or CS8655 in the transformed compilation. This does not change the "no crash" conclusion but it is not literally "no impact".

By-product: the open question of 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:271, whether a partial declaration of a closed class must repeat `closed`, is answered. MakeAndCheckTypeModifiers accumulates the modifiers of all parts with `result |= mods`, so one part carrying the modifier suffices and the design-time generated partial parts need not repeat it.

Not verified: whether Metalama.Compiler will be based on the stable Roslyn that carries the non-experimental API (Metalama.Compiler is not cloned, FACTS.md:6). The November 2026 date and the 5.12 number are inferences from the release cadence, not published facts (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:268).

evidence:
Union declaration maps to TypeKind.Struct: dotnet/roslyn main, src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/EnumConversions.cs:35-38 maps DeclarationKind.Struct, DeclarationKind.Union and DeclarationKind.RecordStruct to TypeKind.Struct (fetched 2026-09-03). Metalama maps that to its own TypeKind.Struct at Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CodeModel/Source/SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:69-79, reads IsReferenceType from the symbol at :133 and IsRecord from the symbol at :173.

IsRecord is false for a union: dotnet/roslyn main, src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/Source/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:1038-1044 returns declaration.Declarations[0].Kind == DeclarationKind.Record only. The proposal resolves the point explicitly: csharplang proposals/csharp-15.0/unions.md line 872, "A union declaration is a plain struct, not record struct".

The [Union] attribute is added on the emit path only: dotnet/roslyn main, src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/Source/SourceNamedTypeSymbol.cs:1735 declares AddSynthesizedAttributes(PEModuleBuilder moduleBuilder, ref ArrayBuilder<CSharpAttributeData> attributes) and :1866-1876 adds UnionAttribute there when ShouldApplyUnionAttribute() is true, that is when the type is a union declaration and the source did not apply the attribute itself. A union read from metadata does expose the attribute: src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/Metadata/PE/PENamedTypeSymbol.cs:980-1036 filters CaseSensitiveExtensionAttribute, ObsoleteAttribute, IsReadOnlyAttribute, IsByRefLikeAttribute, CompilerFeatureRequiredAttribute, RequiredMemberAttribute and IsClosedTypeAttribute from GetAttributes, and does not filter UnionAttribute. The asymmetry stated by the finding is therefore verified, not merely plausible.

IUnion is part of the declared interface set of the source symbol, not an emit-time addition: dotnet/roslyn main, src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/Source/SourceNamedTypeSymbol_Bases.cs:378-383, case DeclarationKind.Union calls addImplicitlyImplementedInterface with WellKnownType.System_Runtime_CompilerServices_IUnion, in the same switch that adds IEquatable<T> for records. The proposal states the same at unions.md:706-716 and 783-812.

The synthesized members are visible in the compile-time symbol model: dotnet/roslyn main, src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/Source/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:4977-4981 creates SynthesizedUnionValuePropertySymbol and :5044-5049 creates one SynthesizedUnionCtor per case type during member computation.

The rejection of an introduced instance field or auto-property is real: dotnet/roslyn main, src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/Source/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:2084-2091 reports ERR_InstanceFieldInUnion for every non-static field whose associated symbol is not the synthesized Value property; src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Errors/ErrorCode.cs:2478 gives ERR_InstanceFieldInUnion = 9373; src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/CSharpResources.resx:8342-8344 gives the exact text "Instance fields, auto-properties or field-like events are not permitted in a 'union' declaration." Do not add a TypeKind.Union value: the precedent is TypeKind.RecordClass and TypeKind.RecordStruct, both obsolete with the message "TypeKind.Class and INamedType.IsRecord", and a new TypeKind value would need a new arm in every switch over the Metalama TypeKind enum, several of which throw in the default arm (the delta report counts 17 TypeKind switches, 12 with a throwing default arm; the finding's figure of 9 does not match that inventory). Two constraints follow from the Roslyn API timeline and were not in the finding. First, ITypeSymbol.IsUnion exists in the consumed build 5.10.0-1.26365.3 but is marked [RSEXPERIMENTAL006], so referencing it requires suppressing that diagnostic, and it does not exist at all in the Roslyn 5.0.0 variant that serves Rider; the implementation must therefore be gated to the latest Roslyn variant, and the lower variant must return a constant false. Second, ITypeSymbol.UnionCaseTypes does not exist in the consumed build: it was added to the Roslyn public API after the 5.10 window and is present only on main, which becomes the 5.12 stable. notes:
Every external premise of the finding was checked and none is false. Four points required correction or completion.

1. The finding marks the attribute asymmetry as plausible. It is now verified in both directions: the attribute is added only in AddSynthesizedAttributes, which takes a PEModuleBuilder, and the metadata reader filters seven attributes from GetAttributes without filtering UnionAttribute. The contrast with closed classes is worth carrying into the sibling finding: IsClosedTypeAttribute is filtered from the metadata attribute list (PENamedTypeSymbol.cs:1027-1031), so a closed class is invisible in Attributes in both directions, whereas a union is visible in one direction only.

2. The IUnion interface is not an emit-time addition. It is added in the declared base interface computation, in the same switch that adds IEquatable<T> for records, so it is visible in the code model of the current compilation as well. The finding's statement is correct but its reason, "Roslyn adds it implicitly", is worth making precise, because the design-time pipeline sees it too.

3. The first open question is answered. ITypeSymbol.IsUnion is present in the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 build and is marked [RSEXPERIMENTAL006]; ITypeSymbol.UnionCaseTypes is not present there and appears only on main, that is in the future 5.12 stable. Neither member exists in the Roslyn 5.0.0 variant. The proposed change as written, "Implement IsUnion in SourceNamedTypeImpl from ITypeSymbol.IsUnion and UnionCaseTypes mapped through Compilation.Factory.GetIType", is therefore not compilable against the current RoslynApiMaxVersion for the UnionCaseTypes half, and needs an experimental-diagnostic suppression plus variant gating for the IsUnion half. The finding survives this, since it already lists the question as open, but the change grows a dependency on the Roslyn 5.12 move.

4. The scope of the Roslyn predicate is wider than a union declaration. Any class or struct carrying [Union] is treated as a union, so an INamedType.IsUnion implemented from ITypeSymbol.IsUnion will also be true for classes, whose TypeKind is Class and whose IsReferenceType is true. The restriction on instance fields, auto-properties and single-parameter public constructors is checked only for a union declaration (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:2084-2107 tests IsUnionDeclaration); an attribute-based union type is checked for different conditions (:2108-2119, ERR_MissingUnionCaseTypes and ERR_MissingUnionValueProperty). An eligibility rule written as "must not be a union" would therefore be stricter than the compiler for attribute-based unions. The safest rule is to reject introduction of an instance field, auto-property or field-like event when the target is a union declaration, and that distinction is not observable through ITypeSymbol.IsUnion alone; the syntax kind UnionDeclaration or the absence of a user-written [Union] attribute is required to make it.

The second open question, whether the public API should expose the synthesized Value property as a distinguished member, is not settled by any external source. The proposal only requires that a union type expose a public Value property of type object (unions.md:117-127 and 783-812), so the member is discoverable by name and signature; nothing in Roslyn marks it, since SynthesizedUnionValuePropertySymbol is an internal symbol class.

One statement inside the proposed change is not an external premise but does not match the report it cites: the finding says a new TypeKind value would need a new arm in 17 switches, 9 of which throw in the default arm, whereas the inventory in 08-roslyn-api-delta.md gives 17 TypeKind switches with 12 throwing default arms (lines 24 and 198). The corrected proposed change states the inventory figures.

The correction rests on two facts the finding does not report. Value { get; }` property, its getter and its backing field all reach the code model: the property and the getter store a syntax reference to the UnionDeclarationSyntax, so DeclaringSyntaxReferences is non-empty and its kind is SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration. GetPropertyKind finds the backing field, sees the non-empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences and calls HasExplicitAccessorBody, which does not crash: its switch expression matches only PropertyDeclaration, EventDeclaration and IndexerDeclaration and falls into the `_ => false` arm, so Value is classified as PropertyKind.Auto and IsAutoProperty returns true, which is accurate. SourceProperty.cs:115 casts with `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax` and survives. Linking/SymbolExtensions.GetDeclarationFlags switches on the kind of the primary declaration and throws AssertionFailedException at SymbolExtensions.cs:63 for a kind outside its list, so the first linker analysis of Value or of its getter crashes, in the same way that LinkerRecordHelper.cs:45,65 had to special-case RecordDeclaration for the synthesized record members.
corrections.proposed_change: Treat Value like the synthesized record members: add the union declaration kind to the kind list of GetDeclarationFlags and extend LinkerRecordHelper (theme 04). The new kind cannot be named as SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration in shared engine source, because the value does not exist in Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 5.0.0, which compiles the same files through Metalama.Framework.Engine.5.0.0.csproj, and because it is marked with ExperimentalAttribute (RSEXPERIMENTAL006) until Roslyn 5.12; guard the arm with ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER, or use the numeric constant, and revisit once the latest variant is renumbered to 5.12, where the marker is gone and C# 15 is a non-preview language version. Beyond the switch arm, decide and implement what happens when an aspect targets a union at all, because the compiler rejects most of what the pipeline would emit: CS9373 forbids every instance field, auto-property and field-like event other than the backing field of the synthesized Value, CS9374 forbids an explicitly declared public one-parameter constructor, CS9375 requires every declared constructor to chain with a `this` initializer, and the compiler adds Value unconditionally, without the duplicate-signature check it performs for record members, so a Value property emitted into the union declaration collides with the synthesized one. The likely outcome is a diagnostic that rejects the unsupported advice rather than a code path that emits it. Add a code-model unit test that reads Constructors, Properties, IsAutoPropertyOrField and IsImplicitlyDeclared of a union, and remember that the test can only run in the latest Roslyn variant.
corrections.consequence_class: Assertion or crash for an aspect that touches Value or its getter; for the constructors, no crash, but an aspect that introduces a field, an auto-property, a field-like event, a public one-parameter constructor or a constructor without a `this` initializer into a union produces a compiler error in the generated code (CS9373, CS9374, CS9375).
corrections.size: M, shared with theme 04, plus the diagnostics for unsupported advice on a union.

notes:
The finding rests on no premise about C# 15 semantics, the csharplang proposals or the Roslyn public API, so those parts of the brief have nothing to bite on. Its only external premises concern the .NET SDK, plus one indirect Roslyn timeline premise, and the finding survives all of them with three corrections.

First, the .NET 11 SDK exists but is not stable. Only `11.0.100-preview.7` (2026-08-11) is downloadable today; general availability is 2026-11-10. The finding writes as though the supported SDK were installable now.

Second, and more consequential for the value of the proposed leg, the preview .NET 11 SDK carries Microsoft.Net.Compilers.Toolset `5.10.0-1.26363.117`, a build of the same Roslyn 5.10 window as the `5.10.0-1.26365.3` that Metalama consumes. In that window `LanguageVersion.CSharp15` does not exist and `Default`, `Latest` and `LatestMajor` map to C# 14. A .NET 11 leg added before November therefore tests the .NET 11 host runtime and the `net11.0` target framework only, and cannot surface any C# 15 behaviour. This makes the timing of the leg part of the recommendation rather than an implementation detail.

Third, the stated consequence is the weakest part of the finding. MSBuild's task load context performs no target-framework check on a task assembly and accepts framework assemblies at a version greater than or equal to the requested one, which is exactly why a `net10.0` task loads on a .NET 11 MSBuild; the repository's own doctrine already argues from this tolerance when it declines to ship `net11.0` toolset assets. The licensing task is thus a poor justification for the leg. The leg is still worth having, but for the `net11.0` target framework, the .NET 11 host runtime and, after November, the Roslyn 5.12 command-line compiler.

The open question is largely answerable without cloning PostSharp.Engineering: the .NET SDK component takes an arbitrary version string at the Metalama call site, unlike the Visual Studio component, which takes an enumeration member, and prereleases are already permitted, so no catalogue entry gates a .NET 11 SDK.

One incidental inaccuracy outside my lens: the claim that every standalone project targets `net10.0` is contradicted by `src/Tests/Standalone/Issue32827/Test/Test.csproj:4`, which targets `netstandard2.1`. I corrected it in place because it appears in the text I was asked to restate.

The central claim of the finding, that the standalone .NET Core leg is `net10.0` and that this is a coverage gap under a .NET 11 SDK, holds. Three details are wrong.

First, the count. `<TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>` appears 88 times, not 92; the total of 92 is reached only by including four `<TargetFrameworks>net10.0</TargetFrameworks>` declarations. The parenthetical "69 and 7 scenario directories" is correct, and the coincidence that `Standalone` holds both 69 scenario directories and 69 singular declarations may be what produced the confusion.

Second, and most consequentially, the claim that `DefaultLanguageVersion/DotNet` "becomes an early detector of the C# 15 default" is not supported by the code. That project pins `net10.0`, and the implicit language version is a function of the target framework, as both the comment at `Metalama.Framework.targets:115` and the warning text at `:245` state. Its implicit version stays at C# 14.0, which the allow-list at `:118` accepts. The claim also overlooks that the three scenarios which do move to `net11.0` by themselves inherit an explicit `LangVersion` of 14.0 from `Metalama.Framework/Directory.Build.props:46`, so `LangVersionImplicitlySet` is not in play for them at all. Detecting the C# 15 default requires a new scenario that both targets `net11.0` and clears the inherited `LangVersion`.

Third, the proposed change is not workable as written for most of the subset it names. Five of the seven named scenarios are multi-project solutions that mix `net10.0` and `netstandard2.0`; a global `TargetFramework` would be applied to the `netstandard2.0` projects as well and would defeat what those scenarios test. `CompiledBindingsWpf` is `net10.0-windows`, and `SingleFile` has no project file to override.

Two smaller inaccuracies. The title's "run on `net10.0` only" is a simplification: fourteen projects deliberately target `net8.0`, `net9.0`, `net462`, `net472`, `net48` or `net10.0-windows`, and 25 target `netstandard2.0`. And the citation `DotNet.csproj:6` bundles three facts that live on three lines: the stale comment is at line 3, the target framework at line 6, and the `LangVersion` reset at line 11.

Two claims could not be checked in this session and are left as the finding rated them. The semantics of `NETCoreAppMaximumVersion` under a .NET 11 SDK is external to this repository and no SDK is installed in this container. The behaviour of `TestOptions.Properties` is external as well: PostSharp.Engineering is not cloned, no `test.json` in this repository uses `Matrix` or `Properties`, and only the presence of the members could be confirmed, from the strings of the downloaded `PostSharp.Engineering.BuildTools.dll` in the scratchpad. The open question about `ManySolutions` and `dotnet test` therefore stands unanswered.

corrections.what_happens_today: A union declared in a project that contains compile-time code is not classified at all. The effect is wider than the declaration line: because VisitTypeDeclaration is the only place that sets _isInCompileTimeType (TextSpanClassifier.cs:77-111), VisitMember (TextSpanClassifier.cs:163-173) returns without marking and without recursing, so no member of the union is classified either. corrections.proposed_change: The classifier route alone is not sufficient and would introduce a false positive. TemplateAnnotator has no dispatch for unions either, and its default path annotates a type declaration that no override handles with RunTimeOrCompileTime (TemplateAnnotator.cs:446-451), a value the classifier accepts as compile-time (TextSpanClassifier.cs:80-82). Routing every unhandled TypeDeclarationSyntax to VisitTypeDeclaration in the classifier would therefore mark run-time unions, run-time interfaces and extension blocks as compile-time, whereas a run-time class is correctly skipped today because TemplateAnnotator.VisitTypeDeclaration annotates it RunTimeOnly (TemplateAnnotator.cs:773). The classifier helper uses only members of the abstract base (Modifiers, Keyword, OpenBraceToken, CloseBraceToken, ConstraintClauses, Identifier, BaseList, AttributeLists, TypeParameterList), so it compiles unchanged. Because the same route also changes interfaces and extension blocks, the Formatting baselines must be re-adopted; no current baseline contains a declared interface, and a new case should be added to Tests/Formatting/AllDeclarations.cs.
corrections.size: S for the two routes, plus the re-adoption of the Formatting baselines that the interface and extension-block change affects.
corrections.consequence_class: Silent wrong output (cosmetic). Confirmed: no diagnostic and no assertion; SafeSyntaxWalker only wraps exceptions and the union node falls through to the Roslyn default visit.

notes: The central claim holds: there is no union dispatch in TextSpanClassifier, and a union in a project with compile-time code receives no classification. Three details are corrected. First, the scope of the effect: the whole union body loses its classification, not only the declaration header, because _isInCompileTimeType is never set. Second, "design-time only" is inexact: the same classifier output is written by the HTML code writer and asserted by the Formatting aspect tests, which run during a build. Third, and most important, the proposed change is incomplete and would regress: TemplateAnnotator has the same missing dispatch, and its default path annotates an unhandled type declaration RunTimeOrCompileTime, a value the classifier treats as compile-time, so adding the classifier route by itself would highlight run-time unions and run-time interfaces as compile-time. The annotator must be fixed first, or together. The pre-existing interface gap is worth noting on its own: a compile-time interface is not classified today either, by exactly the same mechanism, and no test baseline pins it (no declared interface appears in any .cs.html file in the repository). The confidence caveat of the finding remains valid: reaching this code requires a union to be parsed in a project that Metalama classifies, which the current language-version plumbing makes unlikely in 2027.0.

notes:
Attempts to refute the central claim failed. The claim that nothing in the repository builds or tests under the .NET 11 SDK or against `net11.0` survives a repository-wide grep for `net11.0`, a search for every `global.json`, and an inspection of the Docker scenarios, which pin .NET SDK 10.0.302.

Three details are wrong and are corrected above.

The most consequential is the behaviour matrix. The finding states that scenario (d), a .NET 11 SDK of version `11.0.100` against `MaximumSdkVersion` `11.0`, produces no LAMA0601, and attributes that conclusion to the reading that `[MSBuild]::VersionGreaterThan` pads missing components with zero. The conclusion contradicts the reading it cites: padding `11.0` to `11.0.0.0` makes `11.0.100` greater, not equal. The reading itself is correct, and I verified it against the implementation rather than leaving it as a plausible assumption. `IntrinsicFunctions.VersionGreaterThan` in dotnet/msbuild evaluates `SimpleVersion.Parse(a) > SimpleVersion.Parse(b)`; `SimpleVersion` documents that unspecified components are treated as zero, initialises the three lower components to zero in `Parse`, and compares the four components in order in `CompareTo`. LAMA0601 therefore fires for every shipped .NET 11 SDK, which makes the finding's statement that the platform check "already admits both" true of the target framework axis only. This also changes the consequence class, because a spurious warning to every user on the .NET 11 SDK is shipped behaviour, not only a coverage gap. It reinforces rather than weakens the finding: it is exactly the defect that the missing coverage hides.

The second correction concerns the claim that the platform test would have caught LV-1. `SupportedPlatform.TestedTargetFrameworks/test.json` forbids only LAMA0600, LAMA0601 and LAMA0602, and `MetalamaCheckLangVersion` emits a warning with no code, which `testing.md:226` says does not fail a scenario without `FailOnUnexpectedDiagnostics`. Adding `net11.0` to that project alone would therefore not catch LV-1, and the `DefaultLanguageVersion` scenario named in the proposed change is what does.

The third correction is that `SupportedPlatform.UntestedTargetFramework/README.md:34-35` already assigns the varying .NET SDK matrix to `metalama/Metalama.Tests.DotNetSdk`, so the proposed second `DotNetComponent` competes with an existing decision rather than filling an unowned gap.

Two claims could not be verified in this session and remain assumptions. PostSharp.Engineering is not present on this machine, so neither the generation of `global.json` from `DotNetSdkVersion` (asserted by `platform-support.md:199-201`), nor the `rollForward` policy of the generated file, nor the state of `ToolInvocationOptions.BlockedEnvironmentVariables` could be read. `metalama/Metalama.Tests.DotNetSdk` is not cloned, so whether it already covers the .NET 11 SDK is unknown; that is the open question the finding should carry, alongside the existing one about `rollForward`. The statement of `platform-support.md:338-339` concerns the toolset of the Metalama.Compiler repository, which is likewise not cloned, so "not exercised by continuous integration" is verified for this repository only.

The `where` list of the finding contained five entries that repeat earlier entries in an abbreviated form, such as `Program.cs:19-25` and `platform-support.md:338-339`. The corrected list uses repository-relative paths throughout.

The proposed change would compile in both Roslyn variants, because every element of it is an MSBuild property, a project file or a build-orchestration constant, and none is C# source subject to a `ROSLYN_*` define. It does not conflict with existing code. It is not minimal, because it omits the `MaximumSdkVersion` edit, which is the only part that changes shipped behaviour and which is independent of the container.

corrections.what_happens_today: The public API has IntroduceClass and IntroduceInterface; there is no IntroduceStruct, IntroduceRecord or IntroduceUnion, and NamedTypeBuilder rejects records by assertion. A closed class cannot be introduced because no builder property exists. The builder setters for IsAbstract, IsSealed and IsStatic validate nothing beyond CheckNotFrozen, so no contradictory combination is rejected today either. If IsClosed were added by copying IsAbstract and made to imply IsAbstract, GetTypeSyntaxModifierList would emit `abstract closed class`, which the C# compiler rejects with ERR_ClosedExplicitlyAbstract; the diagnostic name is present in the Roslyn 5.9.0 binary, alongside ERR_ClosedSealedStatic.
corrections.consequence_class: No impact today (the feature is absent). For a future implementation that does not adapt ModifierHelper, the outcome is a C# compiler error (ERR_ClosedExplicitlyAbstract) on the transformed compilation, not a Metalama assertion and not a crash: no builder validation exists that could fire, and the syntax factory accepts any token list.
corrections.proposed_change: Add `new bool IsClosed { get; set; }` to INamedTypeBuilder (the `new` modifier is required once CM-5 adds the read-only `IsClosed` to INamedType; closed applies to classes only, so the property does not belong to IMemberOrNamedTypeBuilder). Validate in NamedTypeBuilder that TypeKind is Class (known at construction, NamedTypeBuilder.cs:34 and 55) and that IsSealed and IsStatic are false. Because the IsSealed and IsStatic setters of MemberOrNamedTypeBuilder are virtual and are called in any order by user code, a check in the IsClosed setter alone is insufficient: either override those setters in NamedTypeBuilder or verify the combination when the builder is frozen. Make IsAbstract read true when IsClosed is true, which matches the Roslyn rule that a closed class carries the Abstract flag (this rests on the Roslyn feature semantics, not on code in this repository). Store the flag in NamedTypeBuilderData and expose it in IntroducedNamedType. In GetTypeSyntaxModifierList emit the `closed` token and skip `abstract` when the type is closed. The token emission must be confined to the latest Roslyn variant: SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword does not exist in Roslyn 5.0, which Metalama.Framework.Engine.5.0.0 compiles against from the same sources, and it is experimental (RSEXPERIMENTAL006) in the consumed 5.10 preview; the gating mechanism is decided by the variant finding of this report and the current policy in the two .props files forbids production branches on ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER. The open question about token order is resolved by the code: GetTypeSyntaxModifierList never emits `partial` for a type, and the design-time generator appends `partial` after the existing modifiers, so a `closed` token emitted there yields `closed partial class`. Do not add union introduction for 2027.0: record introduction is not supported either, and a union declaration requires a case list that the builder has no model for.

notes: The central claim holds: type introduction is limited to classes and interfaces, no closed flag exists anywhere in the builder, data or emission path, and a naive implementation would emit `abstract closed class`. Four details were wrong or incomplete. (1) The cited range IMemberOrNamedTypeBuilder.cs:64-95 does not exist; the file is 46 lines and the properties are at lines 28-45. (2) The consequence class named an assertion or a crash, but the failure mode of an unadapted ModifierHelper is a C# compiler error on the generated code; the builder validates nothing, so no assertion can fire. (3) The proposal emits Token(SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword) without gating, which does not compile in the Roslyn 5.0.0 variant (Engine.5.0.0 compiles the same sources) and hits RSEXPERIMENTAL006 in the consumed 5.10 preview; the report's own variant finding at lines 163-165 covers the mechanism, so the proposal should defer to it rather than remain silent. (4) The setter-only validation of IsSealed and IsStatic is insufficient because those setters are virtual base members that can be called after IsClosed. The open question about `partial` ordering is answered by ModifierHelper.cs:198-236 (no partial for types) and DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs:516 (partial appended last). The claim that Roslyn treats a closed class as abstract and rejects explicit `abstract` depends on external Roslyn semantics; the binary confirms only the existence of ERR_ClosedExplicitlyAbstract and ERR_ClosedSealedStatic. Roslyn 5.0.0 binaries are not on disk, so the absence of ClosedKeyword there rests on FACTS.md.

notes:
The finding survives every external premise except two details of the proposed change, which is why the verdict is corrected rather than confirmed.

First, ITypeSymbol.IsUnion is broader than a union declaration. The proposal separates union types, which are any class or struct carrying System.Runtime.CompilerServices.UnionAttribute (unions.md:36-46), from union declarations, which are the union keyword shorthand (unions.md:724-747). Roslyn reflects that separation: IsUnionTypeCore is IsUnionDeclaration or HasUnionAttribute (SourceNamedTypeSymbol.cs:1463-1477). Using IsUnion to choose the emitted keyword would convert a working case, an attribute-marked partial struct, into the very CS0261 that the finding is about.

Second, the open question is answered by the compiler and not by the proposal, which is silent about parts. The single occurrence of "partial" in unions.md is the grammar at line 742. Roslyn stores the parameter list of the first part in DeclarationWithParameters, reports CS8863 for a second one, and reports CS9370 only when no part has one. A generated part that repeats the case types would be an error; a generated part that omits them is correct. This makes the fix smaller than the finding assumed, because the code model does not have to expose case types.

Two further observations that bound the value of the fix, neither of which changes the verdict. A union declaration forbids instance fields, auto-properties and field-like events for the whole symbol, not per part: SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:2084-2105 iterates the type members and reports ERR_InstanceFieldInUnion, that is CS9373 (ErrorCode.cs:2478). An aspect that introduces a field or an auto-property into a union will therefore fail with that error whatever keyword the generated part uses, so the design-time fix restores only the member kinds a union accepts. Also, the union case types are established from the single-parameter constructors of the union-defining type (unions.md, section "Union creation members"), so a part that introduces a public single-parameter constructor would be reported as ERR_InstanceCtorWithOneParameterInUnion (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:2097-2099).

On the version timeline, the finding's phrase "the July 5.10 build" is accurate for the currently consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3, but the FACTS addendum establishes that the next stable Roslyn is 5.12 and that C# 15 support in 2027.0 requires that move; on main the union syntax API carries no experimental marker, so the argument for text parsing rests on the Roslyn 5.0.0 variant alone.

notes:
The finding's conclusion survives every attempt to refute it, and its weakest link has been replaced by a measurement. The coordinator derived "the November 2026 baseline carries Roslyn 5.12" from the release cadence, and the impact report 08-roslyn-api-delta.md paragraph 1 explicitly flagged that date as "an inference from the cadence, not a published fact". It is now a fact: dotnet/sdk release/11.0.1xx, the .NET 11 general-availability feature band, pins Microsoft.Net.Compilers.Toolset to 5.12.0-1.26451.112 as of a build dated 2026-09-01.

Two subsidiary premises were false and are corrected. Neither changes the outcome.

First, dotnet/roslyn has more release branches than release/dev18.0 and release/dev18.3, and one of them, release/stable, is versioned 5.10.0. So the sentence "will never have a stable counterpart" is too strong: Roslyn 5.10 will ship as a Visual Studio product. The operative statement, which is true, is narrower: no stable Microsoft.CodeAnalysis 5.10.0 package is served by nuget.org, and none is expected, because the nuget.org stable packages are published for the .NET software development kit feature bands. Since ToNuGetVersionString names a package that a user machine must restore, a bare "5.10.0" identity would still fail the restore. The finding's conclusion is unaffected.

Second, the cadence is stated with the wrong mechanism. Visual Studio 2026 snaps monthly and Roslyn minors follow it one per month; the stable nuget.org packages follow the quarterly software development kit feature bands. Anyone reasoning from "Visual Studio 2026 quarterly releases" would compute the November 2026 baseline as 18.12 by luck rather than by the right chain, and would get the wrong answer for a different date. Worth fixing in platform-support.md at the same time as the 5.11 correction, because platform-support.md:233-236 rests its whole Roslyn floor on that reasoning.

Two independent facts confirm that the target must be 5.12 and not 5.10 or 5.11, both from files fetched directly. LanguageVersion.cs on release/stable has no CSharp15, so no Roslyn 5.10 build could deliver C# 15 even if it were published as a stable package. Syntax.xml on release/stable still carries the five ExperimentalUrl attributes, so the generator would still strip the union, with-element and labeled break and continue nodes; on release/insiders and on main only UnsafeExpressionSyntax keeps one. This also confirms the finding's statement about the generator, and it dates the change to the 5.11 window rather than to 5.12, which does not affect the plan because 5.11 has no stable package either.

The open question about System.Text.Json is now partly answered and should be restated. The floor is not fixed per Roslyn minor: 5.9.0's Features package requires 10.0.1, and the consumed 5.10 preview requires 10.0.8 per the comment in Roslyn.5.10.0.props. The floor tracks the servicing version current when the package is built, so a 5.12 package built alongside .NET 11 may require an 11.0.x version. Step 2 must read the nuspec rather than assume that the existing pin of 10.0.11 still satisfies it.

First, `IsBaseTypeDeclaration` (SyntaxKindExtensions.cs:41) is written as `kind.IsTypeDeclaration || kind is SyntaxKind.EnumDeclaration or SyntaxKind.DelegateDeclaration`, so it does not need a change of its own; listing it as a second edit site is wrong. Second, the precedent cited for the implementation technique is mis-stated: `AllLanguageVersions.cs:13-19` declares hard-coded numeric casts as `const`, which is the technique the proposal explicitly rejects, and a `static readonly` field produced by `Enum.TryParse` cannot appear inside the `is ... or ...` constant pattern, so the property body has to be restructured. Both options remain viable; the proposal should say which trade-off it accepts. Third, the consequence is not purely a design-time one: the same generator runs during a build from LinkerPipelineStage.cs:113-124, where the diagnostic sink is deliberately discarded, so the build silently omits the DesignTimeGeneratedCode file while the linker still injects the members into the assembly.

Two observations that strengthen rather than weaken the finding. The same root cause makes `SymbolExtensions.IsPrimaryConstructor` (SymbolExtensions.cs:288-291) return false for a union's primary constructor, and unions are declared with a parameter list in the grammar (Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1959), so that path is exercised by the same source. And the duplicate-modifier defect in `TheCodeFixProvider.GetFixedDocumentAsync` is independent of unions: the method never inspects the existing modifier list, so it is worth hardening on its own account rather than only removing its trigger.

The proposal to widen `IsTypeDeclaration` rather than to loosen the test at the `IsPartial` site is the right direction, and I tried to refute it. `ExtensionBlockDeclarationSyntax` also derives from `TypeDeclarationSyntax` (Syntax-5.10.0.xml:2083), so the kind test is load-bearing and cannot be dropped, and `KindCheckOptimizationAnalyzer.cs:722-727` would object to a bare type test. The analyzer matches the property by name only, so the implementation may change freely. The blast radius is about nine other production call sites, which is why the size estimate of M is right and why the change should be reviewed site by site rather than treated as a one-line edit.

Not verified here. That a union symbol carries `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.TypeKind.Struct` rests on the finding's own reading of Roslyn main; `dotnet/roslyn` is not cloned and no Roslyn assembly is present in the local package cache, so `SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:69-79` was checked only for what it does with each possible input. If the stable Roslyn gives unions a new `TypeKind`, the default arm of that switch throws `InvalidOperationException` and the consequence class becomes a crash rather than a wrong warning. That is the one open risk that would change this finding materially. The exact compiler error number for the duplicated modifier (claimed as CS1004) is likewise unverifiable here; the statement was softened to "a duplicate-modifier compile error".

The two aspect tests whose expected output differs between the variants use ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER, which the latest variant defines." `eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.5.10.0.props:8-10` states the same in the other direction, and line 10 is the single `DefineConstants` entry. `git grep -n ROSLYN_ -- '*.cs'` returns exactly two files, `Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Metalama.Framework.Tests.AspectTests/Tests/Aspects/DesignTimeInvalidCode/UnknownAccessorInTemplate.cs:7` and `UnknownAccessorInTemplate_Roslyn5_0.cs:7`, so the finding's statement of the current state is accurate.

One part of the proposed change is inaccurate and should be corrected before a story is written. The finding says that the `#if ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER` option "requires lifting the policy stated in the two .props files". The policy is written down in two places and already permits the branch. `Directory.Packages.md:221` reads "A symbol is warranted again only when the source has to branch on a distinction between two variants that no existing symbol expresses. The `.props` comments record a state of the source, not a prohibition. So the `#if` route needs the condition to be met and the two comments and `Directory.Packages.md:213` to be updated, not a policy reversal. A story should say that.

A fourth mechanism exists that the finding does not list, and it is already wired. `Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Metalama.Framework.Engine.csproj:37-38` compiles `../../.generated/$(ThisRoslynVersionNoPreview)/Metalama.Framework.Engine/*.cs`, with a `-stubs` fallback, so each variant already compiles its own generated sources. `eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:18` and `:37` generate one output directory per version name, currently 5.0.0 and 5.10.0, and `eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Generator.cs:64-97` writes the `RoslynApiVersion` enum into it, so `RoslynApiVersion.Current` really is variant-specific and the guard the finding names is available. corrections.proposed_change: When reading a manifest, clamp the language version to `RoslynApiVersion.Current.ToLanguageVersion()` at the two fallback sites (`CompileTimeProjectRepository.Builder.cs:596`, `CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:1355`) and report a warning that names the library's language version and the host's maximum, so that a library compiled with a newer language than the host understands degrades with a message rather than with CS8192. The `UsedApiVersion` string form matters for LV-13; the integer language version never reaches `ToDisplayStringSafe` on the read path, so LV-5 and LV-13 remain separate.

notes: Refutation attempts and their outcome. (1) The claim that the writer is the \"5.10 variant\" is false for the consumed build: the 5.10 preview has no `CSharp15` and maps `Default` to `CSharp14` (FACTS.md:54-56; 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:16-17,78). (2) The claim that Roslyn 5.0 \"rejects\" 1500 is confirmed and made precise: CS8192 at the parse stage, no exception at construction, at parsing or at binding; the finding's own confidence note already anticipated this.
