evidence:
Confirmed premises.

1. Syntax and API shape. `BreakStatementSyntax` and `ContinueStatementSyntax` gain an optional `Name` of type `IdentifierNameSyntax`, new in the 5.10 window and marked experimental, absent from Roslyn 5.0 (scratchpad/impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:66-68). The local grammar confirms it: eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1296 declares `<Field Name="Name" Type="IdentifierNameSyntax" Optional="true" ExperimentalUrl="https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/issues/83266" />` inside the `BreakStatementSyntax` node (:1290-1300). Because `Name` is a `Node` field, it is a child node, so the workaround `node.ChildNodes().OfType<IdentifierNameSyntax>()` proposed by the finding does reach it on any package version.

2. No new `SyntaxKind` for a labeled break, and the target label is an ordinary labeled statement (scratchpad/impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:99, :126). The proposal amends section 13.5 of the standard so that the statement immediately nested in a `labeled_statement` is "labeled with" the identifier (csharplang proposals/csharp-15.0/labeled-break-continue.md, section "13.5 Labeled statements").

3. Target resolution. `break identifier;` exits "the nearest enclosing switch_statement or iteration_statement labeled with that identifier"; without an identifier it exits the nearest enclosing switch or iteration statement (labeled-break-continue.md, sections 13.10.2 and 13.10.3). The finding's statement that a generated plain `break;` exits the innermost loop of the target, and therefore silently changes the target, is correct.

Premises that are false or incomplete.

4. The feature check is in the binder, not in the parser. `LanguageParser.ParseBreakStatement` on dotnet/roslyn main parses the optional label unconditionally and performs no feature check: `this.IsTrueIdentifier() ? this.ParseIdentifierName() : null` (src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Parser/LanguageParser.cs:9354-9361, and identically at the 5.10-window commit 27d6bed68b458350aca01f91397fa8be9605d47b, lines 9394-9401). The check is `MessageID.IDS_FeatureLabeledBreakContinue.CheckFeatureAvailability(diagnostics, node, name.GetLocation())` in `Binder.BindBreakOrContinue` (src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Binder/Binder_Statements.cs:2955-2966 on main, and line 2966 at the 5.10-window commit). The finding's reachability paragraph attributes the rejection to the parser.

5. The open question is answered in the negative. `CheckFeatureAvailability` reads the language version from `syntax.SyntaxTree.Options` (src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Errors/MessageID.cs:394-406), not from the compilation. `CompileTimeCompilationBuilder` attaches parse options to every tree it creates: `CSharpSyntaxTree.Create((CSharpSyntaxNode) compileTimeSyntaxRoot, new CSharpParseOptions(languageVersion, preprocessorSymbols: runTimePreprocessorSymbols), path, Encoding.UTF8)` (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CompileTime/CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:348-352). The binder of the compile-time compilation therefore re-checks the feature version although `CSharpSyntaxTree.Create` does not re-parse, and a compile-time scope `break outer;` produces the feature error instead of being accepted silently. The compile-time language version is capped at `CSharp14` for every .NET SDK of major version 10 or later, and the cap also applies when the project language version is `preview`, because the code returns the smaller of the two (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Utilities/LanguageVersionProvider.cs:44-70).

6. The diagnostic named in the consequence class is the wrong one. For a labeled `break` whose label designates no enclosing labeled loop, the binder reports `ERR_NoBreakId`, which is CS9393, or `ERR_NoContinueId`, which is CS9394 (src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Errors/ErrorCode.cs:2505-2506; scratchpad/impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:129). CS0159 is `ERR_LabelNotFound` (ErrorCode.cs:137) and belongs to `goto`. The binder explicitly discards the diagnostics of `BindLabel` when the break target is not found, so CS0159 is not reported on this path (Binder_Statements.cs:2972-2973).

7. Reachability is not gated on TP-8. In the consumed Roslyn, `MessageID.RequiredVersion` returns `LanguageVersion.Preview` for `IDS_FeatureLabeledBreakContinue` (MessageID.cs at commit 27d6bed6, lines 496-504); it returns `LanguageVersion.CSharp15` only on main, that is on the future 5.12 (src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Errors/MessageID.cs:499-506). `LanguageVersion.CSharp15 = 1500` exists only on main (src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/LanguageVersion.cs:283) and is absent from the stable 5.9.0 and from the consumed 5.10 preview (scratchpad/FACTS.md addendum, "State of the C# 15 API in the stable Roslyn 5.9.0"; scratchpad/impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:78). `VerifyLanguageVersion` accepts `LanguageVersion.Preview` when `AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures` is set (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Pipeline/CompileTime/CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:70-76). An aspect project with an explicit `<LangVersion>preview</LangVersion>` therefore reaches every run-time scope path today, and TP-8 cannot name `LanguageVersion.CSharp15` before Roslyn 5.12 is consumed.

8. The test option does not select the variants the finding expects. `TestOptions` parses the argument with `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse`, and when the parse fails on a numeric argument of at least 10 it sets `SkipReason` (Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/TestOptions.cs:680-698). `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse` accepts "15" and "15.0" only where `CSharp15` exists (LanguageVersion.cs:580-583 on main), so with both currently consumed packages, 5.0 and the 5.10 preview, `@LanguageVersion(15.0)` skips the test in every variant and yields no coverage. `TryParse` accepts "preview" on every version (LanguageVersion.cs:492-494).

9. Nesting rule for the label. The proposal states that only the statement immediately nested within a labeled statement is labeled with that identifier, and gives `a: b: while (…) …` as the example in which only `b` labels the loop, so `break a;` inside the body does not target the `while` (labeled-break-continue.md, note under section 13.5, and the "nested labels" open question, whose recommendation is not to support it). A labeled `continue` may target only an iteration statement, not a `switch` (labeled-break-continue.md, section 13.10.3).

The core defect survives every correction: the annotator does not read the label, the generated run-time factory drops it, and the emitted `break;` silently targets a different loop.

corrections.what_happens_today:
Template scope classification: VisitBreakStatement and VisitContinueStatement annotate the statement with CurrentBreakOrContinueScope (TemplateAnnotator.cs:1375-1379), which every loop and switch sets to its own scope for its body (ScopeContext.cs:123-132, callers at :1414, :2500, :2533, :2559, :2927). The Name child is never read, so a break outer; inside a run-time inner loop nested in a compile-time outer loop is classified run-time, and the reverse is classified compile-time, whatever the label designates. Neither TemplateAnnotator nor TemplateCompilerRewriter overrides VisitLabeledStatement; a labeled statement gets no scope annotation of its own because AddScopeAnnotationToVisitedNode returns statements untouched (TemplateAnnotator.cs:676-680), and its transformation kind is then decided by IsCompileTimeCode from the parent chain or from an annotation forced by an enclosing compile-time if or foreach (TemplateAnnotator.cs:1360-1361, :1423; TemplateCompilerRewriter.cs:196-266). The label designates the nearest enclosing switch or iteration statement carried by a labeled statement whose immediately nested statement is that switch or loop (csharplang proposals/csharp-15.0/labeled-break-continue.md, sections 13.5, 13.10.2 and 13.10.3), so the scope of the statement must follow the labeled loop and not the innermost one.

Run-time scope: the generated TransformBreakStatement builds SyntaxFactory.BreakStatement(attributeLists, breakKeyword, semicolonToken) from the stripped field list (Generator.cs:481-519), so the label is dropped and the generated run-time code contains a plain break; that exits the innermost enclosing switch or loop of the target. No diagnostic.

Compile-time scope: the statement is kept as compile-time C# (TemplateCompilerRewriter.cs:2266-2287, case StatementSyntax). The base CSharpSyntaxRewriter.VisitBreakStatement visits Name through VisitIdentifierName (TemplateCompilerRewriter.cs:2908-2980), where the compile-time branch delegates to _compileTimeOnlyRewriter (:2980), so the label identifier is preserved. The compile-time compilation does not accept the result. Roslyn checks IDS_FeatureLabeledBreakContinue in the binder and not in the parser (Binder_Statements.cs:2955-2966; ParseBreakStatement in LanguageParser.cs:9354-9361 has no check), and CheckFeatureAvailability reads the language version from the parse options of the syntax tree (MessageID.cs:394-406). CompileTimeCompilationBuilder attaches new CSharpParseOptions(languageVersion, ...) to every tree it creates (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:348-352), so the check runs again although CSharpSyntaxTree.Create does not re-parse. The compile-time language version is capped at CSharp14 by LanguageVersionProvider.cs:44-70 for every .NET SDK of major version 10 or later, and the cap also applies when the project language version is preview, so the compile-time compilation reports the feature error on the label rather than accepting it silently. This failure mode is loud, and it becomes silent only if the compile-time language version is raised to the required version.

A labeled statement whose loop is run-time inside a compile-time block: the forced CompileTimeOnly annotation (TemplateAnnotator.cs:1423) makes the generated VisitLabeledStatement take the base.VisitLabeledStatement branch (Generator.cs:419-420), which casts the transformed child, an InvocationExpressionSyntax, to StatementSyntax. The InvalidCastException is wrapped into SyntaxProcessingException by SafeSyntaxRewriter.Visit (SafeSyntaxRewriter.cs:56-61). A labeled statement directly in the template body has no annotation and is transformed as run-time code (TemplateCompilerRewriter.cs:239-262, the null parent case returns false), which wraps a compile-time loop into a run-time labeled block through TransformStatement (TemplateCompilerRewriter.cs:625-630). Labels are useless in templates today because goto is rejected (TemplateAnnotator.cs:2601-2606), so none of these paths is covered by a test (Tests/UnsupportedSyntax/GotoNotSupported.cs is the only labeled statement in the template test suites).

Reachability: the paths above are open today and do not wait for TP-8. In the consumed Roslyn, IDS_FeatureLabeledBreakContinue requires LanguageVersion.Preview and not CSharp15 (MessageID.cs at the 5.10-window commit 27d6bed6, lines 496-504), and LanguageVersion.CSharp15 does not exist in the stable 5.9.0 or in the consumed 5.10 preview, so an aspect project with an explicit <LangVersion>preview</LangVersion> and MetalamaAllowPreviewLanguageFeatures passes VerifyLanguageVersion (CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:70-76) and reaches every run-time scope path. At C# 14 or lower the template is rejected, but by the binder and not by the parser: the syntax tree is well formed, TemplateCompiler.TryAnnotate still runs and still mis-classifies the statement, which is what design-time syntax highlighting uses, and only the following check on semanticModel.GetDiagnostics stops the rewriter (TemplateCompiler.cs:152-162). Adding C# 15 to SupportedCSharpVersions.All (TP-8) makes the paths reachable without the preview flag; it cannot name LanguageVersion.CSharp15 before Roslyn 5.12 is consumed, because that enum value exists only on Roslyn main (LanguageVersion.cs:283).
corrections.proposed_change: (1) In TemplateAnnotator, add VisitLabeledStatement that visits the inner statement and copies its scope annotation to the labeled statement, and record label name to scope in ScopeContext. Record the mapping only when the statement immediately nested in the labeled statement is a switch statement or an iteration statement, because the proposal labels only the immediately nested statement: in a: b: while (...) only b labels the loop, and break a; does not target it (labeled-break-continue.md, note under section 13.5). A labeled continue may target only an iteration statement, never a switch (section 13.10.3). (2) In VisitBreakStatement and VisitContinueStatement, when Name is not null, resolve the label scope from the context, annotate the statement with that scope, and report a new error, in the family of TemplatingDiagnosticDescriptors next to LAMA0101, when a run-time break targets a compile-time loop, since the unrolled loop has no run-time counterpart; a compile-time break targeting a run-time loop must be annotated run-time so that the label survives in the generated code. (3) In TemplateCompilerRewriter, handle a labeled statement whose inner statement is run-time by transforming the whole labeled statement (the generated TransformLabeledStatement already exists) instead of letting the base rewriter cast. Because the Name field is absent from Roslyn 5.0 and marked experimental in the consumed 5.10 package (Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1296), step (2) must read the label through node.ChildNodes().OfType<IdentifierNameSyntax>() until the stable package is consumed, or be written after the package update; Name is a child Node, so that enumeration reaches it. Add template tests under Tests/Syntax/ for the four combinations of compile-time or run-time outer loop with compile-time or run-time inner loop. Do not annotate them with @LanguageVersion(15.0) if coverage is wanted before Roslyn 5.12: LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse rejects "15.0" on both consumed packages, and TestOptions.cs:680-698 then sets SkipReason, so every variant would skip the tests and they would prove nothing. Use @LanguageVersion(preview) together with the preview flag for coverage now, and switch the tests to @LanguageVersion(15.0) when the latest variant moves to Roslyn 5.12, at which point the Roslyn 5.0 variant skips them by the same mechanism.

notes:
The finding survives. Its central claim, that the annotator ignores the label and that the generated run-time factory drops it, rests on no external premise that fails, and the C# 15 semantics confirm the consequence: the label selects the nearest enclosing labeled switch or loop, so an emitted plain break silently retargets to the innermost one.

Five external corrections were needed. First, the language-version check for labeled break and continue is performed by the binder and not by the parser, so the statement always parses and the annotator always sees it; the rejection at C# 14 comes from semanticModel.GetDiagnostics inside TemplateCompiler, which runs after TryAnnotate. Second, the finding's open question is answered in the negative: because the feature check reads the parse options of the syntax tree and CompileTimeCompilationBuilder attaches parse options carrying the compile-time language version, the check runs again in the compile-time compilation even though CSharpSyntaxTree.Create does not re-parse, so a compile-time scope labeled break fails loudly rather than being accepted silently. Third, the diagnostic named in the consequence class is wrong; the correct codes are CS9393 and CS9394, not CS0159. Fourth, reachability is not gated on TP-8: in every Roslyn that Metalama consumes today the feature requires LanguageVersion.Preview, which VerifyLanguageVersion accepts under MetalamaAllowPreviewLanguageFeatures, so the run-time scope paths are already open; and TP-8 cannot name LanguageVersion.CSharp15 before Roslyn 5.12 is consumed. Fifth, the proposed test annotation @LanguageVersion(15.0) would skip the new tests in every variant on the current packages, giving no coverage; @LanguageVersion(preview) is required until Roslyn 5.12 arrives.

One refinement was added to the proposed change: the label-to-scope map must be populated only when the statement immediately nested in the labeled statement is a switch or an iteration statement, because the proposal explicitly rejects nested labels, and a labeled continue may not target a switch.

Two limits of this verification. The consumed package Microsoft.CodeAnalysis 5.10.0-1.26365.3 was not read directly; the parser, binder and MessageID behaviour attributed to it was read at commit 27d6bed68b458350aca01f91397fa8be9605d47b, the end of the 5.10 window, which the Roslyn API delta report establishes as API-identical to the consumed build. The date at which Roslyn 5.12 ships is an inference from the release cadence and not a published fact, as the delta report itself states.

evidence:
Premise 1, extension indexers are a C# 15 feature and are not permitted in C# 14, so no C# 14 test can exercise one. Confirmed. The proposal lives at proposals/csharp-15.0/extension-indexers.md and states that it extends the grammar "relative to proposals/csharp-14.0/extensions.md" by adding "indexer_declaration // new" to extension_member_declaration (local copy /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Metalama/ccf204f4-b0b3-5fe6-a8de-fe20f6791d2c/scratchpad/ext-indexers.md:11-21); the C# 14 production has only method_declaration, property_declaration and operator_declaration. The feature is gated on IDS_FeatureExtensionIndexers, which returns Preview in Roslyn 5.9.0 and in the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 and CSharp15 on main (FACTS.md:31, 54; impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:16, 147). The local grep confirms the absence of any indexer in the C# 14 extension-member tests: `grep -rn "this\[" Tests/Aspects/CSharp14/ExtensionMembers` returns nothing.

Premise 2, extension indexers add no new syntax node, no new SyntaxKind and no new symbol API, so they reuse IndexerDeclarationSyntax inside ExtensionBlockDeclarationSyntax and surface as IPropertySymbol with IsIndexer on a type of TypeKind.Extension. Confirmed. impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:21 ("Extension indexers and closed classes add no node"), :96 ("Extension indexers are IPropertySymbol instances with IsIndexer == true declared on an INamedTypeSymbol with IsExtension == true (TypeKind.Extension), using the 5.0 members ExtensionParameter, ExtensionGroupingName, ExtensionMarkerName and AssociatedExtensionImplementation"), :144-145; FACTS.md:28. The proposal names no new node and describes the lowering as an extension property named Item plus static get_Item/set_Item implementation methods with the receiver prepended (ext-indexers.md:180-196). This supports the finding's premise that the same engine paths as for extension properties are taken.

Premise 3, inside an extension block the receiver is named by the receiver parameter and `this` is not available, so an emitted `this.<member>` is invalid there. Confirmed, and it is a rule of the already shipped C# 14 feature, not of C# 15. The extension-indexers proposal states: "All rules from the C# standard that apply to ordinary indexers apply to extension indexers, but extension members do not have an implicit or explicit `this`" (ext-indexers.md:50-51). The C# 14 extensions proposal states: "Instance members refer to the receiver with the receiver parameter name" (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Metalama/ccf204f4-b0b3-5fe6-a8de-fe20f6791d2c/scratchpad/ext14.md:144). This confirms the reported pre-existing gap for the non-inlined trampolines of extension methods and properties.

Premise 4, an extension block that declares an indexer must name its receiver parameter and there is no static extension indexer. Confirmed: "Because indexers are always instance members, an extension block that declares an indexer must provide a named receiver parameter" (ext-indexers.md:29-30). The finding does not state this; it strengthens the receiver-contract part of the finding and narrows the proposed test matrix.

Premise 5, the injected override member (a private indexer carrying an additional marker parameter) is a legal extension member. Not contradicted. The forbidden modifiers on an extension member are abstract, virtual, override, new, sealed, partial, protected and the related accessibility modifiers, plus readonly, and init accessors are forbidden (ext14.md:171-173; ext-indexers.md:32-35). `private` is not among them. The committed baseline of the analogous property test shows that the injected member does not survive in the inlined output (tests/Metalama.Framework.Tests.AspectTests/Tests/Aspects/CSharp14/ExtensionMembers/ExtensionMembers_OverrideProperty.t.cs contains only the two original members with the receiver name `test` substituted).

Premise 6, refuted as stated: the proposed tests under Aspects/CSharp15/ExtensionIndexers cannot be written against the Roslyn that Metalama consumes today. LanguageVersion.CSharp15 does not exist in the stable 5.9.0 assemblies nor in the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3; it was added to main on 2026-08-11 by dotnet/roslyn#84799 (FACTS.md:54-56; impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:17, 78). In those builds the six C# 15 features are reachable only under LanguageVersion.Preview, and Metalama rejects Preview unless AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures is set (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Pipeline/CompileTime/CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:72; FACTS.md:21) and rejects any version outside {10..14} (SupportedCSharpVersions, FACTS.md:16). The next stable Roslyn is expected to be 5.12, not 5.10 or 5.11 (FACTS.md:48-49; impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:15, 18). The test option `@LanguageVersion(15.0)` would today set a skip reason, "is not recognized by the current version of Roslyn" (Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/TestOptions.cs:681-696).

corrections.what_happens_today: No test exercises an indexer inside an extension block, because the C# 14 grammar for an extension member admits only a method, a property and an operator; the C# 15 proposal adds indexer_declaration to that production (ext-indexers.md:11-21). The feature is gated on IDS_FeatureExtensionIndexers, which requires LanguageVersion.Preview in the stable Roslyn 5.9.0 and in the consumed preview 5.10.0-1.26365.3, and LanguageVersion.CSharp15 only on Roslyn main since 2026-08-11 (FACTS.md:31, 54; 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:16-17, 147). An extension indexer adds no syntax node, no SyntaxKind and no symbol API: it is an IndexerDeclarationSyntax inside an ExtensionBlockDeclarationSyntax and surfaces as an IPropertySymbol with IsIndexer on a type of TypeKind.Extension (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:21, 96, 144-145), so the engine paths described in the finding are the paths that will be taken. Two rules of the extension-member feature that the finding does not state also hold. First, an extension block that declares an indexer must provide a named receiver parameter, and there is no static extension indexer, because an indexer is always an instance member (ext-indexers.md:29-30). Second, an extension member has no implicit or explicit `this` and refers to its receiver by the receiver parameter name (ext-indexers.md:50-51; ext14.md:144), which is what makes the receiver substitution of CreateIndexerAccessExpression necessary and what makes the `this.<member>` of the non-inlined trampolines invalid inside an extension block. The injected private override indexer is not forbidden: the modifiers that an extension member may not carry are abstract, virtual, override, new, sealed, partial, protected and the related accessibility modifiers, plus readonly, and an init accessor is not allowed (ext14.md:171-173; ext-indexers.md:32-35).
corrections.proposed_change: Add the aspect tests, and sequence them after the language-version prerequisite. The tests cannot be written against the Roslyn that Metalama consumes today: LanguageVersion.CSharp15 exists only on Roslyn main since 2026-08-11 and the first stable package expected to carry it is 5.12 (FACTS.md:54-56; 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:17-18, 78), while Metalama rejects LanguageVersion.Preview unless AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures is set (CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:72) and rejects any version outside C# 10 to C# 14 (SupportedCSharpVersions, FACTS.md:16, 21). A test carrying the option @LanguageVersion(15.0) is skipped today with the reason that the version is not recognized by the current version of Roslyn (TestOptions.cs:681-696). The test matrix should also follow the feature rules: there is no static extension indexer and the receiver parameter is always named, so there is no counterpart to ExtensionMembers_Contract_OnReceiver_Static, and no init-accessor case. The second part of the proposal, making the trampoline helpers use IExtensionBlock.ReceiverParameter.Name when the containing type is an extension block, is independent of C# 15 and can proceed now, because it repairs the already shipped C# 14 extension methods and properties.

notes:
Every external premise of the finding that concerns the behaviour of the language holds. The only correction is one of sequencing: the proposed tests name a C# 15 language version that no Roslyn consumed by Metalama exposes, so they are blocked on the same prerequisite as the rest of the C# 15 work, whereas the trampoline repair is not, because it concerns the C# 14 extension members that already ship.

Two additions that make the finding more precise. An extension block that declares an indexer must name its receiver parameter, so the indexer test matrix has no static case and no unnamed-receiver case. An extension member may not have an init accessor, so the accessor matrix is get and set only.

One nuance that neither refutes nor corrects the finding. In the consumed Roslyn the extension-indexer feature is already reachable under LanguageVersion.Preview, so a test could in principle be written today with the @LanguageVersion option and the AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures project option, ahead of the move to the stable Roslyn. That route is not recommended, because the expected output would have to be revised once the language version becomes C# 15.

Not verified: whether Roslyn accepts a private extension indexer. The proposals list the forbidden modifiers and private is not among them, but no compiler source was read on this point, and Metalama.Compiler is not cloned (FACTS.md:6), so the behaviour of the Metalama compiler fork on the new syntax is an assumption.

State of the code, verified on branch topic/2027.0/26-09-03-update-eng-7e3j07.

The finding is accurate. /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Patterns/src/tests/Metalama.Patterns.Contracts.UnitTests/DoubleTests.cs:5 guards the `using Xunit;` directive with `#if NET6_0`, and line 13 guards the whole body of the class, which ends at line 43. /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Patterns/src/tests/Metalama.Patterns.Contracts.UnitTests/Metalama.Patterns.Contracts.UnitTests.csproj:4 declares `<TargetFrameworks>net472;net10.0</TargetFrameworks>`. evidence:
Premise 1 (a union reports TypeKind.Struct), CONFIRMED and no longer conditional. dotnet/roslyn main, src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/EnumConversions.cs:33-37 maps DeclarationKind.Struct, DeclarationKind.Union and DeclarationKind.RecordStruct to TypeKind.Struct. TypeKind gains no value between 5.0 and main (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:94). A union is neither IsRecord nor IsRecordStruct (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:1038-1050, both compare declaration.Declarations[0].Kind to Record and RecordStruct respectively), so Metalama's INamedType.IsRecord (SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:173, forwarding INamedTypeSymbol.IsRecord) is false and the arm selected in CreatePartialType is `TypeKind.Struct when !type.IsRecord`, which emits StructDeclaration (DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs:747-758). The finding's alternative branch, "If Roslyn reports a new TypeKind value instead, SourceNamedTypeImpl.TypeKind throws before this point", is dead: SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:69-79 receives TypeKind.Struct and does not throw.

Premise 2 (a generated `partial struct U` beside a source `partial union U(...)` is rejected), CONFIRMED, and the diagnostic can now be named. DeclarationKind.Union is a distinct value (Declarations/DeclarationKind.cs:14-27; SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration maps to it at :41). Two single declarations merge into one type only when their kinds are equal (Declarations/SingleTypeDeclaration.cs:260-265, `thisDecl._kind != otherDecl._kind` returns false). Unmerged same-name declarations that are both partial produce ERR_PartialTypeKindConflict (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:1455-1459), CS0261, whose message on main is "Partial declarations of '{0}' must be all classes, all record classes, all structs, all unions, all record structs, or all interfaces" (CSharpResources.resx:1161-1163). The word "unions" in that message is direct confirmation that a union part and a struct part cannot be merged.

Premise 3 (`partial` is permitted on a union), CONFIRMED. Grammar of the proposal: `attributes? struct_modifier* 'partial'? 'union' identifier ...` (csharp-15.0/unions.md:742-747). Implementation: SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:340-347 adds DeclarationModifiers.Partial for TypeKind.Struct and excludes only Ref for a union declaration.

Premise 4 (the `closed` case), REFUTED as an open question; the compiler behaves as the finding's optimistic branch. Modifiers of the parts are unioned: SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:453-459, `result |= mods` over declaration.Declarations. DeclarationModifiers.Closed is an ordinary member of the allowed set for a class (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:331-332), IsClosed is read from the merged flags (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:902), and the implicit abstractness is applied to the merged value (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:400-403). No diagnostic requires `closed` on every part: the only closed-related error codes are ERR_ClosedTypeNameDisallowed 9380, ERR_ClosedSealedStatic 9381, ERR_ClosedBaseTypeBaseFromOtherAssembly 9382, ERR_UnderspecifiedClosedSubtype 9383, ERR_ClosedExplicitlyAbstract 9384 and ERR_ClosedBadDerivedTypesProperty 9395 (Errors/ErrorCode.cs:2489-2507), and the partial modifier check reports only accessibility conflicts (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:249-253). The proposal itself never mentions `partial` (closed-hierarchies.md contains no occurrence of the word). So `closed` merges exactly like `abstract` and `sealed`, and the generated `partial class C` without `closed` is legal.

Premise 5 (the case list on partial parts), REFUTED as stated in the proposed change. Roslyn allows the case list on at most one part and requires it on at least one. SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:4108-4149: the first part carrying a ParameterList becomes DeclarationWithParameters, and any further part with a ParameterList reports ERR_MultipleRecordParameterLists, whose message on main is "Only a single partial type declaration may have a parameter list" (CSharpResources.resx:6621-6623), CS8863. SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:4992-5061: when no part carries a non-empty ParameterList, ERR_UnionDeclarationNeedsCaseTypes (CS9370, "A union declaration must specify at least one case type.", CSharpResources.resx:8333-8335) is reported. The case list is therefore syntactically optional on a part: UnionDeclarationSyntax.ParameterList is `Optional="true"` (eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1965), and the parser produces null when the token after the type parameter list is not `(` (Parser/LanguageParser.cs:1837-1839). The proposal grammar makes the parenthesized case_types mandatory (unions.md:742-747), but the implementation does not, and the implementation is what the generated file must satisfy.

Premise 6 (the union case cannot be written without the latest-variant API), CONFIRMED, with a version correction. SyntaxKind.UnionKeyword, SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration, UnionDeclarationSyntax and SyntaxFactory.UnionDeclaration are absent from Roslyn 5.0 and present but [RSEXPERIMENTAL006] in stable 5.9.0 and in the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:58-61, FACTS.md:53). The markers are removed only by commit #84799 of 2026-08-11, so the first stable package exposing them without an experimental attribute is expected to be 5.12 (FACTS.md:49, 55-56; 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:15, 32, 90). A union is neither IsRecord nor IsRecordStruct (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:1038-1050), so CreatePartialType takes the arm `TypeKind.Struct when !type.IsRecord` and generates `partial struct U { ... }` beside the source `partial union U(...)`. The two parts have different DeclarationKind values, do not merge (Declarations/SingleTypeDeclaration.cs:260-265), and the compiler reports CS0261 ERR_PartialTypeKindConflict, whose message on main is "Partial declarations of '{0}' must be all classes, all record classes, all structs, all unions, all record structs, or all interfaces" (CSharpResources.resx:1161-1163). The alternative branch of the finding, in which a new TypeKind value would make SourceNamedTypeImpl.TypeKind throw first, does not exist. For a `closed partial class C` the generated part is `partial class C` and this is legal: the compiler unions the modifiers of all parts (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:453-459, `result |= mods`), reads IsClosed from the merged flags (:902) and applies the implicit abstractness to the merged value (:400-403); no error code requires `closed` on every part (Errors/ErrorCode.cs:2489-2507). This is no longer an open question and no longer depends on the proposal, which never mentions `partial`.
corrections.proposed_change: Add a `union` case that emits a UnionDeclarationSyntax with `parameterList: null`. Do not copy the source case list: Roslyn accepts the case list on at most one partial part and reports CS8863 ERR_MultipleRecordParameterLists ("Only a single partial type declaration may have a parameter list", CSharpResources.resx:6621-6623) on every further part carrying one (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:4108-4149), while the source part already satisfies the at-least-one requirement of CS9370 ERR_UnionDeclarationNeedsCaseTypes (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:4992-5061). A part without a case list is representable and parseable: UnionDeclarationSyntax.ParameterList is optional (Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1965) and the parser produces null when the token after the type parameter list is not `(` (Parser/LanguageParser.cs:1837-1839). The factory has no convenience overload (SkipConvenienceFactories="true", Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1954), so all twelve arguments must be passed. The case still needs variant gating, because the union syntax API is absent from Roslyn 5.0 and is [RSEXPERIMENTAL006] in stable 5.9.0 and in the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3; the gate belongs to the latest variant, whose symbol follows the variant version and becomes ROSLYN_5_12_0_OR_GREATER after the renumbering to the stable Roslyn 5.12. For `closed`, no production change is required; a regression test with @TestScenario(DesignTime) on a `closed partial class` is optional confirmation rather than a step whose outcome is unknown.
corrections.consequence_class: For unions, a design-time compilation error in the generated document (CS0261) once the language version is C# 15, so the IDE shows errors on the type. For `closed`, no impact: the compiler merges the modifier across partial parts, so the omission in the generated part is correct as written.

notes:
The finding survives, and its union half is now firmer than it was stated: the two hedges it carried are resolved in its favour. The union target reports TypeKind.Struct as a verified fact, and the compiler error is identified as CS0261, whose message text on Roslyn main names unions explicitly.

Three premises needed correction and one is refuted outright.

The refuted one is the `closed` open question. The compiler unions the modifiers of all partial parts, `closed` is an ordinary DeclarationModifiers value, and no diagnostic requires it on every part, so the generated `partial class C` is correct today. The proposal is silent on `partial`, but the implementation is not ambiguous. The work item for `closed` therefore reduces to an optional test.

The load-bearing correction is in the proposed change for unions. Copying the source case list into the generated part, which the finding proposes, would itself produce a compilation error: Roslyn permits the case list on at most one partial part, through the same DeclarationWithParameters mechanism that records use, and reports CS8863 on any further part that carries one. The generated part must pass a null parameter list, which is both representable in the syntax model and parseable.

The last correction is nomenclature that follows the FACTS addendum: the union syntax API is present but experimental in stable 5.9.0 and in the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3, and only the move to the stable Roslyn 5.12 removes the experimental markers, so the conditional compilation symbol should be named after the renumbered latest variant rather than after 5.10.

One scope remark that is not a defect of the finding. No Roslyn that Metalama consumes today exposes C# 15 as a non-preview language version, and Metalama's own language version plumbing stops at C# 14, so the union failure is reachable only after the language version work of the release lands. That ordering affects when the fix is needed, not whether the finding is true.

Two items of the source Roslyn API delta report that were listed as unverified are now settled. Whether a partial declaration of a closed class must repeat the modifier: it must not, and it need not. Whether the ParameterSyntax entries of a union case list carry an identifier: they are parsed with identifierIsOptional set to true, and at least one parameter is required when the parenthesized list is present (Parser/LanguageParser.cs:4851-4862).

corrections.proposed_change: Detect a union in CreatePartialType from the primary declaration syntax kind (SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration), resolved as in DT-1, and emit a union part. Do not use ITypeSymbol.IsUnion as the discriminator: Roslyn defines it as NamedTypeSymbol.IsUnionType (PublicModel/TypeSymbol.cs:205), which is IsUnionDeclaration || HasUnionAttribute for a source type (SourceNamedTypeSymbol.cs:1463-1469) over TypeKind Class or Struct (NamedTypeSymbol.cs:1944-1949), so a source type declared as a struct or a class and marked with the union attribute reports IsUnion == true; emitting a union part for it would produce the same CS0261 in the opposite direction. SyntaxFactory.UnionDeclaration is absent from Roslyn 5.0.0 and is experimental in the consumed 5.10 preview, so build the part from text with SyntaxFactory.ParseMemberDeclaration using the parse options of the compilation (the generator already reuses them at lines 54-57; the parser gates the union keyword on IsFeatureEnabled(IDS_FeatureUnions), so those options are required), then apply the modifiers, type parameter list, base list, braces and members through the TypeDeclarationSyntax base class, whose With* accessors are in the Roslyn 5.0 shipped public API, so that UnionDeclarationSyntax is never named. Alternatively route through the generated syntax factory of eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter once the stable grammar no longer strips the node. notes:
The central claim is confirmed in full. CreatePartialType has no union arm, a union symbol reaches the TypeKind.Struct arm at line 749 because Roslyn maps DeclarationKind.Union to TypeKind.Struct and reports IsRecord as false, and the emitted partial struct part cannot merge with the union part because the merge identity of SingleTypeDeclaration includes the declaration kind. The resulting diagnostic is CS0261, whose message text explicitly enumerates unions, which is direct confirmation that the compiler treats a union part and a struct part as a kind conflict. The statements about AddHeader, about the unreachable assertion arm at line 788, and about containment as LAMA0049 are all accurate, and the dependency on DT-1 is real: SyntaxKindExtensions.IsTypeDeclaration excludes UnionDeclaration, so SourceNamedTypeImpl.IsPartial returns false for a partial union and the generator returns early with LAMA0048 before reaching CreatePartialType.

Two details required correction, both in the proposed change and its open question.

First, the alternative discriminator suggested by the finding, a new INamedType.IsUnion fed by ITypeSymbol.IsUnion, is over-broad. Roslyn defines ITypeSymbol.IsUnion through NamedTypeSymbol.IsUnionType, which for a source type is IsUnionDeclaration or the presence of the union attribute, over any type whose kind is Class or Struct. A source type written as a struct or a class and carrying that attribute therefore reports IsUnion == true while its declaration is a struct or a class declaration. Keying the generator on that property would emit a union part for such a type and reintroduce CS0261 in the other direction. Only the primary declaration syntax kind is a correct discriminator, which is the other option the finding already offers.

Second, the open question is answerable from the compiler source and resolves in favour of the simpler design. Roslyn records at most one declaration with a parameter list per merged type and reports ERR_MultipleRecordParameterLists for any further one, and it takes the union case types from that single part. A generated part that omits the case-type list is therefore correct and required, and the code model does not need to expose the case types.

One further point supports the feasibility of the proposal in both Roslyn variants: TypeDeclarationSyntax already exposes WithMembers, WithModifiers, WithOpenBraceToken, WithCloseBraceToken, WithBaseList and WithTypeParameterList in the Roslyn 5.0 shipped public API, so a skeleton parsed from text can be completed without ever naming UnionDeclarationSyntax and without suppressing the experimental attribute. The parser gates the union keyword on the language feature, so reusing the compilation parse options is not merely convenient but necessary.

A minor nuance on the consequence: the diagnostic location is the first location of whichever conflicting symbol Roslyn visits second in declaration order, so the error can surface on the user's own union declaration rather than on the generated document. This does not change the consequence class, which remains a reported diagnostic rather than a silent failure or a crash.

Size M is appropriate and unchanged.

corrections.proposed_change: Keep the proposal, with four corrections. (1) There is no interim mapping. evidence:
Every external premise of CM-4 is true; three of them need a correction that the finding survives, and the open question is answerable.

CONFIRMED PREMISES.

1. `closed` is a C# 15 modifier gated on the language version. `ERR_FeatureNotAvailableInVersion15 = 9399` exists in dotnet/roslyn main `src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Errors/ErrorCode.cs:2511`, and the modifier is checked through `MessageID.IDS_FeatureClosedClasses` (`src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/Source/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:534`, downloaded copy line 534). FACTS.md:31 and the delta report 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:117 state the same.

2. A closed class is implicitly abstract, and an explicit `abstract` is an error. `SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:398-402` (downloaded copy): `case TypeKind.Class: if ((mods & DeclarationModifiers.Closed) != 0) mods |= DeclarationModifiers.Abstract;`. The rejection is at `SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:374-381`: `if ((mods & DeclarationModifiers.Closed) != 0) { if ((mods & (Sealed | Static)) != 0) diagnostics.Add(ErrorCode.ERR_ClosedSealedStatic, ...); if ((mods & DeclarationModifiers.Abstract) != 0) diagnostics.Add(ErrorCode.ERR_ClosedExplicitlyAbstract, ...); }`.

3. The error name and code cited by the finding are exact. `ErrorCode.cs:2489-2493` gives `ERR_ClosedTypeNameDisallowed = 9380`, `ERR_ClosedSealedStatic = 9381`, `ERR_ClosedBaseTypeBaseFromOtherAssembly = 9382`, `ERR_UnderspecifiedClosedSubtype = 9383`, `ERR_ClosedExplicitlyAbstract = 9384`. The message in `src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/CSharpResources.resx:8369-8371` is "'{0}': a closed type cannot be marked abstract because it is always implicitly abstract." So the predicted `abstract closed class` output is indeed rejected, with exactly that diagnostic.

4. The premise that `closed` does not apply to structs or interfaces holds. `SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:327-354` adds `DeclarationModifiers.Closed` only in `case TypeKind.Class: case TypeKind.Submission:`; the `TypeKind.Struct`, `TypeKind.Interface` and `TypeKind.Delegate` arms do not add it, and `TypeKind.Extension` allows no modifier at all. The proposal (proposals/csharp-15.0/closed-hierarchies.md, "Syntax") says "Allow `closed` as a modifier on classes. A `closed` class is implicitly abstract. Thus, it cannot also have a `sealed` or `static` modifier. It is an error to explicitly use an `abstract` modifier on a `closed` class." Closed interfaces are listed under "Optional features", not in the C# 15 design.

5. The Metalama-side mechanism the finding predicts is real. `Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CodeModel/Helpers/ModifierHelper.cs:223-232` emits `abstract` from `if ( namedType.IsAbstract && namedType.TypeKind != TypeKind.Interface )` and `sealed` from `if ( namedType.IsSealed )`, so an `IsAbstract` that returned true for a closed type would produce `abstract closed class` and CS9384.

6. The reason given for not introducing unions holds. `ErrorCode.cs:2475` has `ERR_UnionDeclarationNeedsCaseTypes = 9370`, and 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:108 records that the case types are the `ParameterList` of `UnionDeclarationSyntax`, which the builder model has no counterpart for.

7. Validating `TypeKind is Class` in the setter is consistent with Roslyn, because Metalama's `TypeKind.Class` covers record classes: `Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework/Code/TypeKind.cs:27-30` marks `RecordClass` obsolete in favour of "TypeKind.Class and INamedType.IsRecord".

CORRECTED PREMISES.

A. "Closed applies to classes only" must not be read as excluding record classes. Roslyn's allowed-modifier computation excludes only `Static` for records (`SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:329-337`), so `Closed` is allowed on a record class, and the very first example of the proposal is `public closed record class GateState;` (closed-hierarchies.md, "Summary"). The conclusion of the finding is unaffected: the property still belongs on `INamedTypeBuilder` and not on `IMemberOrNamedTypeBuilder`, and Metalama's builder rejects records for an unrelated reason.

B. `SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword` cannot be named unconditionally in engine code. On branch `release/dev18.0` (Roslyn 5.0, the lower variant that serves Rider per FACTS.md:11), `src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Syntax/SyntaxKind.cs` ends the contextual keyword block at `ExtensionKeyword = 8451`; there is no `ClosedKeyword`. In the stable 5.9.0 and in the consumed `5.10.0-1.26365.3` the value exists but carries `[RSEXPERIMENTAL006]` (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:58 and :90; FACTS.md:53), which is a compile-time error unless suppressed. FACTS.md:56 states the general rule: "every engine reference to the union or closed API must be gated to the latest variant, because the Roslyn 5.0 variant that serves Rider does not have it."

C. corrections.what_happens_today: The public API has IntroduceClass and IntroduceInterface; there is no IntroduceStruct, IntroduceRecord or IntroduceUnion, and NamedTypeBuilder rejects records by assertion. A closed class cannot be introduced because no builder property exists. If IsClosed were added by copying IsAbstract, ModifierHelper.GetTypeSyntaxModifierList would emit `abstract closed class`, which Roslyn rejects with ERR_ClosedExplicitlyAbstract (CS9384, "a closed type cannot be marked abstract because it is always implicitly abstract"). Independently of that, the `closed` modifier cannot be emitted at all before Metalama consumes a Roslyn that exposes SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword without the experimental marker, and before the language version plumbing reaches C# 15.
corrections.proposed_change: Add `bool IsClosed { get; set; }` to INamedTypeBuilder (the modifier applies to classes only, so not to IMemberOrNamedTypeBuilder; note that Roslyn allows it on record classes as well, so the restriction is against structs, interfaces, enums and delegates, not against records). Validate in the setter that TypeKind is Class and that IsSealed and IsStatic are false, mirroring ERR_ClosedSealedStatic, and make IsAbstract read true when IsClosed is true, mirroring the implicit abstractness that Roslyn applies in SourceMemberContainerSymbol.MakeModifiers. Store it in NamedTypeBuilderData and expose it in IntroducedNamedType. In GetTypeSyntaxModifierList, emit the `closed` token and skip `abstract` when the type is closed, because an explicit `abstract` is ERR_ClosedExplicitlyAbstract. Place `closed` before `partial`: ModifierUtils.reportMisplacedPartialModifier requires `partial` to be the last modifier, so `partial closed class` is CS0267 and `closed partial class` is the only valid order. The token itself cannot be written as `SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword` in shared engine code: the value does not exist in Roslyn 5.0, which serves the lower variant, and it is marked RSEXPERIMENTAL006 in the consumed 5.10 preview and in the stable 5.9.0, so either gate the emission to the latest Roslyn variant or write the numeric value with a cast and suppress the experimental diagnostic, in the same way the report notes for LanguageVersion 1500. Finally, guard the feature at run time: emitting `closed` requires the target compilation to provide System.Runtime.CompilerServices.IsClosedTypeAttribute and CompilerFeatureRequiredAttribute, which the compiler does not embed, and requires the user language version to be C# 15, so an introduced closed class must be diagnosed rather than emitted when either prerequisite is missing. Do not add union introduction for 2027.0: record introduction is not supported either, and a union declaration requires a non-empty case list (ERR_UnionDeclarationNeedsCaseTypes, CS9370) carried in the ParameterList of UnionDeclarationSyntax, for which the builder has no model.
corrections.consequence_class: No impact today (the feature is absent). For the future implementation: a compiler error in transformed user code if ModifierHelper is not adapted (CS9384), a build break of the Roslyn 5.0 variant if SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword is named unconditionally, and a missing well-known member error if the target framework does not provide IsClosedTypeAttribute.

notes:
The finding is sound and its central claim is exact: Roslyn makes a closed class implicitly abstract and rejects an explicit `abstract` with ERR_ClosedExplicitlyAbstract, which is the failure mode the finding predicts for a naive IsClosed implementation.

Three additions were made. First, the open question is now closed: `partial` must be the last modifier, so the order is `closed partial class`. Second, the emission of the token is not free, because the Roslyn 5.0 variant has no ClosedKeyword and the 5.9/5.10 builds mark it experimental; this ties the item to the move to the stable Roslyn described in the FACTS addendum. Third, a closed class declaration requires two well-known attributes that the compiler does not synthesize, which is a run-time prerequisite of an introduced closed class rather than a compile-time concern of the engine.

Two points were not verified. The exact synthesis of `[CompilerFeatureRequired("ClosedClasses")]` on the constructors of a closed class was not located in the sources read; only the well-known member lookup at SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:1979-1980 was seen, and the delta report records the same limitation. Whether every partial declaration of a closed class must repeat the `closed` modifier is still unresolved; the proposal does not discuss `partial`, and this matters for the design-time partial documents that Metalama generates.

The finding's ordering of the release timeline is consistent with the FACTS addendum: the closed-class API is unusable in a non-preview language version until Metalama consumes Roslyn 5.12, so this item cannot be delivered ahead of the C# 15 language-version plumbing.

evidence:
Central mechanism confirmed. (1) The inlined body is emitted verbatim and flattened into the caller statement list: Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Linking/Substitution/InliningSubstitution.cs:34 (Substitute), :51-53 (GetSubstitutedBody), :57 (statements.Add(inlinedBody)), :71-72 (the result carries LinkerGeneratedFlags.FlattenableBlock); Linking/LinkerRewritingDriver.cs:73 and :105-111, :137-147, :160, :195, :202 (every return path of GetSubstitutedBody carries FlattenableBlock); Linking/LinkerLinkingStep.CleanupBodyRewriter.cs:93-97 and :194-208 (AddFlattenedBlockStatements splices flattenable blocks, recursively, into the enclosing statement list, unconditionally, with no dependency on formatting options). (2) No component renames user labels: a grep of LabeledStatement under Linking/ returns only LexicalScopeFactory.Visitor.cs:86-91, LinkerLinkingStep.CleanupBodyRewriter.cs:135-152, LinkerAnalysisStep.SemanticBodyAnalyzer.cs:181,330, LinkerLinkingStep.RemoveTrivialLabelRewriter.cs:53-54, Substitution/InliningSubstitution.cs:63-68 and Substitution/BlockWithReturnBeforeUsingLocalSubstitution.cs:170-176, none of which rewrites a user label identifier. (3) Template labels reach the target verbatim: Templating/TemplateCompilerRewriter.cs:390-441 renames only declarations whose symbol satisfies IsLocalSymbol, and IsLocalSymbol at :491-497 accepts only local functions, anonymous functions, locals, parameters and type parameters, so an ILabelSymbol declaration falls through to the "symbol reference" path at :438-441 and the identifier is serialized unchanged. (4) Templates may contain a labeled statement and may not contain goto: Templating/TemplateAnnotator.cs has no VisitLabeledStatement override, and VisitGotoStatement at :2601-2606 reports TemplatingDiagnosticDescriptors.LanguageFeatureIsNotSupported, which is LAMA0101 with Error severity (Templating/TemplatingDiagnosticDescriptors.cs:24-30). (5) The behaviour is pinned by an existing baseline: Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Metalama.Framework.Tests.LinkerTests/Tests/Methods/Overrides/TargetBody/UsingLocal_Jump.cs:24,27 declares a user label myLabel in the target body, and UsingLocal_Jump.t.cs:32,34 shows it copied verbatim into the body of the override after inlining. Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Metalama.Framework.Tests.AspectTests/Tests/Aspects/Overrides/Methods/MultipleAspects.t.cs:5-11 shows two aspect templates and the original body merged into one flat block of a single method.

Refuted details. (a) The parenthetical claim that two copies of the same template are never inlined into one method is wrong. The "exactly once" rule counts references to one semantic, not expansions of one template: Linking/LinkerAnalysisStep.InlineabilityAnalyzer.cs:165-174 obtains the reachable references of a single semantic and requires Count == 1. Each override method is a separate semantic, so a chain of overrides is inlined into one method, as Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Metalama.Framework.Tests.LinkerTests/Tests/Methods/Overrides/TemplateBody/LocalFunction_ComplexFlow.t.cs and MultipleAspects.t.cs both show. Two overrides produced from the same template therefore land in one block, and their labels collide exactly as a template label and a target label would. (b) The claim that LexicalScopeFactory.Visitor makes the linker labels __aspect_return_N, epilogue and postBase unique is only half right: __aspect_return_N comes from a plain counter at Linking/Inlining/InliningAnalysisContext.cs:45-53 and never passes through a lexical scope; only epilogue and postBase do (Linking/LinkerInjectionStep.Rewriter.cs:921-922). (c) The proposed allocation mechanism is not reachable where the change would be made. LexicalScopeFactory is constructed at Linking/LinkerInjectionStep.cs:75 from the final compilation model and is passed only to the injection step and to Pipeline/DesignTime/DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs:59; a grep of GetLexicalScope shows no use in the analysis or linking steps. In addition, TemplateLexicalScope is documented as intentionally single-threaded (Templating/TemplateLexicalScope.cs:13-17) while substitutions are generated concurrently (Linking/LinkerAnalysisStep.SubstitutionGenerator.cs:339 and :530).

Open question answered. The template compiler does not preserve BreakStatementSyntax.Name. eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1296 and :1307 declare the Name field of BreakStatementSyntax and ContinueStatementSyntax with ExperimentalUrl; eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Model/TreeReader.cs:19,35-43,55-57 removes every experimental field before generation; eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Generator.cs:425-440 generates each Transform method from the remaining fields only, so the node is rebuilt without the Name. corrections.what_happens_today: A label is useful only as the target of a goto statement, and a template may not contain a goto statement, so in practice no template body carries a label. With C# 15, `outer: foreach (...) { ... break outer; }` becomes an ordinary idiom, and a labeled statement is already accepted in a template today, because TemplateAnnotator overrides VisitGotoStatement (Templating/TemplateAnnotator.cs:2601-2606, reporting LAMA0101 with Error severity) and has no VisitLabeledStatement override. A template label is emitted into the target verbatim: Templating/TemplateCompilerRewriter.cs:390-441 renames only declarations whose symbol satisfies IsLocalSymbol, and IsLocalSymbol (:491-497) accepts locals, parameters, type parameters, local functions and anonymous functions, so a label symbol is not renamed. The linker then merges bodies into one statement list: InliningSubstitution.cs:34-72 returns the inlined body inside a block flagged FlattenableBlock, LinkerRewritingDriver.cs:73-160 flags every substituted body the same way, and LinkerLinkingStep.CleanupBodyRewriter.cs:93-97 and 194-208 splice those blocks, recursively and unconditionally, into the enclosing statement list. No substitution renames a user label; a grep of LabeledStatement under Linking/ finds only CleanupBodyRewriter, SemanticBodyAnalyzer, RemoveTrivialLabelRewriter, LexicalScopeFactory.Visitor and BlockWithReturnBeforeUsingLocalSubstitution, and none of them rewrites a label identifier. Two labels of the same name therefore end up in one block after flattening (CS0140), or one label shadows a label of a contained scope when the inlined body remains inside a nested block, for example the block that the using-local rewrite introduces (CS0158). The collision arises in two equally realistic configurations. The first is a template label against a label of the target body; LinkerTests Methods/Overrides/TargetBody/UsingLocal_Jump.cs:24,27 and its baseline .t.cs:32,34 show a user label of the target copied verbatim into the override after inlining. The second is a template label against itself, when two overrides are chained: the inlineability rule counts the references to one semantic, not the expansions of one template (LinkerAnalysisStep.InlineabilityAnalyzer.cs:165-174 requires exactly one reachable reference to the semantic), so each override is a separate semantic and a chain of overrides is inlined into a single method, as AspectTests Aspects/Overrides/Methods/MultipleAspects.t.cs:5-11 shows. Two aspects that expand the same template, or the same aspect applied twice, therefore place two copies of the same label in one block. For completeness, the lexical scope collects user label identifiers (LexicalScopeFactory.Visitor.cs:86-91) only so that names allocated through it do not collide with them; among the labels the linker generates itself, only `epilogue` and `postBase` are allocated that way (LinkerInjectionStep.Rewriter.cs:921-922), while `__aspect_return_N` comes from a private counter (Inlining/InliningAnalysisContext.cs:45-53).
corrections.proposed_change: Rename the labels of the inlined body when it is spliced into the caller. The natural place is InliningSubstitution.Substitute (Linking/Substitution/InliningSubstitution.cs:34-72), which already holds the substituted body, or a dedicated rewriter invoked from there; a new SyntaxNodeSubstitution is a poor fit, because a substitution is keyed on a single pre-registered node while the rename has to cover a whole body. Do not allocate the new names through LexicalScopeFactory.GetLexicalScope(destination).GetUniqueIdentifier: LexicalScopeFactory is constructed in the injection step (LinkerInjectionStep.cs:75) and is not available to the analysis or linking steps, and TemplateLexicalScope is documented as intentionally single-threaded (TemplateLexicalScope.cs:13-17) whereas substitutions are generated concurrently (LinkerAnalysisStep.SubstitutionGenerator.cs:339, 530). Follow instead the precedent of the return label and derive the new name from the inlining context, for example from the counter of InliningAnalysisContext.cs:45-53 or from InliningSpecification.ContextIdentifier, which is deterministic and thread-safe. The rewrite has to cover LabeledStatementSyntax.Identifier, GotoStatementSyntax.Expression (user goto statements do occur in a target body, as UsingLocal_Jump shows, and the linker emits its own goto statements to __aspect_return_N), and the Name of BreakStatementSyntax and ContinueStatementSyntax. The last two members do not exist in Roslyn 5.0.0 (eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Syntax-5.0.0.xml declares neither), so the rewrite must not name them: override VisitIdentifierName on a CSharpSyntaxRewriter and act when the parent is of kind BreakStatement or ContinueStatement, which compiles unchanged against both Roslyn variants and is inert under the 5.0 variant, where such syntax cannot be parsed. A smaller alternative worth measuring first is to leave the syntax alone and refuse the inlining when the inlined body and the destination body declare a label of the same name, by treating the semantic as not inlineable in LinkerAnalysisStep.InlineabilityAnalyzer.cs; that produces a call instead of an error and needs no new rewriting. Either way, add linker tests Methods/Overrides/Labels/* covering a labeled loop in the override only, in the target only, in both, and in two chained overrides expanded from the same template. Note separately that a template written with `break outer;` currently loses its label before this collision can matter, because TreeReader.RemoveExperimentalDeclarations (eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Model/TreeReader.cs:35-43, 55-57) strips the experimental Name field declared at Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1296 and :1307, and Generator.cs:425-440 rebuilds each node from the remaining fields only.

notes:
The central claim survives an adversarial reading: the linker copies user labels verbatim into a flattened statement list, nothing renames them, the template compiler does not rename them either, and an existing baseline (UsingLocal_Jump.t.cs) shows a user label being copied through an inlining. The consequence class is right as stated: the failure is a C# error on the transformed compilation (CS0140 for a duplicate label in one block, CS0158 when the inlined body stays in a nested block), not a crash, an assertion or a Metalama diagnostic. No assertion fires on the path: InliningSubstitution and CleanupBodyRewriter treat a LabeledStatementSyntax like any other statement.

Three details were wrong and are corrected above. The most consequential is the parenthetical about "exactly once", which understated the exposure: the rule counts references to a semantic, so two overrides expanded from the same template are chained and inlined into one method, and the same template's label then appears twice. The second is the attribution of __aspect_return_N to the lexical scope. The third is the proposed allocation mechanism, which is not reachable from the linking step and is not thread-safe there.

Two further observations for the parent agent. First, the linker test LocalFunction_ComplexFlow.t.cs produces two nested local functions of the same name, which would not compile; that is an artefact of the linker test harness, whose pseudo-templates are hand-written C# and therefore bypass the run-time symbol renaming of TemplateCompilerRewriter. It is not evidence that local functions collide in the real pipeline, and it does not weaken the label claim, because labels bypass that renaming in the real pipeline as well. Second, the finding's own open question is answered from the generator source rather than left open: the experimental Name field of BreakStatementSyntax and ContinueStatementSyntax is removed before code generation, so a run-time `break outer;` in a template is currently rebuilt as a plain `break;`. That is an independent defect worth its own finding; it lowers the practical urgency of LK-9 slightly, because the canonical C# 15 idiom is already broken in templates for a different reason, but it does not affect the collision itself, which depends only on the labeled statement.

Premise A, the consequence class NETSDK1045, is confirmed. In dotnet/sdk, `src/Tasks/Common/Resources/Strings.resx` defines the resource `UnsupportedTargetFrameworkVersion` as "NETSDK1045: The current .NET SDK does not support targeting {0} {1}.", and `src/Tasks/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks/targets/Microsoft.NET.TargetFrameworkInference.targets:195-197` raises it through `NETSdkError` under the condition `'$(_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV)' > '$(NETCoreAppMaximumVersion)'` with the arguments `.NET;$(_TargetFrameworkVersionWithoutV);$(NETCoreAppMaximumVersion)`. Under a 10.0.4xx SDK, `NETCoreAppMaximumVersion` is 10.0, so a project that adds `net11.0` fails there, before any targeting pack is resolved.

Premise B, that pinning an 11.0.x SDK in `global.json` makes the default `LangVersion` C# 15, is only partly true and is attributed to the wrong component. The .NET SDK contains no per-target-framework `LangVersion` default. A grep of the local copies of `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.props`, `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.targets`, `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.CSharp.props` and `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.BeforeCommon.targets` from dotnet/sdk main returns no occurrence of `LangVersion`, and a GitHub code search for `LangVersion` under `src/Tasks/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks/targets` returns only `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Common.targets:45-46` (`<LangVersion>Preview</LangVersion>` when `EnablePreviewFeatures` is true and `IsNetCoreAppTargetingLatestTFM` is true) and a pass-through in `Microsoft.NET.PreserveCompilationContext.targets`. A search for `_MaxSupportedLangVersion` in dotnet/sdk returns nothing.

The default is computed by the compiler toolset. In dotnet/roslyn, `src/Compilers/Core/MSBuildTask/Microsoft.CSharp.Core.targets` sets `_MaxSupportedLangVersion` to 7.3 for target frameworks below .NET Core 3.0 and .NET Standard 2.1 (lines 8-9), to 8.0 for .NET Core below 5.0 (lines 12-14), and to `9 + (major - 5)` for `.NETCoreApp` (lines 23-24), which gives 14.0 for `net10.0` and 15.0 for `net11.0`; lines 26-29 then cap the result at `_MaxAvailableLangVersion`, and line 32 assigns it to `LangVersion` only when the user has not set one.

The cap depends on the Roslyn version, which is what makes the finding's statement conditional. `_MaxAvailableLangVersion` is 14.0 on `release/dev18.0` (Roslyn 5.0), on `release/dev18.3` (5.3), at commit `35d9211b841e7613c1d2f8f5af6d628ace696c4c` (the 5.9.0 stable commit) and at commit `27d6bed68b458350aca01f91397fa8be9605d47b` (2026-07-28, the end of the 5.10 window that contains the consumed `5.10.0-1.26365.3`), all at line 27 of that file. It is 15.0 at commit `fb723b29b175828bf666ed995a2ccaf0fb41e1ad` (2026-08-25, the 5.11 window) and on `main` (5.12). The change therefore falls between 2026-07-28 and 2026-08-25, which brackets the commit "Add C# 15 language version (#84799)" of 2026-08-11 identified by the Roslyn API delta report (08-roslyn-api-delta.md, summary item 3 and the table row for `LanguageVersion.CSharp15`).

Add an `11.0.x` variant of the two docker scenarios that pin `10.0.302`. Read the `MSBuildExtensionsPath` note of `CLAUDE.md` first: two feature bands in one image were the cause of `MSB4062`.

The language-version part of the original proposal needs three corrections.

First, `global.json` does not decide the default `LangVersion`, and the trade-off between 10.0.400 and 11.0.x that the finding describes does not exist. The .NET SDK carries no per-target-framework language default; its only assignment is `Preview` under `EnablePreviewFeatures` (`Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Common.targets:45-46`). The default is computed by the compiler toolset in `Microsoft.CSharp.Core.targets`, which derives `_MaxSupportedLangVersion` from the project's target framework (lines 8-14 and 23-24: `net472` and `netstandard2.0` give 7.3, `net10.0` gives 14.0, `net11.0` gives 15.0), caps it at `_MaxAvailableLangVersion` (lines 26-29) and assigns it to `LangVersion` only when the user has not set one (line 32). Moreover, if any project in the repository targets `net11.0`, the SDK must be 11.0.x, because 10.0.400 fails with NETSDK1045; there is no option to keep 10.0.400 in that case.

Second, the rewrite at `Metalama.Framework.targets:118-120` is not triggered by the compiler that the repository consumes today. `_MaxAvailableLangVersion` is 14.0 in Roslyn 5.0, 5.3, the 5.9.0 stable commit and the whole 5.10 window, and 15.0 only from the 5.11 window onward and on `main` (5.12). With a Metalama.Compiler based on the consumed `5.10.0-1.26365.3`, a `net11.0` project that does not set `LangVersion` receives 14.0, which is in the allowed list of the condition at line 118, so neither the rewrite to 12.0 nor the `MetalamaCheckLangVersion` warning occurs. The rewrite becomes real only after Metalama.Compiler is rebased on Roslyn 5.11 or later, in practice on the 5.12 that the .NET 11 SDK carries (`dotnet/sdk` `eng/Version.Details.props:80` pins `Microsoft.Net.Compilers.Toolset` 5.12.0-1.26452.110). This makes the language-version work a consequence of the compiler rebase, and it should be tracked with that item rather than with the container change.

Third, the scope is narrower than stated. Only projects whose target framework is `net11.0` are concerned, not "every standalone scenario that does not set LangVersion": `net10.0` stays at 14.0, `netstandard2.0` at 8.0 and `net472` at 7.3 under any of these toolsets. Note also that `LangVersionImplicitlySet` is a Metalama.Compiler property and does not exist in dotnet/roslyn, so the exact value depends on the fork, which was not read because Metalama.Compiler is not cloned.

The remaining open question is therefore only whether PostSharp.Engineering 2023.2.420 exposes a Visual Studio 2027 Build Tools component version, and whether a release candidate SDK is acceptable in the image until general availability.
