corrections.what_happens_today: `RunTimeCodeHasher` and `CompileTimeCodeHasher` are generated with one `Visit<Node>` override per grammar node, and the generator strips every node and field that carries `ExperimentalUrl` (in the consumed grammar: `UnionDeclarationSyntax`, `WithElementSyntax`, `UnsafeExpressionSyntax`, and the `Name` field of `BreakStatementSyntax` and `ContinueStatementSyntax`). Two consequences follow. First, `UnionDeclarationSyntax` has no override, so `CSharpSyntaxWalker.DefaultVisit` runs; the walker is constructed with `SyntaxWalkerDepth.Node` (`SafeSyntaxWalker.cs:39`), and `DefaultVisit` calls `VisitToken` only when the depth is at least `SyntaxWalkerDepth.Token`, so the union identifier, its modifiers and the `union` keyword contribute nothing to the hash, while the case types (the `ParameterList`), the base list and the members still do. Second, the generated `VisitBreakStatement` and `VisitContinueStatement` hash only the attribute lists, the keyword and the semicolon, because the `Name` field was removed before generation, so the label of a labeled `break` or `continue` is never hashed even by `CompileTimeCodeHasher`, which otherwise hashes bodies. `DiffStrategy.IsDifferent` treats an equal hash as no change (lines 80-85), so the pipeline is not re-run. Observable effects: renaming a union, or adding `partial` to it in response to LAMA0048, in a file with no other change does not trigger re-analysis, so the stale result and the stale LAMA0048 persist until an unrelated edit; changing the target label of `break` or `continue` inside a template does not rebuild the compile-time project, so the template keeps its previous behaviour at design time. Separately, `PartialTypesVisitor` and `PartialTypesHasher` override only class, struct and record, so a partial union is never listed in `SyntaxTreeVersion.PartialTypes` and the partial-type invalidation of `SyntaxTreeChange.cs:111` and `DiffStrategy.cs:97-150` does not cover unions, whereas `DependencyCollector.cs:63-64` does register unions because it tests `BaseTypeDeclarationSyntax`. Reachability today: in the Roslyn build the repository consumes, and in the stable 5.9.0, unions and labeled break or continue are preview features (`MessageID.RequiredVersion` returns `LanguageVersion.Preview` for `IDS_FeatureUnions` and `IDS_FeatureLabeledBreakContinue`), so this syntax parses only under `LanguageVersion.Preview`; the gap becomes reachable from ordinary C# 15 source once the repository moves to a Roslyn in which those features are gated on `LanguageVersion.CSharp15`.
corrections.proposed_change: Perform the correction as part of the move to the next stable Roslyn, which is 5.12 and not 5.10: no stable 5.10 or 5.11 package exists, and the `ExperimentalUrl` and `[RSEXPERIMENTAL006]` markers on the union node, the with-element node and the break and continue `Name` field were removed by dotnet/roslyn commit #84799 of 2026-08-11, together with the introduction of `LanguageVersion.CSharp15`. Following `updating-roslyn.md` steps 4 and 5, add the new grammar as `eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Syntax-5.12.0.xml`, copied from the `Metalama.Compiler` branch that targets that Roslyn, and register the version in the list at `GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:18`; do not overwrite `Syntax-5.10.0.xml`, because the document forbids reusing the previous version's file and the version checker derives from it. The union node and the break and continue `Name` field carry no `ExperimentalUrl` in that grammar, so the generator emits the missing overrides and hashes the missing field. Because the hasher is generated per Roslyn version (`GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:37, :46-47`), the corrected hashers exist only in the variant built from the new grammar, so add `VisitUnionDeclaration` overrides to `PartialTypesVisitor` and `PartialTypesHasher` under the same variant constraint as DT-1: either a `DefaultVisit` that tests the resolved kind, or an override in a file compiled for the latest variant only, which is a policy exception to record. Add a `DiffStrategy` unit test that renames a union and changes a `break` label and asserts that the hash changes. The test can run before the Roslyn move if it parses with `LanguageVersion.Preview`, under which both features already parse in the consumed build; if it is written against C# 15 instead, guard it with `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse("15.0")`, which fails on the consumed Roslyn and succeeds from the 5.12 grammar onwards.

notes:
Every external premise except the Roslyn version number survives an attempt to refute it, so the finding stands with a correction rather than a refutation.

The false premise is the version identity. The finding names "the stable Roslyn 5.10" five times, in the title, the proposed change and the open question. No stable 5.10 exists, and none is expected: nuget.org serves 5.0.0, 5.3.0, 5.6.0 and 5.9.0, main is versioned 5.12, and the change that removes the experimental markers landed on 2026-08-11, inside the 5.11 window (FACTS.md:48-49; 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:15, :17, :90). Substituting 5.12 for 5.10 leaves the mechanism, the observable effects and the remedy untouched, so the finding survives.

The open question is answered and can be closed. On main, the only node that keeps ExperimentalUrl is UnsafeExpressionSyntax, whose feature MessageID.RequiredVersion deliberately holds at Preview until C# 16. The union node, the with-element node and the break and continue Name field lose the marker, so the repository policy that experimental features are unsupported (updating-roslyn.md:11) does not block this work, and DT-1 and DT-2 are not pointless for the release.

Three refutation attempts that failed. First, that CSharpSyntaxWalker.DefaultVisit might still reach tokens: the source shows VisitToken is called only when Depth is at least SyntaxWalkerDepth.Token, and the per-kind virtual members are generated as a call to DefaultVisit, so the finding's reasoning holds exactly as written. Second, that a union might not be allowed to be partial, which would remove the LAMA0048 scenario: the proposal grammar admits partial. Third, that the label of a labeled break might be stored somewhere the hasher already reaches, for example in a new SyntaxKind: it is stored only in the optional Name field, and no SyntaxKind is added.

Two smaller corrections folded into the corrected text. The generated VisitBreakStatement and VisitContinueStatement also hash the AttributeLists field, which the grammar declares on both nodes and which is not experimental, so "only the keyword and the semicolon" understates by one field; this does not affect the conclusion, because the label is still never hashed. And the proposed change asked to copy the stable grammar over Syntax-5.10.0.xml, which updating-roslyn.md step 4 explicitly forbids; the corrected text adds a new file and registers it instead.

Residual uncertainty, none of which changes the verdict. The 5.12 package does not exist yet, so its grammar is read from dotnet/roslyn main on 2026-09-04 and could still change before release. The Roslyn version of the .NET 11 GA software development kit is not published (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:268). Metalama.Compiler is not cloned, so the branch that will supply the new Syntax.xml was not inspected. The behaviour of the generated hashers was reasoned about from the grammar and the Roslyn walker source and was not executed, in keeping with the instruction not to build or run tests.

One scope observation for the parent agent. Because the syntax parses today under LanguageVersion.Preview while Metalama's pipeline rejects Preview unless AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures is set (FACTS.md:21), the stale-hash behaviour is currently reachable only in a preview-enabled project; it becomes ordinary behaviour once the language version work of the C# 15 support lands. The consequence class remains silent wrong output.

evidence:
The finding has four external premises. All four hold.

1. MSBuild `[MSBuild]::VersionGreaterThan` compares through `SimpleVersion`, and `SimpleVersion` treats missing components as zero.
- dotnet/msbuild `src/Build/Evaluation/IntrinsicFunctions.cs` (found through GitHub code search on the default branch): `public static bool VersionGreaterThan(string a, string b) { return SimpleVersion.Parse(a) > SimpleVersion.Parse(b); }`.
- dotnet/msbuild `src/Build/Utilities/SimpleVersion.cs` (fetched from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/msbuild/main/src/Build/Utilities/SimpleVersion.cs`): the type summary reads "Simple replacement for System.Version used to implement version comparison intrinsic property functions. Allows major version only (e.g. \"3\" is 3.0.0.0), ignores leading 'v' (e.g. \"v3.0\" is 3.0.0.0)", and the documentation states "Treats unspecified components as 0 (e.g. x == x.0 == x.0.0 == x.0.0.0)". The constructor is `public SimpleVersion(int major, int minor = 0, int build = 0, int revision = 0)`, and `CompareTo` compares Major, then Minor, then Build, then Revision.
- dotnet/msbuild `src/Build.UnitTests/Evaluation/SimpleVersion_Tests.cs` (fetched from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/msbuild/main/src/Build.UnitTests/Evaluation/SimpleVersion_Tests.cs`) contains the case `(new SimpleVersion(1, 2), new SimpleVersion(1, 2, 1), -1)`, that is, "1.2" is less than "1.2.1". This is the exact shape of "11.0" against "11.0.100", so `VersionGreaterThan("11.0.100", "11.0")` returns true and the LAMA0601 condition at `Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Package/build/Metalama.Framework.targets:412` is satisfied.

2. The .NET 11 SDK reports a three-component `NETCoreSdkVersion` whose third component is the feature band, so it is strictly greater than "11.0".
- The published .NET 11 SDK previews are numbered 11.0.100-preview.1.26104.118 through 11.0.100-preview.7.26381.103, and the general availability release is expected in November 2026 (dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/11.0, and dotnet/source-build discussion 5519 titled ".NET 11.0 Preview 2 March 2026 Update - .NET 11.0.0-preview.2 and SDK 11.0.100-preview.2"). The stable SDK is therefore 11.0.100 and later feature bands are 11.0.2xx and above.
- `Metalama.Framework.targets:399` computes `_MetalamaSdkVersion` as `$(NETCoreSdkVersion.Split('-')[0])`, which turns "11.0.100-preview.7.26381.103" into "11.0.100".
- That `NETCoreSdkVersion` is the full SDK version, and not a two-component number, is confirmed by the .NET SDK itself using it as a directory name: `src/Tasks/Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks/targets/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.FrameworkReferenceResolution.targets` builds `$(NetCoreRoot)\sdk\$(NETCoreSdkVersion)\PrunePackageData\`, and `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Common.targets` builds `$(NuGetPackageRoot)\microsoft.net.sdk.compilers.toolset\$(NETCoreSdkVersion)` (dotnet/sdk, GitHub code search).

3. The target framework rule does not have the same defect, because `$(TargetFrameworkVersion)` carries two components.
- The .NET SDK computes it as `<TargetFrameworkVersion>v$([MSBuild]::GetTargetFrameworkVersion('$(TargetFramework)', 2))</TargetFrameworkVersion>`, with an explicit version part count of 2 (`Microsoft.NET.TargetFrameworkInference.targets:55`, the copy captured at `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Metalama/ccf204f4-b0b3-5fe6-a8de-fe20f6791d2c/scratchpad/Microsoft.NET.TargetFrameworkInference.targets:55`). For `net11.0` the value is "v11.0", `Metalama.Framework.targets:322` trims the leading "v", and "11.0" against `MaximumNETCoreAppVersion` "11.0" (`Metalama.Framework.props:31`) is not greater. The minimum rules are safe for the same reason: "10.0.400" is not less than "10.0".

4. The .NET 11 SDK is in the supported set, so the diagnostic would reach supported users.
- `Metalama.Framework/docs/platform-support.md:195-197`: "The floor is the .NET 10 SDK. The .NET 11 SDK, released in November 2026, is also in the set."
- `Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Package/build/Metalama.Framework.props:38`: `<SupportedSdkVersionsDescription>The supported .NET SDK versions are 10.0 and 11.0.</SupportedSdkVersionsDescription>`.

The message text asserted by the finding matches `Metalama.Framework.targets:413`, which formats "'%(_MetalamaPlatformRequirement.Identity)' does not support the .NET SDK $(NETCoreSdkVersion), which is newer than %(_MetalamaPlatformRequirement.MaximumSdkVersion)."

No premise of this finding concerns C# 15 semantics, the csharplang proposals for C# 15, the Roslyn public API or the Roslyn version timeline, so the addendum of FACTS.md and the Roslyn API delta report do not bear on it.
notes:
Attempts to refute the finding, and their outcome.

The strongest refutation attempt was that `SimpleVersion` might right-pad the shorter operand to match the longer one, which would make "11.0" and "11.0.100" compare equal. The MSBuild unit test data refute that reading directly: `(new SimpleVersion(1, 2), new SimpleVersion(1, 2, 1), -1)`. Padding with zero is exactly what produces the defect, because it makes "11.0" equal to 11.0.0.0, which is less than 11.0.100.0.

This matters because another report in the same series states the opposite conclusion from the same premise and should be corrected. `Metalama.Framework/docs/2027.0/analysis-reports/01-language-version-and-hosts.md:32` records "`11.0.100` against `11.0`: no `LAMA0601`, on the reading that `[MSBuild]::VersionGreaterThan` pads missing components with zero", and the same claim is repeated at `01-language-version-and-hosts.md:206`. The premise is right and the inference from it is wrong. UT-2 is the correct reading and report 01 needs the correction.

Two secondary observations, neither of which changes the verdict.

First, the prerelease strip at `Metalama.Framework.targets:399` is redundant with respect to the comparison, because `SimpleVersion.Parse` already discards everything after a '-' or a '+' character. It remains useful for the diagnostic text, which prints `$(NETCoreSdkVersion)` unmodified, so there is no reason to remove it.

Second, one citation in the `where` list is off by two lines. The `Test.LegacySdk` requirement is at `Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Standalone/SupportedPlatform.ContributedRequirements/SupportedPlatform.ContributedRequirements.csproj:39-41`, with `<MaximumSdkVersion>1.0</MaximumSdkVersion>` on line 40, not at lines 41 to 43. The substance of the observation is correct: a maximum of "1.0" is far below the SDK of the build agent, so that scenario exercises the rule but not the boundary at which the defect appears. Every other citation is exact: `Metalama.Framework.props:33`, `Metalama.Framework.targets:399`, `Metalama.Framework.targets:412-413` and `Metalama.Framework.targets:322`.

On the proposed change, both variants work under the verified semantics. Comparing on the first two components of `NETCoreSdkVersion` restores the intended meaning of `MaximumSdkVersion`. The sentinel "11.0.99999" also works, because .NET SDK feature bands are three-digit values (100, 200, 300, 400) followed by a two-digit patch, so no released 11.0 SDK reaches that build number; it is the less readable of the two.

Note that LAMA0601 is emitted by a `<Warning>` task, so it is a warning rather than an error, but the repository builds with `TreatWarningsAsErrors` under `ContinuousIntegrationBuild`, and users commonly do the same, so the practical effect on a .NET 11 SDK is a failed build for anyone who does.

notes:
The finding survives. Its central external claim, that no Roslyn consumed today exposes C# 15 as a requestable language version and that a `@LanguageVersion(15.0)` test is therefore skipped rather than failed, is correct, and the evidence for it is now stronger than the finding states.

Six corrections, none of which overturns the finding.

1. The confidence caveat can be lifted. The finding says the absence of `CSharp15` from the July build is "inferred from the two dates, not from inspecting the build". The source at the end of the 5.10 window (commit 27d6bed6, 2026-07-28, which post-dates the 2026-07-15 build) has been read directly: no `CSharp15` member, no `TryParse` case for it, `IsValid` capped at `CSharp14`, and all six C# 15 features returning `LanguageVersion.Preview` from `MessageID.RequiredVersion`. The FACTS addendum reports the same from the shipped 5.9.0 assemblies.

2. "The stable Roslyn 5.10" does not exist. The FACTS addendum supersedes this, and the dating confirms why: the C# 15 commit of 2026-08-11 falls after the 5.10 window closed on 2026-07-28, so `CSharp15` first appeared in the 5.11 window, and the first stable release carrying it is 5.12. Step 1 of the proposed change, and the dependency on DT-8, must name 5.12.

3. The constant `ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER` is written literally in `eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.5.10.0.props:10`, not derived from a property, so the renumbering of the latest variant renames it by hand and every use must follow.

4. The guard of step 4 is wrong as specified and would fail on the current latest variant. Official Roslyn builds carry the assembly version `Major.Minor.0.0`, so the consumed `5.10.0-1.26365.3` reports 5.10.0.0 while lacking `CSharp15`. A version threshold is in any case a poor proxy, because the value appeared in the middle of a version window.

5. Step 2 must raise `Latest` and `All` per variant. `AllLanguageVersions` (a numeric cast) lets the shared source name 1500 under any Roslyn, but `LanguageVersionFacts.IsValid` of Roslyn 5.0 rejects 1500, so an unconditional raise would hand the Rider variant an invalid language version. Note that FACTS records zero `#if ROSLYN_*` blocks in production source, so this is the first place that would need a variant-dependent value; `ToLanguageVersion` already switches on `RoslynApiVersion` and is the natural place.

6. Two smaller attributions. The C# 14 language version of the aspect test project comes from `Metalama.Framework/Directory.Build.props:45-46` (`LangMaxVersion` 14.0), not from a .NET 10 SDK default; and that project multi-targets `net48;net10.0`, so an SDK-derived default would not be a single value. Separately, the parenthetical "valid on both variants since Metalama.Compiler compiles both" is false today: a `/langversion:15.0` that `TryParse` rejects is reported as CS1617, so this waits on Metalama.Compiler moving to a Roslyn that has `CSharp15`. Metalama.Compiler is not cloned in this session, so that remains an assumption.

The open question is answered. On Roslyn 5.12, `MapSpecifiedToEffectiveVersion` maps `Default`, `Latest` and `LatestMajor` to `CSharp15`. This does not decide the Metalama question, because `SupportedCSharpVersions.DefaultParseOptions` applies Metalama's own `Latest` constant rather than Roslyn's `LanguageVersion.Latest`: what tests without `@LanguageVersion` see is decided by step 2 alone.

One addition drawn from the csharplang proposal rather than a correction: a `partial union` is well formed (`unions.md:742`), which supports the claim that union partial parts are testable in a design-time scenario, but a union permits no instance field, auto-property or field-like event (`unions.md:750-752`), so what an aspect may introduce into such a partial part is restricted. That restriction deserves its own test rather than being assumed away.

notes:
Verdict: the proposed change is "None", and there is nothing to implement, so no pull request and no issue can already implement it. No open or merged work claims the opposite either, and I found no issue that scopes the closed modifier or patterns over unions in the template compiler.

Evidence that the finding's premise holds on the current branch.

1. The closed modifier introduces no syntax node. /home/user/Metalama/eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Syntax-5.10.0.xml declares only UnionDeclarationSyntax as a new type declaration (line 1954, with the kind UnionDeclaration at line 1955); there is no node or field for closed, which matches FACTS.md line 28 (ClosedKeyword is an existing SyntaxKind value). A grep of Metalama.Framework/src and eng for ClosedKeyword, IsClosed, IsUnion and UnionCaseTypes returns only that one grammar entry, so no engine code names the closed or union Roslyn API today.

2. A modifier keyword is transformed generically. /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Templating/MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:179-204 transforms an entire SyntaxTokenList without inspecting the individual kinds, and MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:239-294 transforms one token: for a keyword whose default token value equals the token value it emits MetaSyntaxFactory.Token(Transform(kind)) at line 274, and otherwise the five-argument form at lines 288-293. Transform(SyntaxKind) at MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:141 delegates to MetaSyntaxFactory.Kind, which is implemented at MetaSyntaxRewriter.MetaSyntaxFactoryImpl.cs:78-82 as a member access built from kind.ToString(), so a keyword that the generator never saw is still rendered as SyntaxKind.<Name> with no per-kind code. This is the mechanism the finding relies on, and it is present as described.

3. Pattern handling in the annotator is type-agnostic. TemplateAnnotator.cs:1533-1556 (VisitIsPatternExpression) derives the scope of the whole construct from the scope of the governing expression alone and then requires the pattern to match that scope; it never examines the type matched by the pattern. TemplateAnnotator.cs:2877-2945 (VisitSwitchStatement) likewise decides the scope from the governing expression at lines 2885-2896 and applies it to the labels and the statements. A pattern whose type happens to be a union or a member of a closed hierarchy therefore needs no new case.

4. CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:349-354 recreates each compile-time syntax tree with CSharpSyntaxTree.Create under the parse options built from the resolved language version, so a compile-time tree that already contains a closed modifier is preserved verbatim; the constraint is the language version of that CSharpParseOptions, which is the subject of TP-8 and of FACTS.md lines 15 to 23, not of this finding.

Scope boundaries worth keeping in the report. First, the finding covers the template compiler and the syntax generator only. Whether the code model exposes closed (ITypeSymbol.IsClosed, GetClosedDerivedTypeInfo) or the union case types belongs to the code-model theme, and per FACTS.md lines 53 and 56 those API members are experimental in Roslyn 5.9 and absent from the Roslyn 5.0 variant, so any engine use of them must be gated to the latest variant. Second, this finding is adjacent to but distinct from TP-6, which reports an actual behavioural difference for a union declaration nested in a compile-time class versus a run-time class; TP-6 proposes work and TP-10 proposes none, so they are not duplicates. Third, no Premium counterpart exists: metalama/Metalama.Premium#85 changes no C# production source, per the pull request survey.

A net10.0 project therefore receives 14.0 under the .NET 11 SDK, and a net11.0 project receives 15.0. corrections.what_happens_today:
Closed classes. The core drops the BaseType reference kind and derived-type indexing only when INamedType.IsSealed is true (ReferenceIndexerRequirements.cs:35-40 and :57-65, over SourceMemberOrNamedType.IsSealed => Symbol.IsSealed). A closed class is implicitly abstract and cannot carry the sealed modifier, and the compiler already confines derivation to the declaring assembly. DerivedTypesMustRespectNamingConvention, ValidateDerivedTypes and InternalOnlyImplement therefore keep working, and the transitive validator that Premium persists for other projects becomes redundant for a closed class but harmless.

Unions. A union declaration lowers to a struct, and the code model assigns TypeKind.Struct to it, so INamedType.IsSealed is true. DerivedTypesMustRespectNamingConvention applied to a union consequently validates nothing, because ReferenceIndexerRequirements.Create removes both the BaseType reference kind and derived-type indexing at :35-40 and :57-65.

The case types of a union are the parameter types of the declaration ParameterList, as the finding states, but the reference to them is not indexed. The parameters declare no symbol: Roslyn's own union tests assert that GetDeclaredSymbol of a union case parameter is null, and the synthesized case constructors have no declaring syntax reference. ReferenceIndexWalker does not override VisitUnionDeclaration, so a union is traversed by DefaultVisit; each case parameter reaches VisitParameter (:176-183), which enters the parameter as the current declaration, and CurrentDeclarationSymbol (:894-903) resolves to null. ReferenceIndexBuilder.AddReference returns immediately when the referencing symbol is null (:15-18). No ParameterType reference from the union to its case type is recorded, and a CanOnlyBeUsedFrom rule on a case type therefore does not see the union declaration. Because VisitUnionDeclaration is not overridden, EnterTypeDeclarationDefinition is not called for the union either: the base list of a top-level union is dropped by the _currentDeclarationNode null guard of IndexReference (:767), and the base list of a nested union is attributed to the containing type rather than to the union.

Finally, pet is Cat c is an is-pattern expression with a declaration pattern, for which the walker has no visitor. ReferenceKinds.IsType is assigned only for the binary is expression (:717) and for a recursive pattern (:729), so pet is Cat c is indexed as ReferenceKinds.Default through VisitIdentifierName (:103). This is the behaviour for every class and is not a change brought by C# 15.
corrections.consequence_class: Two different classes. The closed-class half is genuinely no impact. The union half is silent wrong output, located in the core reference indexer rather than in Premium: an architecture rule on a union case type under-reports, because the union declaration to case type reference is never indexed, and a rule on an interface implemented by a nested union is attributed to the containing type instead of to the union. corrections.proposed_change: No change to Premium source, as the finding concludes, but the reason changes and one of the two proposed tests would fail as written. In core, add a VisitUnionDeclaration override to ReferenceIndexWalker that enters the union with EnterTypeDeclarationDefinition and reports each ParameterList parameter type as a reference whose origin is the union type. The override must be gated to the latest Roslyn variant, because UnionDeclarationSyntax does not exist in the Roslyn 5.0 variant that serves Rider, and it must wait for the union syntax to leave the experimental state. notes:
The finding is right that Premium needs no source change and right about closed classes, but its description of union behaviour is materially wrong and its consequence class of "no impact" does not hold. The decisive step is that a union case parameter declares no symbol, which makes the current declaration symbol null in ReferenceIndexWalker and makes ReferenceIndexBuilder.AddReference drop the reference silently.

Two of the finding's open questions can be closed. The TypeKind that the core code model assigns to a union symbol is TypeKind.Struct, because Roslyn maps DeclarationKind.Union to TypeKind.Struct; no new member of TypeKind is needed and no switch over TypeKind throws. The question of whether a dedicated ReferenceKinds member for a union case is wanted stays open, and it is now coupled to the core walker change rather than being purely cosmetic.

The citation Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1965 is weak evidence on its own, because ParameterList on UnionDeclarationSyntax is an Override of the abstract TypeDeclarationSyntax.ParameterList at line 1900 that ClassDeclarationSyntax, StructDeclarationSyntax, RecordDeclarationSyntax and InterfaceDeclarationSyntax all carry as well. The claim happens to be correct, but it is established by the parser and the symbol construction, not by the grammar field.

One secondary effect I did not fold into the corrections because it is a performance question rather than a correctness one: since a union is traversed by DefaultVisit, the ReferenceIndexerOptions.MustDescendIntoMembers gate that VisitClassDeclaration and VisitStructDeclaration apply is bypassed for the members of a union.

The work belongs to the core theme rather than to the Premium theme, so the coordinator should move the union half of PR-12 into a core finding and leave only the closed-class half and the two aspect tests in Premium.

notes:
The finding's conclusion survives, but its stated mechanism does not, and its open question is answerable from the code today rather than after theme 03.

Three specific corrections.

First, the conditional at the centre of the finding is already decided. The finding writes "If the code model lists it in INamedType.Indexers of the static class, the Caching fabric and any user fabric will add [NotNull]". The code model does not and structurally cannot list it there. INamedType.Indexers accepts only symbols of kind Property that belong to the declaring symbol itself (SymbolRef.Strategy.cs:224-225), and an extension indexer belongs to the extension grouping type, which the code model exposes as a separate IExtensionBlock. Extension blocks are moreover filtered out of every named type collection by IsValidNamedType (SymbolRef.Strategy.cs:298-301), a behaviour pinned by an existing unit test (CodeModelTests.CSharp14.cs:111). This is not a property of extension indexers in particular: it is already true of the extension properties and methods that C# 14 allows, so it is verifiable in the current code rather than dependent on future Roslyn semantics.

Second, the finding overlooks the one path by which an extension member does reach the enclosing static class, namely the compiler-generated implementation method (SourceMethod.cs:169-180; CodeModelTests.CSharp14.cs:112,244-262). The fabric does enumerate those methods and their parameters at ContractExtensions.cs:105-112. The aspect is not applied, because the implementation method is implicitly declared and the eligibility rule at EligibilityRuleFactory.Contracts.cs:87 rejects it, with AddAspectIfEligible skipping silently (AspectQueryExtensions.cs:40). The outcome is the same "no impact", but by a rule that must hold, not by the absence of the declaration from the collection.

Third, the proposed change is close to minimal but incomplete on two points that would make the new tests fail. A test containing an extension indexer cannot compile under the Roslyn 5.0 variant and needs a constant gate of the kind used at Tests/Aspects/DesignTimeInvalidCode/UnknownAccessorInTemplate.cs:7, and it needs a language version that SupportedCSharpVersions does not currently offer (FACTS, lines 16 and 21). The suggested Patterns test must also be attribute-driven rather than fabric-driven, for the reason above.

Two minor citation errors, not affecting the verdict: the cited range EligibilityRuleFactory.Contracts.cs:100-115 covers the return-parameter helper and the IsReceiverParameter predicate, while the receiver-parameter rules are at :117-128; and the test and fabric paths in "where" omit the Metalama.Framework/src/tests/ and Metalama.Patterns/src/ prefixes.

The finding's size (S) and its "covered_by_in_flight" note are accurate: ExtensionMembers_Contract.cs and the seven ExtensionMembers_Contract_OnReceiver_* tests are exactly the #1159 and #1160 work that an indexer test would extend.

evidence:
Premise 1, extension indexers are a C# 15 feature. Confirmed. The proposal is at proposals/csharp-15.0/extension-indexers.md (downloaded 2026-09-04 to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Metalama/ccf204f4-b0b3-5fe6-a8de-fe20f6791d2c/scratchpad/extension-indexers.md, HTTP 200, 18629 bytes), champion issue dotnet/csharplang#9856 (extension-indexers.md:5). FACTS.md:31 lists IDS_FeatureExtensionIndexers among the features whose MessageID.RequiredVersion is LanguageVersion.CSharp15 on Roslyn main. Report 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:142-147 records the same.

Premise 2, the syntax is an ordinary indexer declaration inside an extension block, with no new syntax node. Confirmed. extension-indexers.md:14-22 adds "indexer_declaration" to the "extension_member_declaration" production; extension-indexers.md:38-46 shows "extension(int i) { public bool this[int index] { get => ...; } }". FACTS.md:28 states that extension indexers add no new syntax node and reuse IndexerDeclarationSyntax inside ExtensionBlockDeclarationSyntax; 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:144 states the same and 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:96 records that no IPropertySymbol member is added for the feature. The finding's statement that IndexerDeclaration( ..., Token( ThisKeyword ), ParameterList( ... ), accessors ) is the extension indexer syntax when placed inside an extension block is therefore correct: the "this" keyword and the bracketed parameter list are the ordinary indexer syntax.

Premise 3, an extension block that declares an indexer must have a named receiver parameter. Confirmed verbatim: "Because indexers are always instance members, an extension block that declares an indexer must provide a named receiver parameter." (extension-indexers.md:30-31).

Premise 4, "init" accessors are rejected. Confirmed verbatim: "indexers inside an extension declaration cannot specify abstract, virtual, override, new, sealed, partial, protected (or any of the related accessibility modifiers), or init accessors." (extension-indexers.md:32-35). The same sentence adds five more forbidden modifiers that the finding does not name: abstract, virtual, override, new, sealed and partial, plus protected and the related accessibility modifiers.

Premise 5, the implementation methods are named get_Item and set_Item and take the receiver as the first parameter. Confirmed: "Implementation methods named get_Item/set_Item in the enclosing static class. These methods prepend the receiver parameter to the parameter list and contain the user-defined bodies. They are static ..." (extension-indexers.md:187-190). The worked example emits "public static bool get_Item<T>(T t, int index)" and "public static void set_Item<T>(T t, int index, bool value)" in the enclosing static class, with the type parameters of the extension block copied onto the method and the assigned value last in the setter (extension-indexers.md:216-242). This matches the shape that Metalama already models for extension methods and extension property accessors: /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/AdviceImpl/Introduction/ExtensionImplementationHelper.cs:15-18 documents the helper as creating the static method that C# generates in the parent type, :53 uses extensionBlock.DeclaringType as the parent type, :64 sets IsStatic = true, :69 marks the method implicitly declared, and :72-79 copies the type parameters of the extension block.

Premise 6, the code premise that the rejection is the only barrier, spot-checked although it belongs to the code lens. /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Advising/AdviceFactory.cs:1406 calls ValidateNotExtensionBlock( targetType, "an indexer" ), and the helper at :527-534 throws InvalidOperationException with the message "Cannot introduce {introduced} into '{declaration}' because it represents an extension block." The same helper is called for constructors (:957), fields (:1128, :1158), automatic properties (:1206), events (:1490) and attributes (:1879).

Premise 7, the test folder that the finding names as the model exists: /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Metalama.Framework.Tests.AspectTests/Tests/Aspects/CSharp14/ExtensionMembers, which contains ExtensionMembers_IntroduceAutoProperty.cs and its .t.cs baseline among others. The finding's path fragment omits the "src/" segment.

Premise 8, the Roslyn version. Refuted as written, and this is the correction. The finding's confidence line says the implementation method shape "must be checked against Roslyn 5.10 symbols". No stable Roslyn 5.10 package exists (FACTS.md:48, 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:15), the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 is a main build of 2026-07-15 (FACTS.md:49), and in that build and in the stable 5.9.0 the extension indexer feature is gated on LanguageVersion.Preview because MessageID.RequiredVersion returns Preview for IDS_FeatureExtensionIndexers (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:16) and LanguageVersion.CSharp15 does not exist (FACTS.md:54, 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:16, :78). The value CSharp15 = 1500 and the switch of the six feature gates to CSharp15 come from commit "Add C# 15 language version (#84799)" of 2026-08-11 (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:17, :78). The expected first stable package to contain it is 5.12 (FACTS.md:49, 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:15, :18). Metalama's own plumbing stops at C# 14: SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest = CSharp14 and ToLanguageVersion maps V5_10_0 to CSharp14 (FACTS.md:16), and CompileTimeAspectPipeline.VerifyLanguageVersion reports CSharpVersionNotSupported for any version not in All (FACTS.md:21). A test folder Aspects/CSharp15/ExtensionIndexers therefore cannot compile before the latest Roslyn variant becomes 5.12 and the language version plumbing is raised to C# 15.

Premise 9, two further semantics points that the finding's eligibility rule omits, both from the proposal. First, the IndexerName attribute: "IndexerNameAttribute may be applied to an extension indexer. The attribute is not emitted in metadata, but its value affects conflicts between members, it determines the name of the property and accessors in metadata, and is used when emitting [DefaultMemberAttribute]" (extension-indexers.md:51-60), and the metadata section repeats that the emitted property is named "Item" "(or the value supplied by IndexerNameAttribute)" (extension-indexers.md:184-186). The names get_Item and set_Item are therefore the default and not invariant. Second, the inferrability rule is stated for the combined parameter set, not for the receiver alone: "The existing extension member inferrability rule still applies: For each non-method extension member, all the type parameters of its extension block must be used in the combined set of parameters from the extension and the member." (extension-indexers.md:53-54). An indexer has parameters, so a block type parameter used only in the indexer parameter list satisfies the rule, unlike an extension property.

Premise 10, a consumption restriction that does not constrain the introduction advice: "Decision (LDM/Mads by email 2026-04-07): no extension indexers on strings or arrays." (extension-indexers.md:478 and :512), consistent with 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:146. This governs element access binding on array and string receivers, not the legality of the declaration.

corrections.what_happens_today: Unchanged. Advising/AdviceFactory.cs:1406 calls ValidateNotExtensionBlock( targetType, "an indexer" ), and the helper at Advising/AdviceFactory.cs:527-534 throws InvalidOperationException with the message "Cannot introduce an indexer into '...' because it represents an extension block.", which surfaces as an aspect error at build time.

corrections.proposed_change: Remove the validation at Advising/AdviceFactory.cs:1406 and add an eligibility rule that enforces the declaration restrictions of proposals/csharp-15.0/extension-indexers.md. The rule must require a named receiver parameter, because the proposal states that an extension block declaring an indexer must provide one (extension-indexers.md:30-31); in Metalama terms this is ExtensionBlockBuilder.IsStaticExtension == false for introduced blocks (CodeModel/Introductions/Builders/ExtensionBlockBuilder.cs:34) and a non-empty IExtensionBlock.ReceiverParameter.Name for source blocks. The rule must also reject an init accessor and the modifiers abstract, virtual, override, new, sealed, partial and protected, which the proposal forbids in the same sentence (extension-indexers.md:32-35). Add CreateImplicitAccessorMethod calls for the indexer accessors in AdviceImpl/Introduction/IntroduceIndexerTransformation.cs, following the pattern of IntroducePropertyTransformation.cs:243,262: the implementation methods are static methods of the enclosing static class, generic over the type parameters of the extension block, with the receiver prepended to the parameter list and, for the setter, the assigned value last (extension-indexers.md:187-190 and the worked example at :216-242). Derive their names from the indexer metadata name rather than hard-coding get_Item and set_Item, because IndexerNameAttribute determines the name of the property and of its accessors in metadata (extension-indexers.md:51-60, :184-186). When implementing the inferrability check, apply the rule that the proposal states, namely that every type parameter of the block must be used in the combined set of the extension parameter and the indexer parameters (extension-indexers.md:53-54); a rule copied from extension properties, which have no parameters, would be too strict. Add design-time coverage because DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.CreateExtensionBlock (lines 662-680) copies members verbatim. Tests go under Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Metalama.Framework.Tests.AspectTests/Tests/Aspects/CSharp15/ExtensionIndexers, beside the existing Aspects/CSharp14/ExtensionMembers. Sequencing: this work cannot be tested before two prerequisites land, because the feature is gated on IDS_FeatureExtensionIndexers, which resolves to LanguageVersion.Preview in the consumed Roslyn 5.10.0-1.26365.3 preview and in the stable 5.9.0, and to LanguageVersion.CSharp15 only from the Roslyn commit of 2026-08-11. The prerequisites are the move of the latest Roslyn variant to the stable 5.12 and the addition of C# 15 to SupportedCSharpVersions and to the checks of CompileTimeAspectPipeline.VerifyLanguageVersion.

notes:
The finding survives. Every statement it makes about C# 15 semantics is supported by the proposal proposals/csharp-15.0/extension-indexers.md: the feature exists in C# 15, it reuses the ordinary indexer syntax inside an extension block with no new syntax node or symbol interface, it requires a named receiver parameter, it forbids the init accessor, and its implementation methods are static methods named get_Item and set_Item in the enclosing static class with the receiver prepended.

Three corrections are needed, none of which invalidates the finding.

First, the version reference. The confidence line asks for the implementation method shape to be checked "against Roslyn 5.10 symbols". No stable Roslyn 5.10 exists, the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 is a preview in which the feature is reachable only under LanguageVersion.Preview and in which LanguageVersion.CSharp15 is absent, and the expected stable target is Roslyn 5.12. The work therefore depends on the Roslyn 5.12 move and on the C# 15 language version plumbing, which are separate items; without them the proposed Aspects/CSharp15/ExtensionIndexers tests cannot compile. The shape itself does not need to be checked against Roslyn symbols at all, because the proposal specifies it and because Metalama emits source and lets the compiler perform the lowering; ExtensionImplementationHelper only models the compiler-generated methods in the code model.

Second, the restriction list is incomplete. The proposal forbids abstract, virtual, override, new, sealed, partial and protected in the same sentence as init, so an eligibility rule that checks only init and IsStatic is narrower than the language. The finding's reference to IsStatic == true is harmless but redundant as a member-level check, because C# has no static indexers; the load-bearing check is the one on the block's receiver.

Third, two details the finding does not mention would produce wrong output if ignored. IndexerNameAttribute renames the property and its accessors in metadata, so get_Item and set_Item are defaults rather than fixed names. The inferrability rule is stated over the combined set of the extension parameter and the member parameters, which is a relaxation for indexers relative to extension properties.

One statement of the report that the finding does not rely on is confirmed and is not a constraint on this work: the LDM decision of 2026-04-07 that there are no extension indexers on strings or arrays governs element access binding on those receivers, not the legality of the declaration.

The rejection premise itself was spot-checked in the source and holds, although it belongs to the code lens.

For fields, properties, events, methods and parameters the selection filters on !IsImplicitlyDeclared (MulticastImplementation.cs:403, :412, :421, :449, :459), and the synthesized union members are implicitly declared: SynthesizedUnionValuePropertySymbol.IsImplicitlyDeclared is true (SynthesizedUnionValuePropertySymbol.cs:44), its getter is created over the union declaration syntax so SourcePropertyAccessorSymbol.IsImplicitlyDeclared is also true (SourcePropertyAccessorSymbol.cs:771-786), and SynthesizedUnionCtor inherits the sealed IsImplicitlyDeclared of SynthesizedMethodSymbol (SynthesizedMethodSymbol.cs:29-35). The code model carries that flag through unchanged (SymbolBasedDeclaration.cs:52-57). Those targets therefore behave exactly as for a struct. Instance constructors are the exception. Their eligibility rule (MulticastImplementation.cs:247-252) does not call MustBeExplicitlyDeclared, and the selection filter (!c.IsImplicitlyDeclared || c.Parameters.Count == 0) at :353 and :441 deliberately admits an implicitly declared parameterless constructor. Roslyn adds such a constructor to every struct type that lacks one (SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:5718-5728), and a union always lacks one because every case constructor takes exactly one parameter (SynthesizedUnionCtor.cs:25). An assembly-level multicast aspect with MulticastTargets.InstanceConstructor therefore selects the union's implicit parameterless constructor. If the aspect overrides it, Metalama materializes it as an explicitly declared parameterless constructor (OverrideConstructorAdvice.cs:32, ConstructorBuilder.cs:43-56), which the compiler rejects with CS9375, because a constructor declared in a union must have a this(...) initializer that calls a synthesized or an explicitly declared constructor (unions.md lines 754-755; ErrorCode.cs:2480; CSharpResources.resx:8348-8350; Binder_Statements.cs:3816-3830). Nothing of this is reachable before Metalama moves to Roslyn 5.12, because no consumed Roslyn exposes C# 15 as a non-preview language version.
corrections.proposed_change: Add an aspect test in Metalama.Extensions.Multicast.AspectTests with a union and MulticastTargets.Struct | Method | Property | Field | Parameter, asserting that the synthesized Value property, its getter and the case constructors are not selected. Add a second case with MulticastTargets.InstanceConstructor: either restrict the constructor selection at MulticastImplementation.cs:353 and :441, or the eligibility rule at :247-252, so that the implicit parameterless constructor of a union is not a multicast target, or rely on a general rule in the engine that makes constructor advice ineligible on a union. The underlying defect (materializing the implicit parameterless constructor of a union produces CS9375) is not specific to multicasting and should be recorded against the constructor-advice theme; the multicast change is only the target filter. Adjusting the diagnostic wording "is not a struct or record struct" at :235 remains optional: the sentence is incomplete rather than false, because a union is lowered to a struct.
corrections.consequence_class: Correct behaviour for type, method, property, field, event and parameter targets; invalid generated code (CS9375) for MulticastTargets.InstanceConstructor when the aspect overrides the implicit parameterless constructor of a union.

notes: Every external premise the finding states is true, and its stated dependency ("depends on IsImplicitlyDeclared of the synthesized members") is resolved in its favour: SynthesizedUnionValuePropertySymbol, its synthesized getter and SynthesizedUnionCtor all report IsImplicitlyDeclared true on dotnet/roslyn main, and Metalama's code model forwards that flag. The confidence can be raised from "plausible" to "verified" on the external side. What the finding overstates is "explicitly declared members only": the instance-constructor rule is the single place in MulticastImplementation.cs that intentionally admits an implicitly declared declaration, and a union, being a struct without a parameterless constructor of its own, always has exactly such a constructor. Because a union forbids an explicitly declared constructor without a this(...) initializer, the consequence class "No impact expected" does not hold for that one target kind. Three secondary points. First, the exclusion of the synthesized case constructors is not produced by MustBeExplicitlyDeclared, which the constructor rule never calls, but by the parameter count: a case constructor has one parameter, so (!IsImplicitlyDeclared || Parameters.Count == 0) is false. Second, the synthesized backing field of the Value property is likewise implicitly declared and is excluded by the field filter at :403 and :478. Third, the size estimate should rise from S if the constructor guard is implemented in the multicast package, and the deeper fix belongs to the constructor-advice theme rather than to this finding. Not verified in this session: whether Metalama.Compiler will be based on a Roslyn that reports these symbols identically, since Metalama.Compiler is not cloned (FACTS.md:6); and the behaviour of a partial union declaration, which the proposal permits but which was not read.

notes:
The finding survives, because its subject is real: Premium carries transition-sensitive literals, a copied `nuget.base.config` and hand-picked transitive package pins, and nothing in Premium references the core procedure that will move them. Three premises needed correction and none of them is load-bearing for the concern itself.

First and most important, the phrase "the stable 5.10.0" names a package that will never be published. Roslyn publishes a stable every third minor version, in step with the quarterly Visual Studio 2026 releases; the published 5.x stables are 5.0.0, 5.3.0, 5.6.0 and 5.9.0, and dotnet/roslyn `main` is already versioned 5.12. The transition is therefore a renumbering of the latest variant to 5.12, governed by steps 7, 8 and 10 of `updating-roslyn.md`, and not a change of a prerelease label into a release label in place. That is what raises the size of the edit: the version string is part of the identity of the variant assemblies, so it appears in `InternalsVisibleTo` entries, in package file paths and in the `TargetRoslynVersion` metadata that selects an extension assembly at run time, in eleven tracked Premium files rather than three.

Second, the pin statement was inaccurate about the core repository. The core latest variant pins `System.Text.Json` only; `System.IO.Pipelines` is a global `SystemIOPipelinesLatestVersion` in `Directory.Packages.props`, and Premium additionally pins `System.Memory` and `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe`, which core does not do in its variant file. The two files are not copies of one another, and a re-derivation must read the nuspec of the future stable rather than mirror the core variant.

Third, the nuspec gives a lower bound and not the value to write. In the last published stable, `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Features` 5.9.0, the declared floors for `System.Text.Json` and `System.IO.Pipelines` are 10.0.1, well below both the 10.0.8 named in the core comment and the 10.0.11 pinned in both repositories. The pinned values follow the "latest patch in the line" policy that the Premium file states for `System.Memory`. A re-derivation that copies the floor would lower the pins and reintroduce the vulnerability warnings that the latest-patch policy exists to avoid.

On the open question of the finding, the local evidence answers part of it. `RoslynApiMaxVersion` is consumed in exactly one place in Premium on pr85, `eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.5.10.0.props:3`, and Premium defines no fallback for it anywhere; only `RoslynVersion` and `RoslynMaxVersion` have literal fallbacks in `Directory.Packages.props`. A build that has not run `Build.ps1 prepare`, and therefore has no `eng/Versions.g.props`, would leave `ThisRoslynVersion` empty rather than fall back to the literal. Whether that condition occurs on a developer machine could not be settled here, because the generated file is not in the working tree.

Two premises of the finding were checked and hold as stated: the export of `RoslynApiMaxVersion` and `RoslynMaxVersion` by `eng/src/Program.cs:151`, and the import point at `eng/Versions.props:15`, which imports `Versions.g.props` when it exists. The origin of the core `nuget.base.config` in commit e01ee144 also holds; the file was added by "Restore the roslyn-consolidated feed and target Roslyn 5.10 (#1881)".

No claim of the finding depends on C# 15 language semantics, on a csharplang proposal or on the Roslyn public API surface, so those parts of the reference material bear on it only through the version timeline.

evidence:
Premise 1, `partial union` and `unsafe union` are legal, so a union declaration can carry the modifiers whose absence the finding describes. CONFIRMED. The proposal grammar is `attributes? struct_modifier* 'partial'? 'union' identifier type_parameter_list? '(' case_types ')' struct_interfaces? type_parameter_constraints_clause* ( '{' struct_member_declaration* '}' | ';' )` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/csharplang/main/proposals/csharp-15.0/unions.md, fetched 2026-09-04). Roslyn agrees: a union has TypeKind.Struct (impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:94, EnumConversions.ToTypeKind), and SourceMemberContainerSymbol.MakeModifiers grants the struct arm `DeclarationModifiers.Partial | DeclarationModifiers.ReadOnly | DeclarationModifiers.Unsafe | DeclarationModifiers.Safe`, excluding only `Ref` for a union (scratchpad/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:341-348, dotnet/roslyn main). Metalama reads the modifiers through a kind list that omits UnionDeclaration (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CodeModel/Source/SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:329-350 combined with Utilities/Roslyn/SyntaxKindExtensions.cs:33-35), so the reported IsPartial == false is a genuine consequence of a legal declaration, and the same holds for HasModifier at Utilities/Roslyn/SymbolExtensions.cs:196-201.

Premise 2, UnionDeclarationSyntax derives from TypeDeclarationSyntax and its kind is UnionDeclaration with the numeric value 9082. CONFIRMED. dotnet/roslyn main src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Syntax/SyntaxKind.cs:950 (`UnionDeclaration = 9082`) and :430 (`UnionKeyword = 8452`); eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1954-1978 (`<Node Name="UnionDeclarationSyntax" Base="TypeDeclarationSyntax" ... ExperimentalUrl=...>`); impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:58,60.

Premise 3, "A union always has a ParameterList (the case list)". CORRECTED. The field is declared optional (Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1965, `<Field Name="ParameterList" Type="ParameterListSyntax" Optional="true" Override="true" />`) and the parser parses one only when the next token is an open parenthesis: `var paramList = CurrentToken.Kind == SyntaxKind.OpenParenToken || isExtension ? ParseParenthesizedParameterList(forExtensionOrUnion: isExtension || isUnion) : null;` (scratchpad/LanguageParser-5.10.cs:1822-1823). A union written without a case list therefore produces a UnionDeclarationSyntax whose ParameterList is null, and the compiler reports ERR_UnionDeclarationNeedsCaseTypes = 9370 afterwards (scratchpad/ErrorCode.cs:2475; scratchpad/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:4992-5008, the report_ERR_UnionDeclarationNeedsCaseTypes flag). The statement is true of code that compiles, which is the case the finding reasons about, so the conclusion survives.

Premise 4, the open question about the declaring syntax of the synthesized union members. ANSWERED, and the answer splits in two, which corrects which sites are at risk.
(a) The per-case constructors have no declaring syntax. `internal sealed class SynthesizedUnionCtor : SynthesizedInstanceConstructor` (dotnet/roslyn main src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/Synthesized/SynthesizedUnionCtor.cs), `internal class SynthesizedInstanceConstructor : SynthesizedMethodSymbol` (SynthesizedInstanceConstructor.cs:16), and SynthesizedMethodSymbol returns an empty array and is implicitly declared: `public override ImmutableArray<SyntaxReference> DeclaringSyntaxReferences { get { return ImmutableArray<SyntaxReference>.Empty; } }` and `public sealed override bool IsImplicitlyDeclared { get { return true; } }` (SynthesizedMethodSymbol.cs:21-35). Metalama's GetPrimaryDeclarationSyntax is `symbol.GetPrimarySyntaxReference()?.GetSyntax()` (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Utilities/Roslyn/SymbolExtensions.cs:472), so it returns null for these constructors.
(b) The Value property does have a declaring syntax, and it is the union declaration. `internal sealed class SynthesizedUnionValuePropertySymbol : SourcePropertySymbolBase` is constructed with `TypeDeclarationSyntax syntax` and passes it as `syntax: syntax` to the base (SynthesizedUnionValuePropertySymbol.cs, dotnet/roslyn main), the base returns that reference (`public override ImmutableArray<SyntaxReference> DeclaringSyntaxReferences { get { return ImmutableArray.Create(_syntaxRef); } }`, scratchpad/SourcePropertySymbolBase.cs:559-565), and the property overrides `IsImplicitlyDeclared => true`. The instance is created from the union declaration syntax itself: `var valuePropertySyntax = (TypeDeclarationSyntax)declaration.Declarations[0].SyntaxReference.GetSyntax(); var valueProperty = new SynthesizedUnionValuePropertySymbol(this, valuePropertySyntax, diagnostics);` (scratchpad/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:4977-4990), which also adds the getter accessor and the backing field. The getter is created with the same node (`CreateGetAccessorSymbol` passes `CSharpSyntaxNode`).
(c) Roslyn never creates a primary constructor for a union. DeclarationTreeBuilder sets HasPrimaryConstructor only for a record, class or struct declaration: `var hasPrimaryCtor = node.ParameterList != null && node is RecordDeclarationSyntax or ClassDeclarationSyntax or StructDeclarationSyntax;` (scratchpad/DeclarationTreeBuilder-main.cs:724-733), and SourceMemberContainerSymbol skips the SynthesizedPrimaryConstructor for a union: `if (syntax.Kind() is SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration) { ... } else { var ctor = new SynthesizedPrimaryConstructor(this, syntax); ... }` (scratchpad/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:4123-4137). The proposal states the same, that the parenthesized list declares case types and is not a primary constructor (unions.md).

Consequences of premise 4 for the finding. IsPrimaryConstructor (Utilities/Roslyn/SymbolExtensions.cs:283-291) is false for a union case constructor because `GetPrimaryDeclarationSyntax()` is null, and not because IsTypeDeclaration omits UnionDeclaration; no constructor symbol can ever present a UnionDeclarationSyntax there, so the union exclusion and the `RawKind != 9082` test of the proposed change are unnecessary. SourceConstructor.cs:92-94 is not an affected site, because the switch has an explicit `null =>` arm above it (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CodeModel/Source/SourceConstructor.cs:83) and the containing type is a value type, so the result is ConstructorInitializerKind.None. Conversely, GetDeclarationFlags (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Linking/SymbolExtensions.cs:20-63) is reachable with a UnionDeclarationSyntax through the Value property and its getter, whose kind is neither in the list at lines 26-31 nor an accessor declaration nor null, so control reaches the throwing default arm at line 62; the `case null` arm at lines 57-59 covers only the case constructors. The same asymmetry applies to ImplicitLastOverrideReferenceInliner.cs:72: with the Value property the arm `{ IsTypeDeclaration: true } when declarationSyntax is TypeDeclarationSyntax { ParameterList: { } parameterList } => parameterList` is not matched today and the default arm at line 73 throws, whereas after a blind broadening to `node is TypeDeclarationSyntax` it would match and return the case list as the member body, which is wrong. LinkerLateTransformationRegistry.cs:145-152 and 186-192 carry the same hazard, since the union ParameterList is the case list.

Premise 5, the eligibility argument. The external half is confirmed: both synthesized union members are implicitly declared (SynthesizedMethodSymbol.cs:29-35 for the constructors, SynthesizedUnionValuePropertySymbol.cs for the property). The Metalama line references are slightly off: MustBeExplicitlyDeclared is at Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework/Eligibility/EligibilityRuleFactory.cs:88 and the method rule spans lines 58-71.

Premise 6, "until the stable Roslyn 5.10 removes the experimental attribute". REFUTED as stated. No stable Roslyn 5.10 package exists on nuget.org; the stable line is 5.0.0, 5.3.0, 5.6.0 and 5.9.0, and the November 2026 baseline is expected to carry Roslyn 5.12 (FACTS.md addendum lines 48-49). The ExperimentalUrl and RSEXPERIMENTAL006 markers on the union, with-element and labeled-break syntax were removed by the commit "Add C# 15 language version (#84799)" of 2026-08-11, that is at the 5.11 snap (impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:17 and :90). Furthermore the experimental marker is not the reason a numeric kind test is needed: SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration is new in 5.10 and absent from the Roslyn 5.0 API of the lower variant (impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:58), and production source contains no `#if ROSLYN_*` blocks (FACTS.md line 12), so a single source text compiled against both variants cannot name the enum member at all.

corrections.what_happens_today: A `partial union` reports IsPartial == false, so the design-time generator reports TypeNotPartial (Pipeline/DesignTime/DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs:158-163) and IntroduceMemberAdvice.ValidateBuilder reports CannotIntroducePartialMemberToNonPartialType (AdviceImpl/Introduction/IntroduceMemberAdvice.cs:216-224) for partial members introduced into a union. The premise holds: the proposal grammar allows `partial` on a union, and Roslyn allows Partial, ReadOnly, Unsafe and Safe on a union because a union has TypeKind.Struct. The other sites are latent, but the risk is distributed differently from what the finding states, because the two kinds of synthesized union member differ in whether they have a declaring syntax. The per-case constructors are SynthesizedUnionCtor, which derives from SynthesizedMethodSymbol and therefore returns an empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences and IsImplicitlyDeclared true; Roslyn also never creates a SynthesizedPrimaryConstructor for a union, and DeclarationTreeBuilder sets HasPrimaryConstructor only for a record, class or struct declaration. Every site that switches on the primary declaration syntax of a union case constructor therefore sees null, not a UnionDeclarationSyntax. IsPrimaryConstructor is false for that reason, and SourceConstructor.cs:92-94 is not an affected site at all, because its switch has an explicit null arm above the type-declaration arms and yields ConstructorInitializerKind.None for a value type. The synthesized Value property is the opposite case: SynthesizedUnionValuePropertySymbol derives from SourcePropertySymbolBase and is constructed with the union declaration syntax, so its DeclaringSyntaxReferences is that UnionDeclarationSyntax, and the same node is used for its getter accessor. Consequently Linking/SymbolExtensions.cs GetDeclarationFlags can be entered with kind UnionDeclaration, which matches neither the list at lines 26-31, nor the accessor case, nor the null case, and reaches the throwing default at line 62; and ImplicitLastOverrideReferenceInliner.cs:72-73 likewise falls to its throwing default. Both hazards are carried by the Value property and its getter, not by the case constructors. The LinkerLateTransformationRegistry checks at lines 145-152 and 186-192 remain unreachable today, because they run only after a primary constructor was removed and a union has none. The record-only kind switches remain unreached, because both synthesized union members are implicitly declared and the override eligibility rules require an explicitly declared member (Metalama.Framework/Eligibility/EligibilityRuleFactory.cs:88 for fields, properties and indexers, and lines 58-71 for non-accessor methods). notes:
The finding survives. Its central external premises are true: `partial union` and `unsafe union` are legal, UnionDeclarationSyntax derives from TypeDeclarationSyntax with kind UnionDeclaration = 9082, a union carries synthesized members (a Value property with its getter and backing field, and one public constructor per case type), and none of Metalama's syntax-kind lists mentions the new kind.

Three corrections matter for the work item.

First, the open question is now answered from the Roslyn sources rather than left open, and the answer redistributes the risk. The per-case constructors have an empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences and are implicitly declared, and Roslyn creates no primary constructor for a union, so every kind switch that is fed a union case constructor sees null and takes an existing null arm. The Value property and its getter, by contrast, report the UnionDeclarationSyntax as their declaring syntax, so they are the symbols that can drive an assertion failure in Linking/SymbolExtensions.GetDeclarationFlags and in ImplicitLastOverrideReferenceInliner.

Second, two elements of the proposed change need adjustment. The union exclusion in IsPrimaryConstructor is unnecessary and would be dead code. The blanket replacement of kind lists by `node is TypeDeclarationSyntax` is unsafe at the sites that read TypeDeclarationSyntax.ParameterList, because a union's parameter list is a case-type list; there the broadening converts a loud assertion into a silent wrong result.

Third, the version statement is wrong. There is no stable Roslyn 5.10. The experimental markers were removed on 2026-08-11 by the commit that added LanguageVersion.CSharp15, which places the change at the 5.11 snap, and the stable version expected for the 2027.0 baseline is 5.12. The practical constraint on naming the union kind in code is not the experimental marker but the absence of SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration from the Roslyn 5.0 API used by the lower variant, in a source tree that has no conditional compilation for Roslyn versions.

One further observation for whoever implements this: since no Roslyn that Metalama consumes today exposes C# 15 outside LanguageVersion.Preview, and Metalama caps the language version at C# 14, none of these sites can be reached by user code until both the Roslyn 5.12 move and the language-version work are done, which supports the "latent" classification.

The finding survives. Its conclusion, that these packages impose no obstacle on a `net11.0` test leg, is supported by stronger evidence than the finding itself offers, because the packages were unpacked and inspected in this session rather than inferred. Four corrections were needed.

First, the asset target frameworks named in the finding are wrong in detail. No package in the list carries a `netcoreapp3.1` asset. The actual set is `net8.0` for the test platform packages and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.TestHost`, `net6.0` for `xunit.runner.visualstudio`, `netstandard2.0` for `coverlet.collector`, and no target framework at all for `coverlet.msbuild`.

Second, the reason given for the leg working is inverted. The finding argues that the leg works because no package carries a `net10.0` asset that a `net11.0` leg would fail to find. NuGet does not work that way: it selects the highest asset folder compatible with the project target framework, so a `net10.0` folder would be selected by a `net11.0` project rather than missed. What makes the leg work is that .NET 11 is compatible with all of `netstandard2.0`, `net6.0` and `net8.0`. The conclusion is unaffected, but the stated reason would mislead a reader who applied it to a different package.

Third, the open question about the 17.14 test host can be closed by inspection rather than left open. `Microsoft.TestPlatform.TestHost` 17.14.1 ships no `testhost.runtimeconfig.json`, so the test host runs under the runtime configuration of the test project, and none of the four MSBuild files that the two test platform packages contribute branches on the target framework. There is no version gate to trip. This is inspection of the package rather than an executed test run, so it is strong evidence and not proof, but it removes the conditional from the proposed change.

Fourth, the proposed change names "the version that ships with Visual Studio 2026", which is ambiguous and currently unobtainable. Visual Studio 2026 is a line of minor versions, and `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` has already published 18.0.0 through 18.9.0 against it. The pin has to follow the November 2026 long-term servicing channel baseline specifically, and no `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk` version matching that baseline is published yet, so the correction is a comment change now and a version change after 2026-11-10.

Two entries of the `where` list, `Directory.Packages.props:203` for BenchmarkDotNet and `:212-213` for LINQPad, are over-inclusive. The two projects that consume them each declare a single target framework, `net10.0` and `net10.0-windows` respectively, so no `net11.0` leg reaches them. This also disposes of the open question about LINQPad on .NET 11: the question is real for a future move of the driver to .NET 11, but it is not raised by adding a `net11.0` user target framework leg.

Two accuracy remarks for the story writer, both verified by reading the file:
1. The claim that a run-time union in a file with compile-time code "breaks" the compile-time compilation needs to be stated per path, because two of the cited paths are already kind-agnostic. VisitTypeOrNamespaceMembers at CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter.cs:1452-1461 dispatches on the pattern `{ SyntaxKind.IsTypeDeclaration: true } and TypeDeclarationSyntax`, so a union declared directly in a namespace does reach the private VisitTypeDeclaration, and FindCompileTimeCodeVisitor.VisitTypeDeclaration at CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.FindCompileTimeCodeVisitor.cs:76-85 recurses through the same kind-agnostic pattern. What is missing is the entry point: FindCompileTimeCodeVisitor is a walker whose per-kind overrides are the only way a top-level union is inspected at all, so a compile-time type nested in a run-time union is not detected, and the file is treated as having no compile-time code.
2. The failing paths are the hand-written kind lists, which is why this finding overlaps CM-6. The nested-member switch at CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter.cs:540-541 lists ClassDeclaration, StructDeclaration, InterfaceDeclaration, RecordDeclaration and RecordStructDeclaration and sends everything else to the default at line 557, which calls this.Visit(member).AssertNotNull() and adds the result as a member of a compile-time type; a nested union would therefore be copied verbatim into the compile-time compilation rather than removed. PopulateNestedCompileTimeTypes at lines 356-357 lists the same kinds plus EnumDeclaration and DelegateDeclaration, so a union nested in a run-time type falls to the default at line 371 and is silently ignored, which loses the diagnostic RunTimeTypesCannotHaveCompileTimeTypesExceptTypeFabrics.

Consequence for the story: the proposed change is the same edit as CM-7 (add the visitor override) applied to one more visitor, and the same edit as CM-6 (extend the kind lists) applied to two more switches, so it should be merged into that story rather than carried as its own. notes:
The central claim survives: a Core flavour name that the core engine compares as a string is duplicated in Metalama.Premium build files, no document names those files, and a stale value fails silently. Four details are wrong.

1. `ExtensionLoaderBase.cs:31` does not compare anything. The literal there is assigned to a local variable consumed only by the trace message on line 33, while the filter on line 35 calls `SatisfiesCurrentProcess`. The core document repeats the same inaccuracy at `platform-support.md:319-322`, so the finding inherited it. This strengthens rather than weakens the finding, because that copy is an unused duplicate.

2. The commit citation is wrong. Commit 28c036a9 changes only `Directory.Packages.md`. The commit that moves the two core literals from `net8.0` to `net10.0` is 575be8b8, from the same pull request #1876.

3. The count of eight conflates two different roles. Only four Premium files carry the string that the engine compares, and four more carry the same name as a directory segment or as a `TargetFrameworks` value that must agree with it. Thirty-five Premium build files contain `net10.0` on pr85, so neither eight nor four is the count of the whole rename.

4. `Metalama.Extensions.CodeFixes.AspectTests.csproj:51` is not one of the copies. Its `MetalamaExtensionAssembly` item uses `$(TargetFramework)` in the path and declares no `TargetFramework` metadata, so the null branch of `TargetedAssemblyReference.cs:24` accepts it on every framework. The `net10.0` of that file is the `TargetFrameworks` property on line 11. The finding also omits the identical `Metalama.Extensions.Validation.AspectTests.csproj:52`, which shows the citation was to the wrong kind of line.

The title should say that the Core flavour name is duplicated in four Premium build files as the compared metadata and in four more as a path or target framework name. The schema of this tool has no field for a corrected title, so the correction is recorded here.

One further observation that supports the consequence class and is not in the finding. `Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting.targets:136` filters extension assemblies with `IsTargetFrameworkCompatible`, which accepts a `net8.0` metadata value for a `net10.0` test project, and then writes that value into the file read at line 160. The runtime comparison at `TargetedAssemblyReference.cs:24` is exact. A stale value therefore passes the build time filter and fails the run time one, which is precisely the shape of failure that produces no diagnostic.

The proposed change is documentation only, so the question of compiling under both Roslyn variants does not apply.

Verdict: the proposed change is not implemented, not in progress and not tracked. Neither part of it exists.

Part one, the release gate. The pin is still the prerelease. Directory.Packages.props:28 sets RoslynApiMaxVersion to 5.10.0-1.26365.3 and Directory.Packages.props:30 sets RoslynMaxVersion to the same string, with the comment at Directory.Packages.props:25-27 stating that Roslyn 5.10 is a preview restored from the roslyn-consolidated feed. nuget.base.config:4-8 declares that private feed with the comment "Roslyn 5.10 is a preview that is not published on nuget.org". Metalama.Framework.Workspaces, Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting and Metalama.LinqPad are all listed in PublicArtifacts at eng/src/Program.cs:148, 143 and 163, so all three are published.

The documentation states the obligation but does not make it a gate. Metalama.Framework/docs/platform-support.md:274-276 says that RoslynApiMaxVersion follows Visual Studio 2027 and the .NET 11 SDK within three weeks of their stable release, by rule 7. Metalama.Framework/docs/updating-roslyn.md:38-52, the section "Entering and leaving a prerelease Roslyn", documents that the whole switch is the version string of SupportedCSharpVersions.ToNuGetVersionString and that leaving the prerelease is the reverse edit. Neither says that the edit must happen before a public package is produced. The "Verification checklist before the 2027.0 general availability date" at Metalama.Framework/docs/platform-support.md:354-373 has exactly three items (the Visual Studio 2026 long-term servicing channel runtime and Roslyn version, the Rider and C# Dev Kit measurement, and a design-time smoke test); leaving the prerelease Roslyn is not among them. Directory.Packages.md contains no such gate either (a grep for "prerelease", "preview", "nuget.org" and "roslyn-consolidated" returns only lines 79 and 372, both about unrelated matters).

Part two, the build check. Nothing of the kind exists. No pull request covers it. Metalama#1879 touches no build file at all. Metalama.Premium#84 changes only two build files, and leaves RoslynVersion and RoslynMaxVersion untouched. Metalama.Premium#85 moves Premium onto the same prerelease string, so it widens the exposure rather than closing it; the survey of that pull request states that when the stable Roslyn ships, Premium must change RoslynVersion and RoslynMaxVersion in Directory.Packages.props and revisit the nuget.base.config comment, but that is a description of future work, not a scoped issue. Of the pull requests merged since 2026-08-15, #1883 introduced the prerelease pin, and #1889 declared the private feed for the reference-assembly project only; the survey entry for #1889 says explicitly that "adopting Roslyn 5.10 stable is the edit of that one version string, which removes the source again", again as an observation, not as tracked work.

Two corrections a user story must carry. First, per the FACTS addendum, the stable Roslyn of the November 2026 baseline is expected to be 5.12, not 5.10: nuget.org serves stable 5.0.0, 5.3.0, 5.6.0 and 5.9.0 only, and eng/Versions.props on dotnet/roslyn main reads MinorVersion 12. This finding duplicates nothing among DT-1 to DT-9: DT-9 concerns the target framework of the Workspaces and LinqPad hosts, not the Roslyn package version.
