evidence:
Premise 1, "C# 15 extension indexers are declared inside extension blocks": confirmed. The csharplang proposal https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/csharplang/main/proposals/csharp-15.0/extension-indexers.md states "Extension indexers are added to the set of permitted members inside an extension declaration" and "Because indexers are always instance members, an extension block that declares an indexer must provide a named receiver parameter". The Roslyn API delta report agrees: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Metalama/ccf204f4-b0b3-5fe6-a8de-fe20f6791d2c/scratchpad/impact/08-roslyn-api-delta.md:144-146 ("Roslyn reuses IndexerDeclarationSyntax inside ExtensionBlockDeclarationSyntax; no new node, kind or symbol API"; the indexer "appears as an IPropertySymbol (IsIndexer) on the extension type (TypeKind.Extension)").

Premise 2, the version of the two features: refuted as stated in the finding's framing, because the finding contrasts C# 15 with C# 14 as if the extension block itself were new or newly reachable. Extension blocks are a C# 14 feature: MessageID.RequiredVersion returns LanguageVersion.CSharp14 for IDS_FeatureExtensions both at the 5.10 snapshot (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Metalama/ccf204f4-b0b3-5fe6-a8de-fe20f6791d2c/scratchpad/MessageID-5.10.cs:506,512-516) and on Roslyn main (MessageID-main.cs:509,515-519), and Metalama's own IExtensionBlock documents the C# 14 proposal (/home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework/Code/IExtensionBlock.cs:10-11). The Roslyn 5.0 parser already parses ExtensionBlockDeclarationSyntax (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Metalama/ccf204f4-b0b3-5fe6-a8de-fe20f6791d2c/scratchpad/LanguageParser-5.0.cs, one occurrence), so an extension block can be written and validated with the Roslyn version that Metalama.Premium consumes today (FACTS.md:37, Directory.Packages.props RoslynVersion 5.0.0). Only the extension indexer is new: IDS_FeatureExtensionIndexers requires LanguageVersion.CSharp15 on main (MessageID-main.cs:500-507) and LanguageVersion.Preview at the 5.10 snapshot (MessageID-5.10.cs:496-504).

Premise 3, the availability of C# 15 in the consumed Roslyn: LanguageVersion.CSharp15 does not exist in the stable 5.9.0 or in the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 preview, and the six C# 15 features are reachable there only under LanguageVersion.Preview (FACTS.md:54; 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:16). The value and the CSharp15 gating come from commit #84799 of 2026-08-11, inside the 5.11 window, and the first stable package expected to contain them is 5.12 (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:18-19,21; FACTS.md:48-49,55-56). Metalama's own plumbing stops at C# 14 and accepts Preview only with AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures (FACTS.md:16,21).

The open question, on its Roslyn side: an extension block is a type declaration in the Roslyn declaration tree (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Metalama/ccf204f4-b0b3-5fe6-a8de-fe20f6791d2c/scratchpad/DeclarationTreeBuilder-main.cs:702-705 maps ExtensionBlockDeclarationSyntax to DeclarationKind.Extension), and the extension declaration is exposed as a named type symbol with ITypeSymbol.IsExtension and ITypeSymbol.ExtensionParameter (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Metalama/ccf204f4-b0b3-5fe6-a8de-fe20f6791d2c/scratchpad/ITypeSymbol.cs:85-91). Metalama maps every such symbol to ExtensionBlock (/home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CodeModel/Factories/DeclarationFactory.Symbols.cs:187-189; /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Utilities/Roslyn/SymbolExtensions.cs:384-387), and ExtensionBlock reports DeclarationKind.ExtensionBlock (/home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CodeModel/Source/ExtensionBlock.cs:42). An extension indexer therefore has an extension type as its containing symbol, exactly as a C# 14 extension method does; nothing in the Roslyn semantics makes the indexer case different.

Supporting code citations for the finding itself (unchanged by this verification): the switch and its throw at /home/user/metalama.premium/src/Metalama.Extensions.Validation/ReferenceValidationContext.cs:124-134, called from the Destination property at :57; DeclarationKind.ExtensionBlock at /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework/Code/DeclarationKind.cs:116-118; INamedType.ExtensionBlocks at /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework/Code/INamedType.cs:187; the core treating an extension block as a validated declaration at /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/ReferenceGraph/ReferenceIndexerRequirements.cs (DeclarationKind.ExtensionBlock in the BaseType filter and in GetReferenceKindsSupportedByDeclarationKind, which grants ReferenceKinds.All).

Correct text: extension blocks are a C# 14 feature (MessageID.RequiredVersion returns LanguageVersion.CSharp14 for IDS_FeatureExtensions at the 5.10 snapshot and on Roslyn main; IExtensionBlock.cs:10-11 cites the csharp-14.0 extensions proposal), and the Roslyn 5.0 parser already accepts ExtensionBlockDeclarationSyntax. The failure is therefore reachable today, with the Roslyn versions that Metalama and Metalama.Premium already consume, and is not introduced by C# 15. C# 15 only adds extension indexers to the set of members an extension block may declare (proposals/csharp-15.0/extension-indexers.md: extension indexers are added to the set of permitted members inside an extension declaration, and a block that declares an indexer must provide a named receiver parameter), which requires LanguageVersion.CSharp15 on Roslyn main and only LanguageVersion.Preview in the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 preview and in the stable 5.9.0.

Schedule the fix independently of the .NET 11 and C# 15 work rather than inside it. Add the extension indexer variant of the test only after two prerequisites hold: the latest Premium Roslyn variant moves to the stable Roslyn that exposes C# 15 as a non-preview language version (expected 5.12, since no stable 5.10 or 5.11 package exists), and Metalama's language-version plumbing raises SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest to C# 15. notes:
The finding survives the verification. Its code core is untouched by the external premises, and the only external premise that is load-bearing for the report as a whole is the one that dates the exposure. That premise is wrong in its timing: the extension block is a C# 14 construct, present in the Roslyn 5.0 variant, so the throw is reachable in the current release and is not a consequence of the .NET 11 and C# 15 work. Extension indexers are genuinely a C# 15 addition, and the csharplang proposal confirms that they are declared inside an extension block whose receiver parameter must be named, so the block does gain one more reason to be a validation target. That is a marginal increase in likelihood, not the cause of the defect.

The practical consequence of the correction is scheduling: the mapping and the extension-method test belong to the current release rather than to the 2027.0 C# 15 work, while the extension-indexer half of the test cannot be authored until the latest variant is on a Roslyn that exposes C# 15 as a non-preview version. The addendum places that at Roslyn 5.12; the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 and the stable 5.9.0 gate every C# 15 feature, including extension indexers, on LanguageVersion.Preview.

The Roslyn half of the open question is answered in the affirmative: an extension declaration is a type declaration in Roslyn, exposed as a named type symbol with IsExtension, and members declared in the block, indexers included, have it as their containing type. Metalama maps any such symbol to ExtensionBlock, whose DeclarationKind is ExtensionBlock. Whether Metalama's own code model exposes an extension indexer with an IExtensionBlock as its DeclaringType, and whether the reference indexer attributes an element access to the indexer or to the block, remains a question for the code lens; the answer does not change this verdict, because the extension-method path alone already reaches the throw.

evidence:
Every external premise of LK-8 was checked against the csharplang proposal and the dotnet/roslyn main sources, and all of them hold. Details, with sources.

1. A union is a struct in the Roslyn type model, so a Metalama eligibility rule that admits a struct admits a union. Verified first hand: /tmp/ec.cs (downloaded from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/roslyn/main/src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/EnumConversions.cs) lines 34-37 map DeclarationKind.Struct, DeclarationKind.Union and DeclarationKind.RecordStruct to TypeKind.Struct. The report states the same at 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:19 and :94. On the Metalama side, /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CodeModel/Source/SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:69-79 maps Roslyn TypeKind.Struct to Metalama TypeKind.Struct unconditionally, and /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework/Eligibility/EligibilityRuleFactory.cs:174-176 admits "TypeKind.Class or TypeKind.Struct". The Where item cites EligibilityRuleFactory.cs:164-195; the file is at Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework/Eligibility/EligibilityRuleFactory.cs and the rule is at lines 164-195 as stated.

2. The per-case constructors are synthesized, public, single-parameter, implicitly declared and without any declaring syntax. This was the finding's stated open risk ("depends on the Roslyn symbol model for synthesized union constructors") and it is now settled. /tmp/unionctor.cs (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/roslyn/main/src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/Synthesized/SynthesizedUnionCtor.cs) declares "internal sealed class SynthesizedUnionCtor : SynthesizedInstanceConstructor", sets Parameters to a single SynthesizedParameterSymbol at ordinal 0, overrides DeclaredAccessibility to Accessibility.Public, and asserts IsImplicitlyDeclared in AddSynthesizedAttributes where it applies CompilerGeneratedAttribute. Its base chain reaches SynthesizedMethodSymbol (/tmp/sms.cs, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/roslyn/main/src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/Synthesized/SynthesizedMethodSymbol.cs lines 21-35), which returns ImmutableArray<SyntaxReference>.Empty from DeclaringSyntaxReferences and sealed true from IsImplicitlyDeclared. The csharplang proposal agrees: unions.md specifies "a public constructor for each of the case_types" and "a public object? Value { get; } auto-property".

3. Consequently the Metalama test at /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CodeModel/Helpers/DeclarationExtensions.cs:664-665, "constructor is { IsStatic: false, IsImplicitlyDeclared: true, IsPrimary: false, Parameters: [] }", is false for a synthesized case constructor because Parameters is not empty. /home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/AdviceImpl/Initialization/ConstructorInitializeAdvice.cs:60-101 then takes the else branch and uses the symbol constructor directly as the target, which is a constructor with no syntax. The enumeration filter at lines 68-72 (InitializerKind != ConstructorInitializerKind.This and not a record copy constructor) does not exclude it, because a synthesized case constructor has no initializer.

4. The field prohibition is real and its text is verbatim. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/roslyn/main/src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/CSharpResources.resx, entry ERR_InstanceFieldInUnion: "Instance fields, auto-properties or field-like events are not permitted in a 'union' declaration." The enforcement site is /tmp/smcs.cs (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/roslyn/main/src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/Source/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs) lines 2084-2093: inside "if (IsUnionDeclaration)", every field of GetFieldsToEmit that is not static and whose AssociatedSymbol is not the SynthesizedUnionValuePropertySymbol is reported. Because the test runs over the fields to emit, it covers the backing field of an auto-property and of a field-like event, and it covers private fields, which is exactly the kind of field that OverrideHelper.AddTransformationsForStructField introduces.

5. The single-parameter constructor prohibition is real and its text is verbatim. CSharpResources.resx, entry ERR_InstanceCtorWithOneParameterInUnion: "Explicitly declared public constructors with a single parameter are not permitted in a 'union' declaration." Enforcement at SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:2095-2101: "if (ctor.DeclaredAccessibility == Accessibility.Public && ctor.ParameterCount == 1 && ctor is not SynthesizedUnionCtor)". The proposal states the same rule.

6. A third compiler error applies to any constructor Metalama emits into a union and the finding does not mention it. CSharpResources.resx, entry ERR_UnionConstructorCallsDefaultConstructor: "A constructor declared in a 'union' declaration must have a 'this' initializer that calls a synthesized constructor or an explicitly declared constructor." Enforcement at /tmp/bs.cs (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/roslyn/main/src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Binder/Binder_Statements.cs) lines 3817-3847: a missing initializer and a "this()" default value type initializer are both reported when the containing type is a SourceMemberContainerTypeSymbol with IsUnionDeclaration true. The proposal states the same rule.

7. Reachability and the version timeline. The finding correctly marks the situation unreachable today. Per FACTS.md:54-56, LanguageVersion.CSharp15 does not exist in the consumed Roslyn 5.10.0-1.26365.3 nor in the stable 5.9.0, the union API is present but experimental there, and the next stable Roslyn is 5.12 (FACTS.md:48-49, 08-roslyn-api-delta.md:15 and :18). The Roslyn surface a MustNotBeUnion rule would depend on, ITypeSymbol.IsUnion, exists on ITypeSymbol and not on INamedTypeSymbol (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:36 and :97; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dotnet/roslyn/main/src/Compilers/Core/Portable/Symbols/ITypeSymbol.cs lines 147-153, where the member carries no experimental attribute on main), and it is absent from the Roslyn 5.0.0 variant that serves Rider (08-roslyn-api-delta.md:36, FACTS.md:11 and :56).

Nothing was refuted. The corrections below are refinements of scope and of the proposed change, not contradictions.

where: Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework/Eligibility/EligibilityRuleFactory.cs:164-195 (the Where item gives the file name only; this is the full path, and the type branch is at lines 174-176)
corrections.what_happens_today: Unreachable today, because no Roslyn that Metalama consumes exposes C# 15 as a non-preview language version; unions become reachable only with the move to Roslyn 5.12 (FACTS.md:48-49 and :54-56). After LK-1 and LK-2 the behaviour is as the finding describes, with three refinements of scope. First, the case constructors of a union are SynthesizedUnionCtor instances: public, exactly one parameter, IsImplicitlyDeclared true and DeclaringSyntaxReferences empty. Metalama's IsImplicitInstanceConstructor also requires an empty parameter list, so ConstructorInitializeAdvice treats each of them as an explicit constructor and targets a declaration that has no syntax. Second, the field prohibition covers every non-static field to be emitted, at any accessibility, including the backing field of an auto-property and of a field-like event, and excluding only the backing field of the synthesized Value property; static fields are permitted, so a static introduction into a union is not affected. Third, the single-parameter constructor prohibition applies only to a public constructor, so a non-public forwarding constructor escapes that particular error but still falls under a rule the finding does not mention: a constructor declared in a union must carry a 'this' initializer that calls a synthesized or an explicitly declared constructor, and that initializer must not be 'this()'. A Metalama-emitted constructor with no initializer therefore fails as well.
corrections.proposed_change: Keep the proposal, and add two points. First, the blanket alternative should be preferred for 2027.0, because it costs one diagnostic and covers the three distinct compiler errors (the instance field prohibition, the public single-parameter constructor prohibition and the constructor chaining requirement) as well as the silent case where an initializer is injected into a constructor that has no syntax. Second, the rule cannot read the Roslyn union flag directly from Metalama.Framework: the eligibility rules live in the public assembly, which does not reference Roslyn, and ITypeSymbol.IsUnion is declared on ITypeSymbol rather than on INamedTypeSymbol and is absent from the Roslyn 5.0.0 variant that serves Rider. The code model member INamedType.IsUnion must therefore be implemented in a Roslyn-variant-gated way, returning false in the 5.0.0 variant, and the rules in EligibilityRuleFactory must consume only that abstraction. If MustNotBeUnion rules are written rather than a blanket diagnostic, they should also cover the field-like IntroduceEvent path and the private backing field that OverrideHelper.AddTransformationsForStructField introduces for struct auto-properties, because that field is rejected even though it is private.

notes: The central claim survives every attempt to refute it. There is no API path by which an aspect can request `closed` or `union` on an introduced type, so nothing can crash and no diagnostic is reachable, and the linker preserves a user-written `closed` modifier because it never regenerates the modifier list of an existing type declaration. I checked the two paths that could have regenerated it, the linker injection rewriter and the design-time partial generator, and both preserve the original tokens. Three details are corrected. The line range for GetTypeSyntaxModifierList is 198-236 and the method does not emit `partial` or `unsafe`; the report listed those two keywords. The statement that an introduced class derived from a closed class works because it lives in the same assembly is incomplete, since the specification requires the same assembly as the closed base type, and nothing validates that or the type-parameter rule. The proposed change is not minimal as written, because emitting `closed` next to the existing `abstract` and `sealed` branches produces code that the compiler rejects, and because SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword is an experimental API whose reference is reported as an error today. No test pins the missing behaviour, which is expected for a feature that has no API surface; the existing type-introduction tests under Metalama.Framework.Tests.AspectTests/Tests/Aspects/DesignTime cover only class and interface introduction.

notes:
The central claim holds: a union parameter collapses to one cache key per union type, silently, and a JSON round-trip loses the value. Two details are wrong and are corrected.

First, the code path inside `DefaultFormatter<T>` is misidentified. The finding cites DefaultFormatter.cs:144-148, the branch that appends the type name through the `Type` formatter. That branch is unreachable for a struct, because `HasCustomToStringMethod` (DefaultFormatterHelper.cs:14-20) compares the declaring type of the resolved `ToString` with `typeof(object)`, and for a struct that does not declare `ToString` the resolved method is `System.ValueType.ToString`, declared on `System.ValueType`. The branch actually taken is DefaultFormatter.cs:107-141, which calls `ToString` and wraps the result in braces. Because `System.ValueType.ToString` returns `this.GetType().ToString()`, the resulting text is still the full type name in braces and the collapse is unchanged. The predicted key `{Namespace.Type}` therefore happens to be right, but for a different reason than the finding gives, and the fix has to be placed accordingly: suppressing the collapse by making `HasCustomToStringMethod` stricter would change the behaviour of every struct, not only of unions.

Second, the open question is answered by the sources already in the scratchpad. The compiler synthesizes `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.UnionAttribute` on every union declaration (SourceNamedTypeSymbol.cs:1867-1875) and adds an implicit implementation of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.IUnion` (SourceNamedTypeSymbol_Bases.cs:378-383). Neither type exists in net472, netstandard2.0 or net10.0, which are the target frameworks of Flashtrace.Formatters, so the recognizer must match by name.

Two observations that bear on priority but do not change the verdict. The behaviour is not specific to unions: every user-defined struct that does not override `ToString` already collapses to a single cache key today, and no test pins that case, so the finding describes a long-standing property of Flashtrace that C# 15 unions make easy to hit rather than a regression introduced by the language version. And the finding is conditional on C# 15 becoming usable in a Metalama project at all: per the established facts, no consumed Roslyn exposes `LanguageVersion.CSharp15`, and Metalama.Framework.targets rewrites an unrecognized `LangVersion` to 12.0, so a union cannot be compiled in a Metalama user project until the move to the stable Roslyn.

The consequence class is confirmed as silent. `CachingDiagnosticDescriptors` has no descriptor about parameter formattability, `CacheKeyBuilder.BuildMethodKey` throws only on argument-count and static/instance mismatches, and `DefaultFormatter` swallows an exception from `ToString` at DefaultFormatter.cs:111-118. The size estimate M is unchanged.

Premise 2 (numeric kind values) is confirmed. On `main`, `SyntaxKind.cs` line 430 `UnionKeyword = 8452`, line 432 `ClosedKeyword = 8453`, line 948 `WithElement = 9081`, line 950 `UnionDeclaration = 9082`. corrections.what_happens_today: FindCompileTimeCodeVisitor decides whether a syntax tree is fed to the compile-time rewriter. It overrides only the six classic type-declaration visits, so a union never sets HasCompileTimeCode, which is correct because a union is run-time code. When the same file also declares an aspect, the tree is rewritten by ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter. The rewriter does not select types through visitor overrides alone: it dispatches on the syntax kind, through SyntaxKindExtensions.IsTypeDeclaration and IsBaseTypeDeclaration, both of which enumerate a fixed set of kinds that does not include UnionDeclaration. The outcome therefore depends on where the union is declared. A union declared outside any namespace is removed by the filter of VisitCompilationUnit and never reaches the compile-time compilation. A union declared inside a block-scoped or file-scoped namespace falls into the default arm of VisitTypeOrNamespaceMembers, which calls the base rewriter and copies the union into the compile-time compilation; the namespace is preserved only when the aspect is declared in the same namespace. A union nested in a compile-time type, for example inside an aspect class, falls into the default arm of the member switch of TransformCompileTimeType and is likewise copied. A union nested in a run-time type reaches the default arm of PopulateNestedCompileTimeTypes and is dropped, which is correct by accident. For the two copying paths the compile-time tree is created with parse options set to the compile-time language version, which is C# 14, and Roslyn checks the union feature when it builds the declaration table rather than only in the parser, so the compile-time build fails with a feature-not-available error on a declaration the user never wrote for compile-time. Metalama reports CannotEmitCompileTimeAssembly together with the raw Roslyn errors, whose locations point at the generated compile-time file. The scenario is reachable today only when AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures is set, because the pipeline rejects LanguageVersion.Preview otherwise and admits no version above C# 14; it becomes generally reachable once C# 15 is admitted.

notes:
The finding survives. Its consequence class of no impact is correct for the production code paths: a labeled break contributes one IdentifierNameSyntax that binds to a label symbol, which the Observability walker classifies as an unsupported chain exactly as it already classifies the identifier of a goto statement, and a with element contributes an argument list that the walker analyses like any other argument list. The Metrics visitors are reached through the generated dispatch to DefaultVisit and need no recompilation against the newer Roslyn.

Two premises were strengthened rather than weakened by this verification. The label-binding premise, which the finding itself flagged as unverified, is now established from a comment that the Roslyn authors wrote for exactly this purpose in BoundNodes.xml. The dispatch premise is established from the generated visitor file of the 5.10 window rather than from the general shape of the generator.

The corrections are both about the proposed change rather than about the analysis. The version label 5.10 should be read as the latest Roslyn variant, whose stable form is expected to be 5.12; the gate constant keeps its name across that renumbering, so the proposed change names it correctly. The gate is nevertheless incomplete, because it selects a Roslyn variant and not a language version, and the two C# 15 constructs bind only under a language version that Metalama does not yet offer.

One further observation that the finding does not raise and that the verification did not settle: the aspect test file is also compiled into the test project itself, so C# 15 source in it requires the test project to accept that language version. This is a local matter of the test infrastructure, outside the semantics lens, and it is already recorded in the design-time report at 05-design-time-workspaces-linqpad.md line 86.

notes:
Central claim holds. Every one of the roughly thirty cited locations was opened and contains the text attributed to it, so the inventory itself is accurate and the finding is not refutable on its facts.

Three corrections, all detail-level.

First and most consequential, the consequence class is wrong for one of the thirteen items. Item 9 concerns `MetalamaSourceGeneratorAttribute` in `Metalama.Framework.props:66-78`, which is an MSBuild item group consumed by the aspect eligibility rules, not prose. Re-deriving that list for .NET 10 and .NET 11 changes which partial members an aspect may target, and the failure mode is silent, so the item does not belong in a documentation-only pull request.

Second, the proposed replacement rationale for the `RestorePrerelease` comment is unverified and appears to be incorrect, because the repository contains no floating package version for the property to act on.

Third, two citation slips: the `SupportedPlatform.UntestedTargetFramework.csproj` comment is at lines 11 and 12 rather than 10 and 11, and several entries in the `where` list give a bare file name rather than a repository-relative path.

Two further observations that do not rise to corrections. The title says the finding covers documentation stating "C# 14 as the latest", but no cited location makes that statement; C# 14 appears only in the proposed `NOTES.md` entry of item 13. The declaration that C# 14 is the current template language lives at `/home/user/Metalama/Directory.Build.props:11-16`, which the finding does not cite. Separately, the finding's own open question about whether .NET 10 and .NET 11 added attribute-driven source generators cannot be settled from this repository, which reinforces that item 9 needs its own investigation rather than a documentation edit.

The proposed change is otherwise sound and minimal, and it compiles under both Roslyn variants trivially, because items 1 to 8 and 10 to 13 touch only Markdown, XML documentation comments and MSBuild comments, none of which participate in the variant build.
